Models are assessed with three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus to unseen worlds, and an empirical scaling law is fit.
4C38yMjJgY.key_idea: Vary data volume, mixture diversity, and model size in one controlled continued-pretraining grid and fit validation loss to all three, revealing an early interface phase and a later world phase.
4C38yMjJgY.evidence: 120 configurations evaluated by validation losses and gameplay benchmarks across in-corpus, related, and unseen worlds, with paused and real-time evaluation (from reviews).
4C38yMjJgY.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers: more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity helps related worlds, larger models gain data efficiency but generalize worse to distant worlds, and the models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds.
4C38yMjJgY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic grid over model size, data budget, and mixture, evaluated on both familiar and unseen worlds with offline loss and interactive gameplay.
4C38yMjJgY.main_concern: Conclusions outrun the evidence: the data regime is spread over many game worlds, mixtures confound diversity with exposure to related games, and only one training seed is used.

bKK8WccojU.one_liner: Reweights tokens in RLVR updates to amplify discriminative token-gradient directions and downweight shared high-frequency patterns.
bKK8WccojU.problem: It is poorly understood how response-level rewards become token-level probability changes, and advantage-weighted centroids can be dominated by shared high-frequency patterns such as formatting tokens, diluting discriminative directions.
bKK8WccojU.method: DelTA views the policy-gradient update as a linear discriminator over token-gradient vectors built from positive- and negative-side centroids. It estimates token coefficients that amplify side-specific token-gradient directions and downweight shared or weakly discriminative ones, reweighting a self-normalized RLVR surrogate.
bKK8WccojU.key_idea: Treat the RLVR update as a linear discriminator over token gradients and reweight tokens so the positive and negative advantage-side centroids become more contrastive.
bKK8WccojU.evidence: Seven mathematical benchmarks on two Qwen3 backbones, with reviews citing extensions to code generation, GRPO, out-of-domain tasks, Olmo3-7B, and matched wall-clock comparisons.
bKK8WccojU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results on seven mathematical benchmarks).
bKK8WccojU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find a simple plug-in reweighting of the DAPO surrogate with modest overhead and consistent gains across math benchmarks, model scales, and other settings, with meaningful ablations.
bKK8WccojU.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to discriminative reweighting: baseline dynamics look atypical, scale-matched and simpler weighting baselines are missing, and the mechanism is only partly verified.

1TM3o2opPt.one_liner: Benchmarks LVLMs on multi-view 3D reconstruction as oriented object boxes in metric coordinates, scored on Structure and Metric.
1TM3o2opPt.problem: Static spatial benchmarks test isolated judgments while embodied evaluations mix perception with planning, so cross-view spatial intelligence in LVLMs is not diagnosed directly.
1TM3o2opPt.method: RECONSPATIAL gives LVLMs real multi-view images and target-object queries and asks for oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared camera-anchored metric frame across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor scenes. Reconstructions are scored on Structure (relative layout) and Metric (physical scale and placement), alongside nine atomic spatial QA tasks and offline navigation.
1TM3o2opPt.key_idea: Evaluate spatial intelligence through joint multi-view object-layout reconstruction in metric coordinates, separating relative structure from metric accuracy and linking both to atomic skills and navigation.
1TM3o2opPt.evidence: 18 LVLMs evaluated on reconstruction, nine atomic QA tasks in Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, and offline navigation.
1TM3o2opPt.claimed_gains: Even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric, showing a gap between relative layout and metric reconstruction across 18 LVLMs.
1TM3o2opPt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find evaluating joint scene reconstruction well motivated, with a thorough benchmark covering three environment types and separate Structure and Metric scores.
1TM3o2opPt.main_concern: The task is high-level object-layout estimation rather than full scene reconstruction, novelty over existing reconstruction-based evaluations needs sharper justification, and omitted objects are not penalized.

i0Au2NJZgv.one_liner: Learns a slot-specific onset for temporal-consistency loss through an activity gate, so new objects are acquired before slots are constrained.
i0Au2NJZgv.problem: Slot-slot contrastive consistency preserves existing objects but progressively degrades representations of newly appearing objects even when idle slot capacity remains (an acquisition-maintenance trade-off).
i0Au2NJZgv.method: SlotCommit ties the onset of consistency to a learned activity gate that decides whether a slot contributes to reconstruction. On first activation the slot is committed and its consistency constraint starts on the next transition, and the first enabled consistency loss also trains the activation decision.
i0Au2NJZgv.key_idea: Delay each slot's temporal-consistency constraint until a learned activity gate commits the slot, coupling slot recruitment to the representation-dependent consistency cost.
i0Au2NJZgv.evidence: Matched MOVi-C models for the main acquisition analysis, plus MOVi-E and YouTube-VIS pipeline comparisons and ablations (from reviews).
i0Au2NJZgv.claimed_gains: Learned-onset SSC raises new-object acquisition by idle slots from 27.5% to 50.9% and improves simultaneous entrant-resident representation from 25.5% (end value cut off in the abstract).
i0Au2NJZgv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem diagnosis clear and the activation gate with commitment a useful mechanism, supported by matched-architecture ablations and case studies.
i0Au2NJZgv.main_concern: Detailed acquisition evidence is limited to MOVi-C with no mechanism validation on real videos, commitment is irreversible within a sequence, and SlotCommit trails on some grouping metrics.

NJq0GtPzp1.one_liner: Starts flow-matching graph generation from a learned latent-conditioned graphon source instead of independent noise.
NJq0GtPzp1.problem: Flow-based graph generators start from independent noise or fixed priors, leaving the flow to recover most of the target structure during generation.
NJq0GtPzp1.method: A two-stage procedure first learns a latent graph representation and a graphon-based source distribution, then freezes the source and learns a conditional velocity field that transports source samples toward target graphs. Canonical graph representations support consistent graphon learning, and connectivity-aware regularisation supports structure-preserving generation.
NJq0GtPzp1.key_idea: Learn a latent-conditioned graphon as the flow's source distribution so generation begins from structured samples, then train the velocity field with that source frozen.
NJq0GtPzp1.evidence: Four molecular benchmarks and three synthetic graph families, with ablations on the graphon source, canonical representation, two-stage optimisation, and connectivity-aware regularisation.
NJq0GtPzp1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports competitive chemical validity, diversity, and structural fidelity without figures).
NJq0GtPzp1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the graphon-based structured starting point for flow generation novel, cleanly formulated and theoretically analysed, with extensive experiments.
NJq0GtPzp1.main_concern: Reliance on canonical labeling (McKay's nauty) limits scalability to small graphs, the benefit of graphon targets is weakly shown, and some metrics and baselines (such as FCD and GraphBSI) are missing.

0xAEaSaSpZ.one_liner: Replaces explicit Euler flow-policy sampling with implicit Euler solved as a joint equilibrium system, trained inside soft actor-critic.
0xAEaSaSpZ.problem: Expressive flow policies can represent multiple high-value actions, but sampling them with few integration steps while keeping tractable action densities is hard.
0xAEaSaSpZ.method: DEFlow uses implicit Euler integration and solves all intermediate actions jointly as an equilibrium system. Implicit differentiation plus a discrete change-of-variables formula for the final-action density enables off-policy soft actor-critic training without backpropagating through solver iterations.
0xAEaSaSpZ.key_idea: Treat implicit Euler integration of a flow policy as a deep equilibrium system, using implicit differentiation and a discrete change-of-variables density so no gradients flow through solver iterations.
0xAEaSaSpZ.evidence: Four Multi-Goal docking variants, five manipulation tasks, and five MuJoCo tasks, with matched explicit-Euler comparisons and step-count ablations (from reviews).
0xAEaSaSpZ.claimed_gains: An average relative improvement of approximately 10% in mean successful coverage over the strongest baseline across four Multi-Goal docking variants, the highest mean time-averaged return on four of five manipulation tasks, and broadly competitive results across five MuJoCo tasks.
0xAEaSaSpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find a technically coherent way to combine implicit flow sampling with maximum-entropy RL, with matched explicit-Euler and step-count ablations showing benefit on precision tasks.
0xAEaSaSpZ.main_concern: Compute cost is heavy (training takes about three times as long as SAC), gains are limited to docking and early manipulation learning, and the practical density and gradient approximations are not fully validated.

97ord3tPeP.one_liner: Learns an invertible straightening map of activations, then clamps concept coordinates to a target code at many layers.
97ord3tPeP.problem: Representation interventions in LLMs often hurt utility or fail under distribution shift because concepts are spread redundantly across layers (the hydra effect) and a linear subspace misses context-dependent concept geometry.
97ord3tPeP.method: SAC learns an invertible straightening map that concentrates concept-related variation, then applies a projection clamp enforcing a target concept code in the straightened coordinates; the clamp is idempotent, so it goes inactive once the code is satisfied. Training has two stages: a straightening map amortized across concepts, then lightweight per-concept clamps learned with pairwise preference optimization.
97ord3tPeP.key_idea: Apply an idempotent projection clamp in a learned invertible coordinate system that straightens concept geometry, so multi-layer interventions stop acting once the target concept code holds.
97ord3tPeP.evidence: Concept induction and harmful-concept suppression experiments (AxBench and out-of-distribution jailbreak sets per reviews), mainly on Qwen-2.5-7B for suppression and two similar-size models for induction.
97ord3tPeP.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off before the results).
97ord3tPeP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design clean, with formal fixed-point and idempotence properties and component ablations supporting the combined approach.
97ord3tPeP.main_concern: Suppression gains are overclaimed (average OOD ASR of 14.5 versus 16.5 for LoFiT and 10.7 for training-free ACE, with no variance reported), and the evaluation covers few models.

wzXVFdJDAE.one_liner: Learns fMRI graph dictionaries on each subject's own cortical geometry using Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distance with amortized transport.
wzXVFdJDAE.problem: Projecting every brain onto a common template removes subject-specific information, so dictionary learning on fMRI should account for variability in brain geometry across individuals.
wzXVFdJDAE.method: The approach compares graphs with different geometries and features using the Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distance, and trains a neural network by amortized optimization to approximate the optimal transport plans for large graphs. The graph dictionary atoms are conditioned on the FGW trade-off parameter between feature alignment and structural consistency.
wzXVFdJDAE.key_idea: Learn graph dictionary atoms conditioned on the FGW trade-off parameter, with a neural network amortizing the optimal transport plans between individual-geometry graphs.
wzXVFdJDAE.evidence: Numerical experiments on the HCP dataset with contrast and subject retrieval and classification, including held-out subjects and different graph resolutions.
wzXVFdJDAE.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says it outperforms standard fMRI dictionary learning, without figures).
wzXVFdJDAE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the combination of amortized transport plans with trade-off-conditioned dictionary atoms technically coherent, with a practical speedup and held-out-subject evaluation.
wzXVFdJDAE.main_concern: The gain over the existing GDL and ULOT components is not isolated (no fixed-trade-off dictionary baseline), and the subject-classification evaluation and registration comparison are not fully controlled.

lrbrp69tCo.one_liner: Maps early LM training with a developmental atlas of MLP unit expression, finding a maternal phase that copies initialization.
lrbrp69tCo.problem: Early training is dominated by initial weights, yet runs differing only in seed reach nearly the same loss, so the point where control passes from initialization to learning has not been located.
lrbrp69tCo.method: The authors build a developmental atlas of Pythia that follows the expression of every MLP unit across fifty runs at five sizes plus four larger models, and retrain small models to intervene where the atlas can only correlate.
lrbrp69tCo.key_idea: Track each MLP unit's expression against its initial projection onto the layer's mean input, showing training starts as a copy of initialization and ends when the mean input rotates.
lrbrp69tCo.evidence: Pythia checkpoints from fifty runs at five sizes and four larger models, plus retrained small models for interventions and curve-collapse experiments.
lrbrp69tCo.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative findings, not performance numbers).
lrbrp69tCo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit careful multi-seed experiments with sensible baselines, openly reported negative results, and extensive evidence across Pythia sizes linking initialization to early training.
lrbrp69tCo.main_concern: The sharp initialization-to-training handover may reflect the chosen readout (mean absolute activation) and threshold, and the claim that learning rate and initial scale act only through one ratio is not fully supported by the tested schedules.

7IjRIR4OYu.one_liner: Characterizes the depth and agent counts networks of linear learners need for exact information aggregation under parent limits.
7IjRIR4OYu.problem: Prior work analyzed information aggregation on a given graph and feature allocation, but the limits of designing the network itself were unknown.
7IjRIR4OYu.method: The paper studies the networked learning model of Kearns et al., where agents on a DAG each see one feature and their parents' predictions, fit a linear predictor, and pass only a prediction forward. It proves bounds on depth and agents for exact aggregation with limited parents under an adaptive designer (knows the distribution) and an oblivious designer (fixes the graph before an adversary picks the distribution).
7IjRIR4OYu.key_idea: Prove impossibility for one-parent networks and construct exact-aggregation networks with three parents, simulated by two-parent networks at constant overhead.
7IjRIR4OYu.evidence: Theoretical results only, summarized in a table of bounds for the adaptive and oblivious settings; no experiments.
7IjRIR4OYu.claimed_gains: not stated (a theory paper; the visible abstract shows that for d >= 3 no finite depth guarantees exact aggregation with one parent per agent).
7IjRIR4OYu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find a nontrivial, rigorous structural characterization with a crisp one-parent versus two-parent dichotomy and a useful adaptive versus oblivious analysis.
7IjRIR4OYu.main_concern: The results hinge on a restrictive protocol where each agent must forward its own least-squares prediction, and there are no experiments or concrete agentic use cases to tie the model to practice.

JapmkR2MSa.one_liner: Generates one-shot video transitions from a visual reference alone, using neutral-prompt training, one-way attention, and dissolve null-reference guidance.
JapmkR2MSa.problem: Existing one-shot transition-effect generation models learn a text shortcut, relying on prompt descriptions so the visual transition signal vanishes.
JapmkR2MSa.method: Training pairs inputs with effect-free neutral prompts and applies a one-way attention mask that keeps the reference independent of the target. At inference, null-reference guidance defines the unconditional path as a dissolve of the reference endpoints to isolate and amplify the transition effect; endpoints can be video clips, images, or absent, and the authors release the SEGUE-Benchmark.
JapmkR2MSa.key_idea: Remove text cues and isolate the reference during training, then use a dissolve of the reference endpoints as the unconditional branch in guidance to amplify only the visual effect.
JapmkR2MSa.evidence: Held-out effects and endpoints on the SEGUE-Benchmark (1,692 transition classes, 56,368 training pairs) against baselines adapted to TEG and prior visual effect transfer methods; reviews note the two-sided test set has 38 samples.
JapmkR2MSa.claimed_gains: SEGUE outperforms baselines adapted to TEG and prior visual effect transfer methods on held-out effects even without the transition prompt (no metric figures), on a benchmark of 1,692 transition classes and 56,368 training pairs.
JapmkR2MSa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task practical and the text-shortcut hypothesis testable, with a unified formulation of two-sided and single-sided transfer and a useful released dataset.
JapmkR2MSa.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (fine-tuning with in-context conditioning and one-way attention), the roles of neutral prompts, the attention mask, and guidance are not separately ablated, and most effect classes are procedurally generated.

4yz9RjJXxS.one_liner: Scores imagined video futures by agreement on task-relevant outcomes read from rollouts, to allocate compute and gate actions.
4yz9RjJXxS.problem: Plausible generated videos need not give reliable task outcomes, so video models used for planning can mislead agents.
4yz9RjJXxS.method: FrameTrust is training-free: readers map sampled videos to answers or prompt-constrained objects and relations, separating meaningful disagreement from differences in appearance or trajectory. An entropy difference accounts for environment variation where simulator outcomes exist, and intermediate readouts with adaptive sampling reduce sampling cost.
4yz9RjJXxS.key_idea: Measure agreement among task-level outcome readouts of multiple sampled videos, subtracting simulator-estimated environment entropy, instead of comparing pixels or trajectories.
4yz9RjJXxS.evidence: Maze navigation, deterministic and stochastic Physics, Cups memory, GUI interaction (AndroidWorld, 60 tasks per reviews), and an open-ended generation study on T2V-CompBench prompts.
4yz9RjJXxS.claimed_gains: Early screening saves 67.5% of denoising work with similar screening accuracy, and the GUI application reduces irreversible errors by 59-64% without compromising task success.
4yz9RjJXxS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question timely and the use of semantic outcome agreement instead of pixel differences well motivated, with end-to-end validation in a GUI setting.
4yz9RjJXxS.main_concern: Task readers are under-specified and need per-environment engineering, the headline GUI gain rests on a single benchmark without error bars, and the practicality of multi-rollout video generation is questioned.

qLzMjP0cNf.one_liner: On-policy distillation for radiology reports that weights corrections by each error's estimated downstream clinical cost.
qLzMjP0cNf.problem: Report generators trained on reference prefixes but deployed on their own predictions suffer from early clinical contradictions, and local prediction error does not measure their downstream clinical consequences.
qLzMjP0cNf.method: CEF-OPD finds the earliest contradiction with extracted reference facts and builds a reference-supported minimal correction. Paired continuations from the erroneous and corrected prefixes estimate the downstream clinical cost change (excluding the edited claim), which weights local correction and self-distillation from the pre-error state.
qLzMjP0cNf.key_idea: Weight corrective distillation at the pre-error state by the paired-continuation difference in downstream clinical cost between erroneous and corrected prefixes.
qLzMjP0cNf.evidence: Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU X-ray, with component comparisons against continued supervised fine-tuning and correction-only variants, plus a bound on local clinical risk differences under stated assumptions.
qLzMjP0cNf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find targeting the pre-error state and prioritizing errors by downstream consequence well motivated, with consistent improvements on two benchmarks and useful ablations.
qLzMjP0cNf.main_concern: Equation 9 normalizes by batch size, so gains over uniform weighting may come from a changed effective auxiliary-loss strength rather than the consequence signal, and the gains are modest with a heuristic positive-part weight.

oyutnIaJyL.one_liner: Unified RL post-training framework for text- and image-to-3D generation with antipodal-view rewards and tree-structured rollouts.
oyutnIaJyL.problem: Existing 3D post-training methods mostly target text-to-3D, support only specific architectures, and rely on insufficiently justified reward and rendering designs, giving marginal improvements at substantial training cost.
oyutnIaJyL.method: Next3DGen studies efficient RL algorithms and builds a reward pipeline from explicit 3D quality criteria. For image-to-3D it applies complementary rewards to the reference-aligned view and its antipodal view, and for multi-stage generators it uses tree-structured rollouts with stage-specific credit assignment.
oyutnIaJyL.key_idea: Binary tree-structured rollouts jointly optimize geometry and texture stages with stage-specific credit assignment, while antipodal-view rewards improve unobserved regions of image-to-3D outputs.
oyutnIaJyL.evidence: Text-to-3D and image-to-3D benchmarks on single-stage (TIGON), multi-stage (TRELLIS) and Gaussian-splatting (TripoSplat) generators, with ablations; the text-to-3D set is 100 held-out Objaverse-XL-caption prompts.
oyutnIaJyL.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims consistent gains over pretrained models and over existing post-training methods, without numbers)
oyutnIaJyL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the unified framework across text/image conditioning and architectures, with consistent metric improvements, extensive ablations and an effective tree-structured rollout for multi-stage models.
oyutnIaJyL.main_concern: Evaluation relies on rule-based and proxy metrics (DreamSim, HPSv3, Uni3D) with no human perceptual study and a small text-to-3D prompt set, so holistic 3D quality is not established.

TkWra2xsDM.one_liner: Pairs sparse exact KV retention with learned episodic latent traces built progressively from pre-eviction hidden states under a fixed budget.
TkWra2xsDM.problem: Query-agnostic KV compression loses accuracy under tight budgets: eviction keeps only a sparse token subset, compaction loses precision, and existing hybrids derive the synthetic part from the retention outcome or only after full prefill.
TkWra2xsDM.method: For each context segment a learned constructor synthesizes latent traces from its complete pre-eviction hidden states, and frozen backbone projections map them into native KV states used alongside retained exact states in standard attention. The constructor is trained offline by self-distillation from a full-cache teacher while the backbone and base eviction policy stay frozen.
TkWra2xsDM.key_idea: A learned constructor turns each segment's full pre-eviction hidden states into latent traces that become KV states beside retained tokens, independent of the eviction outcome.
TkWra2xsDM.evidence: Evaluated across 4 long-context backbones, 3 base eviction policies and 12 prefill-intensive tasks, with ablations replacing traces by norm-matched random vectors and a memory/latency comparison against KVzip.
TkWra2xsDM.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text is cut off before the numbers; reviewers cite Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M average 49.1 with Fast KVzip rising to 52.9 with DuetKV)
TkWra2xsDM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the progressive, eviction-independent trace construction well motivated, with broad validation across backbones, evictors and tasks and clean ablations showing trace content matters.
TkWra2xsDM.main_concern: Evidence is concentrated on Qwen-family backbones with per-backbone constructors, and there is no direct comparison to other complementary-KV methods (ResKV, IndexMem, RestoreKV) or to quantization at equal bytes.

3PXn4E10OA.one_liner: Studies weight manifold constraints in LLM pre-training and proposes MACRO, a spectral-norm-oracle optimizer on the Riemannian gradient.
3PXn4E10OA.problem: Weight-normalized, manifold-constrained LLM training performs well, but the effects of explicit weight constraints and their interaction with existing stabilizers such as normalization and weight decay are poorly understood.
3PXn4E10OA.method: They analyze constrained training through activation scales, rotational dynamics and the update-to-weight ratio, using MACRO as a testbed: an optimizer built on a spectral-norm oracle applied to the Riemannian gradient plus a radius selection principle.
3PXn4E10OA.key_idea: Constrain weights to a manifold and apply a spectral-norm (matrix-sign) oracle to the Riemannian gradient, controlling the update-to-weight ratio so weight decay becomes unnecessary.
3PXn4E10OA.evidence: Theoretical analysis and LLM pre-training experiments; reviewers note three model sizes up to 1.2B parameters with five seeds in the main results.
3PXn4E10OA.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says MACRO is competitive with existing algorithms and robust to low-precision computation, without numbers)
3PXn4E10OA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the multi-perspective analysis of weight constraints (activation scales, rotation, update-to-weight ratio) and the practical optimizer with encouraging empirical results.
3PXn4E10OA.main_concern: Limited novelty relative to prior work (the MuonH optimizer and rotational/weight-decay equilibrium analyses), and the Riemannian steepest-descent and convergence claims are not fully justified because matrix-sign after tangent projection does not preserve tangency.

jJZQk8lFh4.one_liner: Continuous rectified-flow language model using analytic singular logits and a compact context-informed embedding space, trained with cross-entropy.
jJZQk8lFh4.problem: Continuous flow language models lag discrete diffusion because they must link a continuous velocity field to a categorical vocabulary, commit to a single token as noise vanishes, and choose an embedding geometry for denoising.
jJZQk8lFh4.method: ReLF trains a rectified-flow model with cross-entropy and adds singular logits that analytically capture the divergent component of token posteriors, leaving the network a bounded residual. The flow runs in a compact, context-informed embedding space, and reflow straightens trajectories for few-step generation.
jJZQk8lFh4.key_idea: Singular logits analytically capture the divergent part of the token posterior, leaving a bounded residual for the network and guaranteeing convergence to valid token embeddings.
jJZQk8lFh4.evidence: Unconditional generation on OpenWebText with 64 function evaluations at several model sizes, scored by generative perplexity at matched diversity (unigram entropy), with a singular-logit ablation and theory (Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.3).
jJZQk8lFh4.claimed_gains: On OpenWebText with 64 function evaluations, ReLF attains lower generative perplexity than autoregressive baselines at every model size tested under matched diversity; no other numbers are stated.
jJZQk8lFh4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the commitment guarantee and singular logits well motivated and the unconditional results strong, with the continuous model beating size-matched autoregressive baselines at every scale.
jJZQk8lFh4.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to saturated unconditional OpenWebText with generative perplexity and unigram entropy, with no discrete-diffusion baseline, weak few-step comparisons, and a hand-crafted Hellinger embedding that is not fully ablated.

KHG8HbEhFU.one_liner: Weights on-policy distillation tokens by Fisher utility: the maximal local loss decrease under an equal KL budget.
KHG8HbEhFU.problem: Token-selection methods for on-policy distillation use heuristic signals such as uncertainty or teacher-student disagreement rather than deriving token importance from the distillation objective itself.
KHG8HbEhFU.method: They define token utility s_t = g_t^T F_t^dagger g_t from the logit gradient and the categorical Fisher matrix, which equals the student-weighted variance of the log-probability ratio for reverse-KL and the Pearson chi-squared divergence for forward-KL. They instantiate it as Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW), a continuous, mean-normalized token weighting.
KHG8HbEhFU.key_idea: Rank each position by how much its loss can drop under an equal local KL budget, giving a closed-form Fisher utility that depends on the KL direction.
KHG8HbEhFU.evidence: Seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and three Qwen3 student-teacher pairs, compared with matched uniform OPD and other token criteria (entropy, KL disagreement, TIP), plus a weight-shuffling ablation.
KHG8HbEhFU.claimed_gains: FUW improves over matched uniform OPD by 1.35–4.0 macro points under reverse-KL and 1.08–2.71 macro points under forward-KL.
KHG8HbEhFU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the derivation clear and the closed-form scores for reverse and forward KL cheap to compute, with consistent gains over uniform OPD and a shuffling control showing weight placement matters.
KHG8HbEhFU.main_concern: Gains over simpler criteria such as TIP are not consistently significant, and the per-position local derivation ignores parameter sharing and downstream effects on the final answer.

ewUkf1LIfW.one_liner: Self-Speculative Prefill builds draft KV entries with low-rank maps, verifies them, and routes tokens to accept or fall back.
ewUkf1LIfW.problem: Prefill dominates long-context inference with short outputs, and existing KV construction methods skip exact computation through open-loop decisions that never check whether constructed cache entries are acceptable.
ewUkf1LIfW.method: SSP has construction, verification, routing and fallback components; its realization ACSSP builds KV entries with low-rank residual KV maps on frozen weights, scores drafts with a training-free attention-weighted verification score, routes tokens to aggressive acceptance or continuation to a conservative anchor, and reuses verification-boundary states.
ewUkf1LIfW.key_idea: Verify draft KV entries with a training-free attention-weighted score and route each token to accept the draft or continue exact computation from a conservative anchor.
ewUkf1LIfW.evidence: LongBench, RepoBench and RULER experiments across multiple model families against POP (and SwiftKV on Llama-3.1-8B), a vLLM implementation, theoretical error bounds, and a verification-versus-random-routing ablation.
ewUkf1LIfW.claimed_gains: Compared with POP, ACSSP improves average quality on LongBench and RepoBench by up to 7.47 points, gives up to 1.25x and 1.34x TTFT speedups on RULER at 32K and 128K, and reduces mean prefill matmul FLOPs by up to 20.19%.
ewUkf1LIfW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a coherent verification-guided KV construction framework with theoretical analysis, a vLLM implementation, broad experiments, and ablations showing verification-guided routing beats random routing.
ewUkf1LIfW.main_concern: Baseline coverage is thin: POP is the main comparison, SwiftKV matches quality at lower latency on some tasks, DASH and FastKV are not compared, and speedups over POP are modest.

jBge92WJps.one_liner: NF-CoT models continuous latent thoughts with a TarFlow-style normalizing flow inside the LLM, giving exact likelihoods and KV-cache decoding.
jBge92WJps.problem: Existing latent-reasoning methods give up native left-to-right generation, probabilistic sampling, KV-cache compatibility and tractable likelihood, the properties that make explicit chain-of-thought effective.
jBge92WJps.method: NF-CoT instantiates a TarFlow-style normalizing flow inside the LLM backbone to define a tractable probability model over compact continuous thoughts distilled from explicit CoT. Continuous-thought positions are generated by an NF head and text positions by the standard LM head in the same causal stream.
jBge92WJps.key_idea: Generate compact continuous thoughts with a normalizing-flow head inside the causal LLM stream, giving exact likelihoods for latent thoughts while keeping KV-cache-compatible decoding.
jBge92WJps.evidence: Code-generation results against SFT and LaDiR on the same backbone and training data, with a likelihood-based RL stage and ablations such as NF-density sample selection.
jBge92WJps.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results; a reviewer cites a 13.3-point average pass@1 increase for unified NF-CoT)
jBge92WJps.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like formulating latent reasoning as an autoregressive probability model that restores sampling, scoring and KV-cache decoding, and find the code-generation gains over SFT and LaDiR convincing.
jBge92WJps.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the flow or the exact likelihood: NF-density sample selection is close to random, the likelihood-based RL gain is modest, and a matched autoregressive Gaussian baseline over the same latents is missing.

0GCxw4jqE5.one_liner: Benchmark of 409 professional Building Information Modeling tasks for computer-use agents in real Revit and Archicad environments.
0GCxw4jqE5.problem: Existing computer-use benchmarks favor breadth across general applications over depth in professional workflows with diverse, tightly coupled operations, as in BIM authoring.
0GCxw4jqE5.method: BIMArena has 409 tasks at three levels (fundamental software operations, long-sequence workflows, domain reasoning), run in isolated real-computer environments with programmatic state-based evaluation. It also tests whether software documentation and expert-curated operational skills improve agent performance.
0GCxw4jqE5.key_idea: Score agents by reading the final BIM model state through native APIs against typed checkpoints, over paired long-sequence and reasoning tasks of increasing depth.
0GCxw4jqE5.evidence: Experiments with proprietary models and open-source computer-use agents in isolated real-computer environments using a programmatic evaluation framework, plus analysis of documentation and expert-skill support and failure cases.
0GCxw4jqE5.claimed_gains: The strongest agent reaches a 98.4% success rate on fundamental software operations but only 26.6% on realistic professional tasks.
0GCxw4jqE5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically relevant and the benchmark well built, with real GUI interaction, native-API state-based scoring without an LLM judge, a three-level task design and paired tasks.
0GCxw4jqE5.main_concern: Contribution beyond existing professional-software and CAD/BIM benchmarks (OSWorld, ProSoftArena) is mostly a new domain, with limited analytical insight and single-run evaluations lacking statistical robustness.

iMrwrAdPuD.one_liner: Adaptive per-attribute steering schedules for discrete diffusion language models, derived from sparse-autoencoder commitment timing profiles.
iMrwrAdPuD.problem: Controlled-generation methods imported from autoregressive models steer uniformly at every denoising step, which is inefficient, degrades quality, and compounds when several attributes are steered jointly.
iMrwrAdPuD.method: They train sparse autoencoders on four DLMs (124M-8B parameters) to measure when each attribute commits during denoising, then use an adaptive scheduling mechanism that concentrates intervention where each attribute is actively forming. An idealized allocation analysis predicts which attributes benefit most.
iMrwrAdPuD.key_idea: Allocate steering strength across denoising steps in proportion to when each attribute's SAE features actively emerge, rather than applying uniform intervention.
iMrwrAdPuD.evidence: SAE analysis on four DLMs, then seven single- and multi-attribute steering tasks on four DLMs against uniform and interval-restricted baselines, with matched-confidence and matched-quality analyses.
iMrwrAdPuD.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent control-quality gains over uniform and interval-restricted baselines across seven tasks on four DLMs, without improvement magnitudes)
iMrwrAdPuD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the SAE-based commitment-timing characterization useful, with broad evaluation across four models and seven conditions and an intuitive budgeted-allocation view of steering.
iMrwrAdPuD.main_concern: Baselines do not isolate the contribution: the schedule is never applied to the contrastive-vector baseline, so it is unclear whether SAE decomposition or temporal scheduling drives the gains, and novelty over prior stage-dependent steering is overstated.

IVJnUfZ3IU.one_liner: Fine-tunes language models against continuously updated activation probes for harmlessness and honesty while preserving probe-based monitorability.
IVJnUfZ3IU.problem: Output-based alignment rewards responses that look aligned and can be satisfied by superficial compliance, while training against probes risks models evading them and losing monitorability.
IVJnUfZ3IU.method: Probe-guided fine-tuning uses linear and non-linear probes that detect undesired properties in model activations as a direct training signal, with probes updated continuously during training instead of frozen. They vary probe type and number of probes per layer on harmlessness and honesty objectives.
IVJnUfZ3IU.key_idea: Retrain the detection probes continuously during fine-tuning so the model cannot bypass a frozen probe, using probe scores on activations as the training loss.
IVJnUfZ3IU.evidence: Linear and non-linear probes on harmlessness and honesty objectives, compared with output-based alignment and inference-time steering at matched data and gradient-update budgets, plus jailbreak and abliteration robustness and linear-decodability checks.
IVJnUfZ3IU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports lower harmfulness at high utility than output-based methods and steering, and higher robustness to jailbreak and abliteration attacks, without numbers)
IVJnUfZ3IU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see training against probes as a timely question and agree that continuously updated probes avoid the frozen-probe failure while reducing harmfulness and improving honesty at preserved utility.
IVJnUfZ3IU.main_concern: Evidence for preserved monitorability (linear decodability only), the fairness of comparisons (DPO is offline, no online-RL baseline without latents) and the small number of tested models are questioned.

k6gGotFd64.one_liner: Self-distillation for amortized cryo-EM reconstruction: VICReg on model-reprojected, re-noised particle views to learn noise-invariant encoders.
k6gGotFd64.problem: Encoders in autoencoder-based heterogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction overfit to the extremely noisy training images and fail to generalize to unseen particles.
k6gGotFd64.method: CryoNOO uses the reconstruction model itself as a denoiser: it reconstructs and reprojects training particles to obtain denoised views, augments them with independent noise realizations, and applies a self-supervised VICReg loss through an expander head that is discarded after training.
k6gGotFd64.key_idea: Reproject each particle through the reconstruction model to get a denoised view, re-noise it with independent noise draws, and apply a VICReg loss across the views.
k6gGotFd64.evidence: Synthetic and experimental cryo-EM datasets, with ablations of noise augmentation and the self-supervised objective (SimSiam, invariance-only, no expander) and a held-out-conformation test.
k6gGotFd64.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says CryoNOO enables large-scale amortized reconstruction from a subset of particles and generalizes to unseen conformations and particles, without numbers)
k6gGotFd64.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method a simple, plug-and-play fix for encoder memorization in cryoDRGN-style models, clearly motivated and written, with multi-dataset experiments and useful ablations.
k6gGotFd64.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to the claimed mechanism: there is no control applying VICReg to raw-image views without reprojection, no stop-gradient ablation, and the unseen-conformation validation is thin.

xilSk7TxGG.one_liner: Shows that much of the representation geometry shared across language models comes from input embedding and output unembedding geometry.
xilSk7TxGG.problem: Language models of different sizes and architectures show similar representation geometry (cycles, helices) often read as traces of computation, but its origin is unexplained.
xilSk7TxGG.method: They trace how input-embedding shape extends into middle layers and how representations converge to output-prediction geometry before the last layer, train models with no hidden layers or one attention layer to recover shared geometry, and run tokenizer interventions.
xilSk7TxGG.key_idea: Attribute shared representation geometry to low-order corpus statistics imprinted on input and output weights, tested with shallow models and tokenizer interventions, rather than to task-specific computation.
xilSk7TxGG.evidence: Embedding and unembedding comparisons with global (CKA) and local (mean neighborhood overlap) metrics, models with zero hidden layers or one attention layer, tokenizer interventions, and tracing of six previously reported structures.
xilSk7TxGG.claimed_gains: not stated (results are qualitative: shallow models recover a large fraction of the shared geometry and six reported structures trace to input or answer shape)
xilSk7TxGG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question important and the simple input/output-geometry explanation well motivated, supported by shallow-model comparisons and both global and local geometry metrics.
xilSk7TxGG.main_concern: Novelty and insight are unclear, since early-layer similarity to embeddings and late-layer similarity to unembeddings follow from residual connections and decoding, and the claim that this explains away task-specific computation is overstated.

Dmh1NL7Nes.one_liner: Learns a set-level scorer from a few hundred finetune-and-evaluate runs to select stronger poison sets for LLM backdoor attacks.
Dmh1NL7Nes.problem: Backdoor evaluations fix the poison count and sample poisons at random, which can understate worst-case vulnerability because attack success depends strongly on which poison set is chosen.
Dmh1NL7Nes.method: They formalize poison selection as oracle-budgeted set optimization and introduce SAILS, which learns a set scorer from a few hundred finetune-and-evaluate runs, ranks millions of candidate sets, and audits only a small shortlist.
Dmh1NL7Nes.key_idea: Learn a surrogate that scores whole poison sets from a few hundred finetune-and-evaluate oracle runs, then rank millions of candidate sets and audit only a shortlist.
Dmh1NL7Nes.evidence: Three LLaMA-3-8B backdoor settings compared with influence baselines (TRAK), random search and greedy selection under different oracle budgets, plus transfer to full-scale finetuning and extensions to code-generation, agentic and API-only backdoors.
Dmh1NL7Nes.claimed_gains: Attack success ranges from 3% to 80% depending only on the chosen poison set, and SAILS improves held-out attack success by 30 percentage points on average over the strongest influence baselines.
Dmh1NL7Nes.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find poison-set composition an important problem and the experiments extensive, covering influence-based, random-search and greedy baselines and an analysis of proxy optimization and set interactions.
Dmh1NL7Nes.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from modeling set interactions rather than learning a better surrogate (a simple Ridge scorer is competitive), and reproducibility and extension-experiment details are ambiguous.

ZGeR4gkEZq.one_liner: Assigns an MX element format per 16x32 tile from a single one-pass statistic using thresholds derived once offline.
ZGeR4gkEZq.problem: Uniform MXFP4 still incurs substantial quantization error, and existing mixed-precision fixes need calibration data, a cost repeated for every new model.
ZGeR4gkEZq.method: AdaptQuant picks an MX element format for each 16x32 tile, the granularity at which Blackwell's block-scaled MMA reads operands, from one statistic computed in a single pass over the tile. The statistic-to-format rule is derived once offline on a single reference model against NVFP4 and reused unchanged on every other model.
ZGeR4gkEZq.key_idea: Select each 16x32 tile's MX format from a single amax/rms-based statistic with thresholds derived once on a reference model, avoiding per-model calibration data.
ZGeR4gkEZq.evidence: 13 open-weight LLMs on a single RTX 5090, with perplexity on WikiText-2 and C4, quantization time, stored memory and prefill throughput against mixed-precision baselines such as MicroMix, plus MMLU results.
ZGeR4gkEZq.claimed_gains: Across 13 open-weight LLMs on a single RTX 5090, mean perplexity over BF16 rises by only 5.0% on WikiText-2 and 3.9% on C4, with 2.9x faster quantization, up to 3.08x less stored weight memory than BF16 and 1.81x BF16's prefill throughput.
ZGeR4gkEZq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the one-time threshold derivation removes per-model calibration cost and that the tile granularity matching Blackwell's block-scaled MMA operands is well motivated, with faster quantization than prior methods.
ZGeR4gkEZq.main_concern: Thresholds come from a single reference model and corpus with no ablation of their generalization, and steady-state throughput gains over MicroMix are small.

SvbGUo8tLU.one_liner: Training-free reranking for ColPali-style retrieval that adds query-level evidence coverage and page-level evidence richness to MaxSim.
SvbGUo8tLU.problem: MaxSim scoring in late-interaction visual document retrievers systematically over-ranks pages with peaked similarity or insufficient supporting evidence.
SvbGUo8tLU.method: EA-MaxSim reranks pages by augmenting MaxSim with query-level evidence coverage (how well a page supports the full query intent) and page-level evidence richness (structural sufficiency of evidence, using spatial layout cues). It is a lightweight module that needs no change to training, document encoding or indexing.
SvbGUo8tLU.key_idea: Rerank by MaxSim plus a query-coverage score and a spatial-layout richness score counting connected regions among salient page patches.
SvbGUo8tLU.evidence: Experiments on ViDoRe v2 and ViDoSeek across different late-interaction backbones (ColPali, ColQwen2), with ablations, component studies and comparisons against VLM-based rerankers.
SvbGUo8tLU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent ranking-quality gains across backbones and datasets, particularly at top ranks, without numbers)
SvbGUo8tLU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, training-free and easy to add to existing late-interaction retrievers, with consistent gains across benchmarks and backbones and competitive results against costlier VLM-based rerankers.
SvbGUo8tLU.main_concern: The strongest results use parameters tuned per document subset (the richness weight is dataset-sensitive), so transfer to new collections is unclear, and ablations lack sensitivity analysis.

aJJzCyKrPe.one_liner: Survey of how clustering with noise is evaluated, plus two noise-aware ARI variants using Cohen's kappa or Matthews phi.
aJJzCyKrPe.problem: External cluster validity indices such as NMI and ARI are undefined for noise labels, so papers handle noise inconsistently, most without proper foundations.
aJJzCyKrPe.method: They survey how noise-detecting clustering papers evaluate and which datasets they use, define four desirable properties for noise-aware external CVIs, and test existing noise-handling strategies against them. They then propose NARI_kappa and NARI_phi, combining ARI on cluster points with Cohen's kappa or the Matthews-Pearson phi coefficient on the binary noise classification.
aJJzCyKrPe.key_idea: Score noise-aware clusterings as ARI over cluster points combined with Cohen's kappa or the Matthews-Pearson phi coefficient on the binary noise-versus-cluster classification.
aJJzCyKrPe.evidence: A literature survey, experiments over existing noise-handling strategies against four properties, and real-data checks with held-out minority classes and foundation-model-annotated images as noise.
aJJzCyKrPe.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says both indices satisfy all four properties and that flawed strategies certify degenerate clusterings with perfect scores, without numbers)
aJJzCyKrPe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find inconsistent noise handling in external clustering evaluation an important, overlooked problem and value the systematic survey, formalized properties and the two proposed measures.
aJJzCyKrPe.main_concern: The real-data noise protocols are proxies (held-out minority classes, CLIP-annotated images) with limited coverage, and practical significance and superiority over singleton ARI/AMI are questioned.

R5na7mjMe5.one_liner: Belief-conditioned successor features and MA-JEPA self-play treat each unseen partner as a task for zero-shot coordination.
R5na7mjMe5.problem: Zero-shot coordination needs cooperation with unseen partners, but learning how a partner changes the ego-agent's effective dynamics is hard when the partner policy is unobserved and rewards are sparse.
R5na7mjMe5.method: BSFs summarize discounted future features conditioned on a belief over the partner's latent type, inferred from interaction history and added to the state. MA-JEPA approximates BSFs in on-policy self-play with a learned history encoder and a temporal-difference latent prediction objective that gives reward-free supervision.
R5na7mjMe5.key_idea: Condition successor features on an inferred belief over partner type and learn them with a TD latent-prediction objective on a history encoder, treating each partner as a task.
R5na7mjMe5.evidence: Overcooked and SMAC against self-play, population-based and agent-modeling baselines, including sparse-reward and RGB-observation settings, with ablations and a proposition that the value of a belief-independent policy is linear in the belief.
R5na7mjMe5.claimed_gains: MA-JEPA outperforms self-play, population-based and agent-modeling baselines on Overcooked and SMAC, with the largest cross-play gains over the strongest baseline under sparse rewards (77%) and RGB observations (32%).
R5na7mjMe5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem and partner-as-task motivation reasonable, with a rigorous theoretical formulation, ablations, and substantial gains in sparse-reward and RGB settings.
R5na7mjMe5.main_concern: The theory assumes state-Markov partners and exact beliefs and covers only belief-independent policies, so it does not justify the implemented MA-JEPA agent, whose policy and partners condition on a learned latent.

V8MDFQbPcY.one_liner: Distills neural likelihoods into closed-form expressions via symbolic regression guided by a parameter-recovery objective.
V8MDFQbPcY.problem: Amortized neural likelihoods are black boxes, and accurately approximating likelihood values does not necessarily preserve the structure needed for parameter estimation.
V8MDFQbPcY.method: A recovery-directed objective guides symbolic regression toward expressions that preserve parameter-recovery accuracy. Candidates are searched on an accuracy-complexity Pareto front, validated with a full Bayesian sampler on simulated subjects, and ranked by their weakest parameter-recovery correlation.
V8MDFQbPcY.key_idea: Steer symbolic regression with a parameter-recovery objective rather than likelihood-fit error, ranking Pareto-front candidates by their weakest parameter-recovery correlation under Bayesian-sampler validation.
V8MDFQbPcY.evidence: The diffusion decision model, whose tractable likelihood gives ground truth, against standard symbolic-regression objectives, plus a second model specification without a closed-form likelihood and SBC/PPC checks.
V8MDFQbPcY.claimed_gains: The recovery-directed objective improves parameter recovery over standard symbolic-regression objectives, and the symbolic likelihoods give over 100 times faster parameter evaluation than neural and exact likelihoods; a reviewer cites the share of expressions passing recovery criteria rising from 1.2% to 19.5%.
V8MDFQbPcY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the insight that density fit and parameter recovery are different objectives well argued, with a careful pipeline and compelling speedups in diffusion-decision-model parameter recovery.
V8MDFQbPcY.main_concern: Only the diffusion decision model with a known exact likelihood is evaluated, not the intractable-likelihood models the method targets, and unnormalized expressions leave bias and calibration of inference unestablished.

KxQc2Uv1sc.one_liner: Extends backward conformal prediction to online settings with a conditional inflation factor and clipped-product surrogate for miscoverage risk bounds.
KxQc2Uv1sc.problem: Under distribution shift in online prediction, the BCP e-value expectation condition may fail and past data may no longer reflect current risk.
KxQc2Uv1sc.method: OBCP introduces a conditional inflation factor and a clipped product surrogate that bounds miscoverage risk without the e-value condition. The resulting three-term bound combines a recency-weighted average of past clipped products, a target-drift term and a finite-sample concentration term, and gives fixed-time high-probability certificates when a valid drift allowance is available.
KxQc2Uv1sc.key_idea: Bound current miscoverage with a recency-weighted average of clipped-product surrogates plus drift and concentration terms, replacing the e-value expectation condition lost under distribution shift.
KxQc2Uv1sc.evidence: Theory (the three-term risk bound and exact relations between the clipped-product statistic and empirical error counting), simulations with oracle-drift certificates, and a chronological real-data audit of the observable product statistic.
KxQc2Uv1sc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, with a carefully scoped and transparent guarantee and a well-motivated risk-reporting view under a fixed set-size budget.
KxQc2Uv1sc.main_concern: The certificate needs an externally supplied drift allowance with no non-oracle construction, so every complete simulated certificate uses oracle drift and the real-data study checks only historical summaries.

Mc23U3z76Z.one_liner: Keeps raw agent trajectories and curates task-adaptive memory at read time with a curator trained on immediate task reward.
Mc23U3z76Z.problem: Write-time memory curation must decide what to remember before the future query is known, irreversibly discards information, and makes learning the curator a long-horizon credit-assignment problem.
Mc23U3z76Z.method: JITMEM retains raw trajectories and defers curation to read time: given retrieved traces and the new task, a memory curator synthesizes a compact, task-adaptive payload that is consumed on the same task, so it can be trained directly from immediate task success.
Mc23U3z76Z.key_idea: Defer memory curation to read time so the curator's payload is consumed on the same task, letting immediate task reward train it without delayed credit assignment.
Mc23U3z76Z.evidence: ALFWorld, WebShop and tau2-bench against no-memory agents and heuristic and learned write-time memory methods (including SkillOS), with ablations and GRPO-trained curators on models such as Qwen3-8B.
Mc23U3z76Z.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the numbers; it says JITMEM consistently outperforms no-memory agents and heuristic and learned write-time memory methods)
Mc23U3z76Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the read-time reformulation simple and effective because it removes delayed-utility credit assignment and trains the curator on task reward alone, with broad evaluation, stable learning curves and thorough ablations.
Mc23U3z76Z.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are not fully controlled: no-memory numbers match another paper's table while the authors' reruns are lower, and a curator that still helps with retrieval off suggests it learns benchmark-specific hints.

Ole3GwAx4M.one_liner: Recasts weighted dataset aggregation along an expert-learner path as numerical quadrature of the path-average state occupancy.
Ole3GwAx4M.problem: Interactive imitation learning mixes expert and learner behaviour to mitigate covariate shift, but mixture points and weights are set as a training schedule without an explicit approximation target.
Ole3GwAx4M.method: They show that along a fixed expert-learner path, weighted dataset aggregation is a numerical quadrature rule for the path-average occupancy, then use classical quadrature theory to derive schedule-dependent rates for finite-state MDPs and compare schedules (Gauss-Legendre, midpoint, endpoint Riemann, DAgger, random-uniform).
Ole3GwAx4M.key_idea: Choose expert-learner mixture points and aggregation weights as quadrature nodes and weights for the path-average occupancy, so interior mixtures cover states that endpoint policies miss.
Ole3GwAx4M.evidence: Quadrature theory for finite-state MDPs (an O(n^-1) endpoint-Riemann bound and geometric convergence for Gauss-Legendre), exact evaluation and sampling experiments on Garnets, and continuous-control experiments with retraining held fixed.
Ole3GwAx4M.claimed_gains: Under independent finite sampling, Gauss-Legendre and midpoint reach an error no more than 20% above direct path-average sampling within at most three rounds at every tested budget for the median instance, while endpoint Riemann, DAgger and random-uniform schedules need many more rounds or fail to reach this level; the TLDR adds that return improves only in some environments.
Ole3GwAx4M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the quadrature framing original and rigorously developed, with a clear account of how mixing expert and learner reaches states neither visits alone and illustrative bias-variance results.
Ole3GwAx4M.main_concern: Practical benefit is not established: it is unclear that matching the path-average occupancy improves reward over a simple 50/50 mixture, and gains appear to come from interior mixtures while quadrature advantages fade under function approximation.

2OJ187fKm6.one_liner: Fault-injection testbed showing which silent tool failures make LLM agents state wrong answers, and which truncation notices prevent it.
2OJ187fKm6.problem: Tool-using LLM agents sometimes state a wrong answer as fact, and it is unclear which properties of a tool failure cause this.
2OJ187fKm6.method: QuietFail injects faults into tools over a real filesystem, SQLite databases, an HTTP service and a shell, where each of 30 multi-step tasks also runs without its fault. It varies what the failing call returns, including adding a truncation notice to otherwise unchanged output.
2OJ187fKm6.key_idea: Hold the returned data fixed and vary only the notice, comparing each faulted run with its fault-free twin, to isolate which failure properties cause confident wrong answers.
2OJ187fKm6.evidence: A main grid of seven agents from five providers (4,305 graded runs) on 30 multi-step tasks, with cross-family grading, a rule-based grader, task-level bootstrap, notice ablations and an audit of tool source code.
2OJ187fKm6.claimed_gains: A tool that silently returns half the requested records raises confident wrong answers by 18.8 points (from 7.3% to 26.1%), while a truncation notice cuts them by 17.2 points, leaving them 0.4 points above the fault-free rate.
2OJ187fKm6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled intervention that holds returned data fixed while changing the notice, the matched fault-free runs, and the practical advice for tool builders.
2OJ187fKm6.main_concern: External validity is limited: the central truncation results rest on 21 hand-built tasks with small outputs, top-k selection (the most common real limit) is untested, and grading relies on an LLM judge without human annotation.

hPo2Qo49v7.one_liner: Spectral hybrid parameterizations for flow matching that adapt the prediction target across time and data covariance directions.
hPo2Qo49v7.problem: Data-, noise- and velocity-prediction are theoretically equivalent in flow matching but perform very differently, and the causes of the gap are unclear.
hPo2Qo49v7.method: They identify the source-data signal-to-noise ratio in each data covariance direction and the architecture-induced information bottleneck as the main drivers. From this analysis they introduce spectral hybrid parameterizations (a binary switch and a continuous variant) that adapt across time and covariance directions and are optimal for Gaussian data.
hPo2Qo49v7.key_idea: Choose between data and noise prediction per covariance direction and time according to the local signal-to-noise ratio, with switching times derived from Gaussian analysis.
hPo2Qo49v7.evidence: Controlled experiments varying source noise scale and bottleneck, Gaussian analysis, and image-generation experiments on 64x64 datasets (including CelebA) across architectures and source scales, with qualitative AFHQ-256 samples.
hPo2Qo49v7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says the parameterizations are robust across regimes and can substantially accelerate optimization at essentially no additional training cost, without numbers)
hPo2Qo49v7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of prediction targets principled and informative, with controlled experiments separating intrinsic dimension from source-data SNR and the compression effect, and promising image-generation results.
hPo2Qo49v7.main_concern: Evaluation is small-scale (mostly 64x64 with qualitative higher-resolution results), and the benefit of the continuous hybrid over simpler denoiser preconditioning and of per-direction over global SNR adaptation is unclear.

efDkna4Qe4.one_liner: Applies strong temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in training, then removes it, lowering LLM loss versus Muon.
efDkna4Qe4.problem: Spectral control on top of Muon has given only modest gains: concentrated spectra suppress gradient directions in coupled weight matrices, while constraints kept throughout training limit adaptation and raise the attainable loss floor.
efDkna4Qe4.method: ORCA (Orthogonal Regularization, Cooled After) applies strong but temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in training, then removes it so weights get a broader spectrum early and adapt freely afterward. It needs no architectural changes and adds minimal overhead.
efDkna4Qe4.key_idea: Shape the weight spectrum with soft orthogonality regularization in the early phase only, then release it, trading an early broader spectrum for later free adaptation.
efDkna4Qe4.evidence: LLaMA, Qwen3 and fine-grained mixture-of-experts models from 130M to 8B parameters, with ablations on regularization timing, effective-rank trajectories, gradient statistics, controlled spectral interventions, and a simplified matrix-factorization theory.
efDkna4Qe4.claimed_gains: ORCA reaches lower final validation loss than Muon across models from 130M to 8B parameters, and its loss reduction relative to Muon matches or exceeds Muon's reduction relative to Adam.
efDkna4Qe4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mixed-effects observation about spectral regularization interesting and the method simple with no architectural change, with consistent gains across architectures and scales and supportive timing ablations.
efDkna4Qe4.main_concern: Novelty over existing orthogonality and Muon-variant work is limited and uncompared, effective-rank causation is not isolated without a norm-matched control, and several gains are small with multi-seed results only at 130M.

JBgLTnYDhQ.one_liner: Converts pretrained 3D reconstruction models to layerwise hybrids: linear attention in tolerant stages, tile-sparse attention in sensitive stages.
JBgLTnYDhQ.problem: The quadratic cost of global attention limits feed-forward 3D foundation models that reconstruct scenes from unposed images to large view sets.
JBgLTnYDhQ.method: Zebra3D assigns linear-centered attention to stages tolerant of linear replacement and tile-sparse attention to sensitive stages, with landmark summaries preserving unselected context. Closed-form affine fitting gives training-free conversion, and optional post-conversion training combines task supervision with output and relational feature distillation.
JBgLTnYDhQ.key_idea: Measure each stage's sensitivity to linear replacement, which tracks attention concentration, and assign linear or tile-sparse attention accordingly, using closed-form affine fitting for conversion.
JBgLTnYDhQ.evidence: Three backbones (VGGT, HunyuanWorld-Mirror, pi^3) on reconstruction and camera-pose benchmarks (e.g., 7Scenes, RE10K, NRGBD, CO3Dv2) against FastVGGT, SAF3R and A3D, with calibration-set and distillation ablations.
JBgLTnYDhQ.claimed_gains: End-to-end speedups reach up to 7.1x at 1,024 views in the aggressive configuration, with training-free conservative variants close to dense counterparts; the abstract is cut off at Zebra3D-VGGT reaching 80.5% after post-conversion training.
JBgLTnYDhQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the depth-wise diagnosis (sensitivity tracks attention concentration, consistent across three backbones) clear and the training-free conversion practical, with extensive evaluation and measurable speedups.
JBgLTnYDhQ.main_concern: The advantage over existing efficient methods is inconsistent across backbones and settings (comparable in some, with no method dominating on VGGT), and absolute latency, memory and relational-distillation ablations are missing.

DoLPblAZdE.one_liner: LLM-assisted pipeline that generates propositions and reference labels to test agents' self-reported belief accuracy and consistency in agentic tasks.
DoLPblAZdE.problem: Beliefs about environment state and task progress could diagnose agent failures, but reference belief labels are often unavailable or hard to obtain.
DoLPblAZdE.method: The pipeline grounds LLM-authored proposition templates in agent trajectories and obtains labels from an LLM-assisted reference observer using formal logical rules and Bayesian inference. It then evaluates consistency and accuracy across World, Epistemic, Affordance and Decision propositions and relates them to task success.
DoLPblAZdE.key_idea: Query beliefs at the same trajectory prefix and score them against labels from a reference observer using logical rules and Bayesian inference, then relate accuracy to task success.
DoLPblAZdE.evidence: ALFWorld, WebShop and Noisy Cabinets with models of 14B parameters or fewer (mostly Qwen family), measuring belief consistency and accuracy and their relation to task success.
DoLPblAZdE.claimed_gains: not stated (findings are qualitative: Affordance and Decision accuracy generally correlate with task success, while World and Epistemic accuracy matter only in specific environments)
DoLPblAZdE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find belief accuracy in agents an important, under-examined question, with a modular proposition pipeline, a rational reference observer under partial observability, and well-designed evaluations.
DoLPblAZdE.main_concern: Only small models (14B and under, mostly Qwen) are tested, and self-reported beliefs are unverified proxies for internal beliefs, with reference labels using information the agent cannot know so Unknown answers may be legitimate.

1F9W34KhUv.one_liner: Training-free distractor filtering for feed-forward 3DGS using self-view and cross-view tests on per-view predicted Gaussians.
1F9W34KhUv.problem: Transient content in casual multi-view captures persists in feed-forward 3DGS reconstructions and causes blurred, duplicated or floating artifacts in novel views.
1F9W34KhUv.method: Self-view filtering compares each input with a rendering that excludes its associated Gaussians to expose unsupported content, and cross-view filtering measures how those Gaussians interfere with reconstruction of other views. Gaussians selected by either path are removed from a single frozen prediction.
1F9W34KhUv.key_idea: Invert the association between predicted Gaussians and their source views: remove Gaussians that the remaining views do not support or that interfere with other views' reconstruction.
1F9W34KhUv.evidence: Several recent feed-forward 3DGS models on novel-view-synthesis benchmarks with distractors and varying numbers of input views, plus clean-input preservation checks and ablations of self-view and cross-view filtering.
1F9W34KhUv.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports improved rendering quality with varying numbers of input views and largely preserved reconstructions on clean inputs)
1F9W34KhUv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free, model-agnostic idea elegant and well motivated, with two complementary filtering signals and consistent gains across backbones and numbers of input views.
1F9W34KhUv.main_concern: Robustness and evidence are limited: consistently observed distractors are retained, filtering depends on view selection and on models exposing per-view Gaussian association, and the gain over simple differential filtering is thin.

Gd4IZKowBl.one_liner: Stability theory for generator-based symmetry discovery, framed as subspace recovery through a task-specific symmetry-measuring operator.
Gd4IZKowBl.problem: Symmetry-discovery methods target functions, data distributions or PDE solution sets through different formulations, making common conditions for success hard to identify.
Gd4IZKowBl.method: They formulate generator-based symmetry discovery as recovering a subspace through a task-specific symmetry-measuring operator, giving one framework for how surrogate models and numerical approximations affect recovered symmetries. They derive sufficient conditions for accurate recovery and an error bound, and add a taxonomy of existing methods.
Gd4IZKowBl.key_idea: Recover symmetry generators as the null-space of a symmetry-measuring operator, with error bounded by surrogate operator error relative to the gap between symmetry and non-symmetry directions.
Gd4IZKowBl.evidence: Theory (sufficient conditions and an error bound) validated in controlled environments across three settings where the true symmetry subgroup, perturbation strength and failure modes can be controlled.
Gd4IZKowBl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified operator-based view of functional, distributional and PDE symmetry discovery timely and the theory convincing under its assumptions, with clear subspace-recovery results.
Gd4IZKowBl.main_concern: The guarantees rest on strong assumptions (finite-dimensional symmetry subspace, isolated spectral gap, small operator error) and do not link surrogate prediction error to operator error, with experiments only in controlled settings.

RlmGMmJscX.one_liner: Proves excess conformal set size over the Bayes-optimal set is bounded by square-root Brier regret, so ordinary loss minimization suffices.
RlmGMmJscX.problem: Conformal prediction fixes coverage but not set usefulness, and it is unclear how well ordinary probability estimation by loss minimization serves the goal of small expected set size.
RlmGMmJscX.method: They treat expected set size at fixed marginal coverage as a downstream objective and prove, for sets induced by probability conformity scores, a bound on excess size of K^(3/2)/alpha times the square root of excess Brier loss, plus a more general model-class bound via the loss improvement achievable by post-processings. They compare against ConfTr.
RlmGMmJscX.key_idea: Bound conformal set-size regret by the square root of proper-loss (Brier) regret, with no margin or density assumption, so standard loss minimization controls set size.
RlmGMmJscX.evidence: Theorems with sharp dependence on K and alpha up to a universal constant, plus experiments comparing loss minimization with ConfTr on synthetic tasks and real data.
RlmGMmJscX.claimed_gains: Excess expected set size over the Bayes-optimal set is at most K^(3/2)/alpha times the square root of excess Brier loss, with sharp dependence on K and alpha; the abstract is cut off before its experimental result against ConfTr.
RlmGMmJscX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and well motivated, with a new perspective of controlling set size through ordinary loss minimization, rigorous theorems, and better results than ConfTr on clear synthetic tasks.
RlmGMmJscX.main_concern: The theory needs population Bayes regret or benchmark-dependent post-processing optimality with no learning guarantee linking it to trained models, and the empirical study uses only one baseline (ConfTr).

6QqOOmOCTe.one_liner: Dynamical mean-field theory of multi-epoch SGD explains late-time overfitting and why ensembling suppresses it at matched compute.
6QqOOmOCTe.problem: Pretraining is becoming bound by total data rather than compute, so scaling laws must account for repeated epochs and for how ensembling interacts with data reuse.
6QqOOmOCTe.method: They run language-model experiments on FineWeb with logit averaging, and derive a dynamical mean-field theory for multi-epoch SGD in power-law random-feature ensembles that tracks error correlations across epochs and models. The resulting optimal stopping times give compute-allocation laws at fixed data and model sizes.
6QqOOmOCTe.key_idea: Ensembling reduces the prediction variance that drives late-time test-error growth, shifting the optimal stopping time, which the DMFT of multi-epoch random-feature SGD quantifies.
6QqOOmOCTe.evidence: Language-model experiments on FineWeb comparing logit-averaged ensembles with wider or deeper single models at matched parameter-token budgets, plus DMFT theory and noiseless random-feature simulations.
6QqOOmOCTe.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says logit averaging reduces late-training deterioration, delays optimal stopping and can outperform wider or deeper single models, without numbers)
6QqOOmOCTe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework connecting data reuse, ensembling and optimal stopping interesting and practically relevant, with nontrivial analysis of ensemble-dependent stopping and supporting FineWeb and random-feature experiments.
6QqOOmOCTe.main_concern: Originality is limited to a specific theoretical extension, the link to language-model training stays qualitative, and the advantage over tuned single models and the proposed compute allocation are not directly validated.

JESONnykQQ.one_liner: Reconstructs surfaces by regressing first-hit depth along each sensor ray with a 1-Lipschitz network traced by sphere tracing.
JESONnykQQ.problem: Neural surface reconstruction from noisy, outlier-laden range scans usually discards sensor positions and visibility, compensating with geometric priors or regularization terms.
JESONnykQQ.method: They formulate reconstruction as robust (Huber) regression of the predicted first surface intersection along each acquisition ray against the measured depth, penalizing surface intersections within the segment between sensor and observed point. The surface is the zero set of a 1-Lipschitz MLP, enabling linearly convergent sphere tracing for the first hit, with no oriented normals, off-surface samples or eikonal loss.
JESONnykQQ.key_idea: Supervise each sensor ray with the first-hit depth of a 1-Lipschitz implicit surface found by sphere tracing, so predicted surfaces in the free space before each measurement are penalized.
JESONnykQQ.evidence: Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real data under varying noise and outlier contamination (including Labatut and an NDF-vis adaptation), plus analysis of the fidelity-robustness trade-off.
JESONnykQQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says competitive performance on clean data and much improved fidelity and robustness under even moderate corruption, without numbers)
JESONnykQQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find first-hit depth regression a clean, well-motivated formulation that uses sensor visibility and replaces several inputs and loss terms with one ray-wise loss.
JESONnykQQ.main_concern: Comparisons are limited: it is unclear how much robustness comes from using sensor positions rather than the formulation, and many recent methods (normal-orientation, Gauss-formula, heat-based) are not compared.

cm9AfLxwbm.one_liner: AgentLance orchestrates LLM agents through a repeated labor market with private-cost bidding, VCG-style payments and subcontracting.
cm9AfLxwbm.problem: Centralized planners assigning every task become a bottleneck as agent pools grow, need agents' private information such as execution costs, and are manipulable: a single inserted preference nearly doubles a favored agent's task share.
cm9AfLxwbm.method: Agents bid using private cost estimates and strategy notes, while the platform selects winners using bids and success probabilities predicted by an estimator, with a VCG-style payment rule encouraging cost-aware bidding. Winning agents can decompose work and subcontract it through the same mechanism.
cm9AfLxwbm.key_idea: Allocate tasks by repeated decentralized bidding on private cost estimates, with VCG-style payments for cost-aware bids and subcontracting through the same market.
cm9AfLxwbm.evidence: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, knowledge-intensive QA and agentic tasks against single-model, centralized-orchestration (e.g., CARROT) and market baselines, with component ablations and cost-estimation interventions.
cm9AfLxwbm.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says AgentLance consistently outperforms single-model, centralized-orchestration and market baselines and shifts work to cheaper agents as cost sensitivity rises, without numbers)
cm9AfLxwbm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the market-mechanism framing clever and well motivated for heterogeneous agents with private costs, with broad task coverage, component ablations and useful analysis of cost estimation and bidding.
cm9AfLxwbm.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to bidding (reflective notes, reputation and subcontracting also change), accuracy lacks error bars or significance tests, and prompted LLM cost and success estimates are unvalidated.

e6wBXihYGF.one_liner: Defines alignment-generalization prediction and benchmarks value representations that predict how fine-tuning on one value shifts others.
