e6wBXihYGF.problem: Post-training on narrow behaviors changes model behavior in unexpected ways across unseen contexts, and developers lack a way to predict how training on one value affects others.
e6wBXihYGF.method: They define the task of predicting how fine-tuning a model to follow one value changes behavior on held-out values, measure generalization effects across 66 values with single-value SFT and DPO, and benchmark representation techniques, comparing activation-based representations with text-description embeddings. They also derive a value taxonomy (ValueMap) from empirical generalization.
e6wBXihYGF.key_idea: Represent each value by model activations when applying it in context, and predict cross-value fine-tuning effects from representational similarity between values.
e6wBXihYGF.evidence: Large-scale analysis over 66 values from modern alignment targets with SFT and DPO on two model families, correlating representation similarity with generalization matrices and with the robustness of multi-value targets.
e6wBXihYGF.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says activation-based representations significantly outperform methods based on textual descriptions, without numbers)
e6wBXihYGF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find predicting cross-value training effects an important problem and value the benchmark and the ValueMap taxonomy, with activation-based representations (especially persona vectors) consistently beating description-based embeddings.
e6wBXihYGF.main_concern: The evidence does not directly show prediction of a specific fine-tuning effect (it correlates similarity with matrix entries), and transfer measurements rely on LLM-judge scores without independent validation.

FqnXcn0AsU.one_liner: ScaleLogic shows RL training compute follows a power law in reasoning depth, with exponent rising with logical expressiveness.
FqnXcn0AsU.problem: Studying how RL training scales with task difficulty lacks controlled, scalable environments, and observed long-horizon reasoning failures may or may not be fundamental to autoregressive transformers.
FqnXcn0AsU.method: ScaleLogic is a synthetic logical reasoning framework with independent control over proof-planning depth (the horizon) and the expressiveness of the formal system, from implication-only logic to first-order reasoning with conjunction, disjunction, negation and universal quantification.
FqnXcn0AsU.key_idea: Vary proof-planning depth and logical expressiveness independently in synthetic tasks with exact verification, then fit RL training compute against depth to measure scaling exponents.
FqnXcn0AsU.evidence: RL training on synthetic ScaleLogic tasks across multiple logic settings, RL algorithms and curricula, with a Z3 audit, plus transfer evaluation on downstream mathematics and general reasoning benchmarks.
FqnXcn0AsU.claimed_gains: RL training compute T follows a power law in reasoning depth D (T proportional to D^gamma, R^2 > 0.99) with gamma rising monotonically with expressiveness from 1.05 to 2.60, and more expressive training gives downstream gains of up to +10.66 points.
FqnXcn0AsU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find ScaleLogic a useful, cheaply generated and exactly verifiable framework, and find the result that more expressive training gives larger, more sustained downstream gains supported by strong experimental coverage.
FqnXcn0AsU.main_concern: The power-law evidence is thinner than the abstract suggests: mostly one run per configuration over short depth ranges with only power-law and exponential fits compared, and expressiveness is not isolated from structural complexity.

VVpjJzCkON.one_liner: Adds DNA molecular priors to genomic foundation model training via regional property prediction and optional local feature injection.
VVpjJzCkON.problem: Genomic foundation models treat DNA as a string with masked-token objectives, without explicitly modeling the biochemical, structural and physical properties essential to biological function.
VVpjJzCkON.method: During self-supervised training VANDAM predicts regional molecular properties, estimated from sequence with established biophysical models, from pooled representations. When functional labels exist and can reward retaining the priors, local features are also injected at the input.
VVpjJzCkON.key_idea: Supervise pooled representations to predict sequence-derived biophysical properties per region, and inject local molecular features at the input when functional labels reward them.
VVpjJzCkON.evidence: Six backbones across four architecture families on 15 held-out genomic tasks (including GFMBench-API tasks), with matched-continuation baselines, component and non-biological controls, and probing of unseen molecular properties.
VVpjJzCkON.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says VANDAM consistently improves downstream performance across six backbones spanning four architecture families and 15 held-out genomic tasks, without effect sizes)
VVpjJzCkON.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find incorporating molecular priors into genomic pretraining a valuable, simple and broadly applicable idea, evaluated across many backbones and tasks with informative matched-continuation controls.
VVpjJzCkON.main_concern: Novelty is incremental over UTR-LM and MIXBend, there is no baseline that feeds the molecular features directly to downstream embeddings, and context length (8,192 bp) and model sizes are small.

uLgqvrIZhH.one_liner: Mixture of Model Optimization hands one model's discovered solutions to other RLVR-trained models, which keep their own weights.
uLgqvrIZhH.problem: RLVR can improve a model's solutions to a single problem, but each model refines toward its own behaviors and, once it stalls, further training rarely changes its approach.
uLgqvrIZhH.method: Instead of training one model longer, MOMO uses the solutions one model has found as the starting point for training other models. Each recipient keeps its own weights, so it brings different learned behaviors to the same solutions.
uLgqvrIZhH.key_idea: Pass the solution buffer from a stalled RLVR run to a different base model as its starting point, so differing learned behaviors push past the stall.
uLgqvrIZhH.evidence: Mathematical constructions, circuit placement and qubit routing with three models of roughly 30B parameters, including a seeded study on the Erdos minimum overlap problem and ablations on transferring solution buffers and retaining weights.
uLgqvrIZhH.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers in the abstract (it says MOMO consistently improves on single-model training and claims new best results on circuit placement, qubit routing and the Erdos minimum overlap problem, holding across seeds); a reviewer cites placement cost falling from 0.9533 to 0.9214.
uLgqvrIZhH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using model diversity through solution transfer simple, well written and promising, with concrete discoveries (including a new Erdos minimum-overlap construction) and ablations supporting buffer transfer and retained weights.
uLgqvrIZhH.main_concern: The central better-than-single-model claim lacks a compute-matched control: MOMO uses 37 model-steps versus 25 for each single-model run, and an equal-budget continued run or independent parallel ensemble is missing.

fdO3ufD302.one_liner: Parallel speculative-decoding drafter pairing a unigram token proposer with a bigram selector to build draft trees.
fdO3ufD302.problem: Parallel drafters lose their gains as the target distribution gets more entropic, especially at later draft-block positions and in long contexts, where limited draft diversity constrains acceptance.
fdO3ufD302.method: A unigram proposer, trained with cross-entropy, generates candidate tokens independently per position, and a lightweight bigram selector predicts transition scores between adjacent candidate pairs to build drafting trees. The selector is trained with a renormalized KL objective on high-temperature data to broaden supervision beyond the greedy path.
fdO3ufD302.key_idea: Score transitions between adjacent candidate tokens with a parallel bigram selector, trained with renormalized KL on high-temperature data, to assemble multi-branch draft trees.
fdO3ufD302.evidence: Seven standardized benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B against drafters including DFlash 2, DSpark and DARTree, with integration into serving engines such as SGLang.
fdO3ufD302.claimed_gains: UBTree achieves an average speedup of 5.84-6.94x over autoregressive decoding across seven benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B; the abstract is cut off before its comparison with other methods.
fdO3ufD302.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design well motivated, balancing adjacent-token dependency modeling with parallel efficiency, and report consistent speedups over tree-based baselines with lower draft latency and serving-engine integration.
fdO3ufD302.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the proposer, selector and tree construction come from DFlash, DFlash 2 and DARTree, and gains over DARTree come mainly from lower draft latency with only a tiny acceptance-length improvement.

z64dYJk8FX.one_liner: Hierarchical classifier whose prototype distances match taxonomic distances exactly, using a frozen head to cut mistake severity.
z64dYJk8FX.problem: Hierarchical classification methods build the taxonomy into the loss, soft targets or feature regularization but lack a principled account of how these changes affect the decision rule.
z64dYJk8FX.method: They define prototype rules (classifiers deciding by distance to class prototypes) and T-faithfulness (squared prototype distances equal taxonomic distances), characterize which feature layouts and classifier heads achieve it, and propose a frozen-head training objective that realizes it by construction. A neural-collapse analysis of an MSE objective explains why training a T-faithful model without freezing the head is hard.
z64dYJk8FX.key_idea: Fix the classifier head so squared distances between class prototypes equal taxonomic distances and class-dependent decision offsets vanish, then train features against that frozen head.
z64dYJk8FX.evidence: Theory (a characterization via the reduced tree Laplacian and a neural-collapse analysis) and an empirical comparison with several strong baselines on three datasets with at most 196 leaf classes and two- or three-level taxonomies.
z64dYJk8FX.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says T-faithful models offer competitive accuracy and the lowest mistake severity among several strong baselines, without numbers)
z64dYJk8FX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the precise geometric decision-rule formulation and the exact constructive characterization (Theorem 3) a nontrivial contribution, with appropriately chosen baselines.
z64dYJk8FX.main_concern: Gains are not isolated to T-faithfulness since both the classifier head and the training objective change, and the evidence is limited to shallow taxonomies with at most 196 leaf classes.

3xacAhxAf0.one_liner: Driving simulator pairing a long-horizon static occupancy world model with a layout generator, needing no HD maps or logs.
3xacAhxAf0.problem: Data-driven driving simulators rely on pre-recorded logs or HD-map priors, so the environments they can produce are capped by the scale of existing annotated datasets.
3xacAhxAf0.method: OccSim is conditioned only on a single initial frame and a sequence of future ego-actions. W-DiT, a static occupancy world model that builds rigid transformations into its architecture, rolls out ultra-long horizons whose frames are fused into maps, while a Layout Generator populates the synthesized topology with reactive agents.
3xacAhxAf0.key_idea: Build rigid transformations into the W-DiT static occupancy world model for stable ultra-long rollouts, fuse frames into maps, and populate them with reactive agents.
3xacAhxAf0.evidence: Long-horizon generation compared with a reproduced SemCity baseline (2D-FID, connectivity), qualitative stress tests beyond 110K frames, ablations of the stabilization recipe, and downstream pre-training of 4D semantic occupancy forecasting models on simulated data.
3xacAhxAf0.claimed_gains: Stable generation of over 3000 frames (an 80x improvement over previous occupancy world models), fused maps spanning over 9 kilometers, qualitative rollouts beyond 110K frames, and simulated data that pre-trains forecasting models to up to 67% zero-shot performance on unseen data, 11% above a previous asset-based simulator.
3xacAhxAf0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem significant and the disentangled static-environment and dynamic-agent design sensible, with substantial long-horizon results (at 10 km, 2D-FID 47.13 and 92.90% connectivity versus 148.29 and 11.70% for reproduced SemCity).
3xacAhxAf0.main_concern: The metrics (FID, connectivity) do not measure revisit or global consistency, the dynamic-agent evidence is weaker than for static generation, and the consistency claim conflates the generator with map fusion.

hond6fKtcG.one_liner: Training-free cache controller for autoregressive video diffusion that schedules exact synchronization separately from adaptive repair.
hond6fKtcG.problem: Existing cache controllers couple when the cache is synchronized exactly with how much approximate computation is spent in between, using one reactive staleness signal for both.
hond6fKtcG.method: Frequency-Step Cache (FSC) performs exact synchronization at full-computation anchors on a dense-to-sparse schedule and adaptive repair between them. A lightweight latent-space risk combining frequency-resolved drift with token age routes each non-anchor step to whole-step replay, selective token repair or full repair without changing the synchronization schedule.
hond6fKtcG.key_idea: Schedule exact synchronization anchors ahead of drift, and let measured frequency-resolved drift and token age decide only how much repair each step between anchors receives.
hond6fKtcG.evidence: SkyReels-V2 (main), FramePack, Matrix-Game and MAGI-1, compared with MotionCache and a coupled reactive controller at matched latency, with ablations and multi-seed fidelity checks.
hond6fKtcG.claimed_gains: not stated as an overall number (the abstract is cut off; a reviewer cites FSC-Quality improving SSIM by 0.031 and reducing LPIPS by 0.024 over MotionCache on SkyReels-V2)
hond6fKtcG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of synchronization and repair well motivated by thorough characterization, with consistent fidelity gains at matched latency across several video foundation models and supportive ablations.
hond6fKtcG.main_concern: The synchronization claim is not cleanly isolated (the reactive comparator also changes reference resets), elapsed steps alone predict reuse error nearly as well as the full risk, and tests cover few chunks and omit a strong related baseline.

50wZa8inrE.one_liner: Offline KV-cache compaction that picks deletions and compensates remaining entries jointly using a quadratic surrogate with closed-form updates.
50wZa8inrE.problem: Existing compaction methods score each deletion candidate independently with the rest of the cache fixed, ignoring that softmax renormalization couples deletion decisions nonlinearly.
50wZa8inrE.method: KV-Surgeon uses calibration data to derive a quadratic surrogate with closed-form expressions for the optimal greedy removal decision and for compensation within the remaining entries. An even faster variant is also introduced.
50wZa8inrE.key_idea: Score each deletion by how well remaining entries can compensate for it under a quadratic surrogate, in the manner of Optimal Brain Surgeon, with closed-form greedy updates.
50wZa8inrE.evidence: QuALITY, LongHealth and Long Code Arena across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 4B to 30B parameters at several compaction ratios, against attention matching (Zweiger et al., 2026).
50wZa8inrE.claimed_gains: Gains of up to four accuracy points on question answering at 50x compaction over attention matching at comparable cost, and an advance of the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier at every evaluated compaction ratio.
50wZa8inrE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find compensation-aware selection a well-motivated improvement over independent token ranking, with an elegant closed-form formulation and consistent accuracy-efficiency gains, especially at aggressive compression.
50wZa8inrE.main_concern: The method closely follows the Optimal Brain Surgeon framework on a quadratic surrogate, the link between surrogate and deployed attention-output objective is incompletely characterized, and end-to-end serving costs are not measured.

MJp8XRMciy.one_liner: Open family of autoregressive protein language models (112M-10B), single-sequence and MSA-promptable, aligned with DPO and steered with SMC.
MJp8XRMciy.problem: Generative protein language models are hard to steer toward desired functional families, particularly in low-data regimes.
MJp8XRMciy.method: They release single-sequence and MSA-promptable autoregressive pLMs from 112M to 10B parameters, compare supervised fine-tuning with few-shot prompting using homologous sequences, align models with large-scale direct preference optimization, and add a Feynman-Kac sequential Monte Carlo procedure that steers generation at inference time without updating parameters.
MJp8XRMciy.key_idea: Prompt autoregressive pLMs with homologous sequences instead of fine-tuning, and steer generation with inference-time Feynman-Kac sequential Monte Carlo toward sequence-level objectives.
MJp8XRMciy.evidence: Fine-tuning versus prompting on 25 held-out protein families, a defluorinase enzyme case study from seven starting enzymes with assay validation, DPO alignment, and benchmarks against PoET.
MJp8XRMciy.claimed_gains: Across 25 held-out protein families, prompting outperforms fine-tuning in the low-data regime and matches it as training-set size grows; seven starting enzymes yielded four new defluorinases with activity in line with natural ones.
MJp8XRMciy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the release as a large, carefully tested open-source protein model family with extensive evaluation, including MSA-conditioned prompting beating SFT on small datasets and experimental enzyme validation.
MJp8XRMciy.main_concern: The FK-SMC procedure is not rigorously specified (no target measure, importance weights or resampling are described), and the contribution relative to existing MSA-conditioned models such as PoET is unclear.

gTo8Ypzidv.one_liner: Shows video diffusion degrades with causal-chain length on multi-ball dynamics, helped by serial computation but not extra denoising steps.
gTo8Ypzidv.problem: Video models should predict the consequences of chains of dependent events, but it is unclear whether denoising iterations give video diffusion the serial computation such reasoning and simulation need.
gTo8Ypzidv.method: Controlled multi-ball hard-sphere experiments with length-matched controls lacking ball-ball interactions, intervention studies (autoregressive/blockwise generation, depth, denoising steps) extended to simulator-state prediction and algorithmic tasks, and a proof that denoising steps add no serial computation beyond the backbone for fully observed deterministic prediction with an exact score.
gTo8Ypzidv.key_idea: Denoising steps with an exact score add no serial computation beyond the backbone, so tasks needing growing serial computation need depth or autoregressive serialization.
gTo8Ypzidv.evidence: Controlled hard-sphere dynamics with length-matched controls, interventions across video prediction, simulator-state prediction and algorithmic tasks (e.g., Turmite), three-seed and extractor-sensitivity checks, and a proposition on exact-score denoising.
gTo8Ypzidv.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative degradation with causal-chain length and disproportionate gains from added serial computation; a reviewer cites rollout-5 error falling from 0.883 for bidirectional to 0.607 for autoregressive generation)
gTo8Ypzidv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question sharp and the controlled experiments, which separate dependency depth from video length and visual complexity, clean and robust, with a clear mathematical structure in the theoretical result.
gTo8Ypzidv.main_concern: The testbed is synthetic deterministic hard-sphere dynamics, interventions confound serial computation with other changes (modeling structure, capacity), and the theory assumes full observability, determinism and an exact score.

HyG8Kz813a.one_liner: Budgeted integer weight learning that converts class-discriminative signals into paired zero-sum +1/-1 updates under a write allowance.
HyG8Kz813a.problem: Programmable synaptic devices have bounded conductance range and write endurance, so learning rules must turn desired changes into useful actions within a finite write allowance.
HyG8Kz813a.method: Votes identify coordinates worth modifying and an executor realises them as paired +1/-1 updates, each pair costing two unit writes, with a batch quota and a cumulative ledger controlling modification. Complete-pair commits preserve integer weights, row balance and coordinate bounds, and historical accumulation with execution subtraction carries unspent priorities forward.
HyG8Kz813a.key_idea: Rank coordinates by class-discriminative votes and spend a write budget on paired +1/-1 transfers that keep integer weights and row sums fixed, carrying unspent priorities forward.
HyG8Kz813a.evidence: Formal guarantees for constraint preservation and conditional optimality of update selection, plus experiments with a single linear layer on first-spike latencies on N-MNIST, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 against memory-strategy variants and random-selection baselines.
HyG8Kz813a.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before results; a reviewer cites 88.1-88.9% on MNIST, 76.2-79.3% on Fashion-MNIST and about 16-17% on CIFAR-10)
HyG8Kz813a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning under limited parameter-update capability a meaningful problem and the framework clearly and precisely formalized, with formal constraint-preservation guarantees and controlled multi-dataset comparisons.
HyG8Kz813a.main_concern: Empirical benefit is narrow: all experiments use a single linear layer with low absolute accuracy, the historical-memory gain is task-dependent (intervals include zero, reversed on CIFAR-10), and baselines are mostly internal.

mnYjgnoAqj.one_liner: Post-trains camera-controlled video models with blended global and voxel-localized rewards for long-horizon 3D consistency.
mnYjgnoAqj.problem: Camera-controlled video models lose object permanence and shift scene structure as the camera moves, and post-training with a single scalar reward per generation is poorly suited to correcting this over long horizons.
mnYjgnoAqj.method: LoGo blends a global reward that preserves camera following and video quality with a spatially localized reward that gives fine-grained credit assignment. Reviewers describe the local reward as unprojecting frames with VGGT-omega and computing voxel-level geometry error.
mnYjgnoAqj.key_idea: Assign credit per 3D voxel by unprojecting generated frames and scoring local geometry error, blended with a global reward that keeps camera following and quality.
mnYjgnoAqj.evidence: Three base models on DL3DV and the new TrajectoryBench (long-horizon, complex camera control), against a Global-only run with the same reward model and RL algorithm and against frame-level, patch and window localization ablations.
mnYjgnoAqj.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers in the abstract (it says LoGo shows a clear advantage across three base models and reduces local object shifts, artifacts and global scene changes); a reviewer cites epipolar error 1.381 versus 1.726 for Global-only.
mnYjgnoAqj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find spatial credit assignment a well-motivated, simple response to scalar video rewards, with gains over a matched Global-only baseline on every consistency metric for all three base models.
mnYjgnoAqj.main_concern: Evidence is partly circular and short-horizon: the training reward and most metrics are VGGT-based reprojection scores with no human study, and evaluation covers at most 240 frames despite the long-horizon claim.

MvcB9Q9RUr.one_liner: Perturbs reward-anticipatory units in LLMs and VLMs to induce anhedonia-like effort-based choices without losing task capability.
MvcB9Q9RUr.problem: Whether frontier models mirror human reward valuation is unclear, and causal links between NAc activity and specific behavioral symptoms of anhedonia are hard to establish in humans.
MvcB9Q9RUr.method: They functionally identify reward-anticipatory units in AI models using ideas from neuroscience, test whether those units predict NAc brain recordings, and evaluate causal involvement through targeted perturbations on clinical anhedonia tests and effort-based decision-making paradigms.
MvcB9Q9RUr.key_idea: Localize reward-anticipatory units, then perturb them and measure clinical anhedonia and effort-choice behavior against random-unit and lexical-control perturbations.
MvcB9Q9RUr.evidence: Six models tested with clinical anhedonia measures, effort-based decision paradigms and human fMRI NAc alignment, with controls (forced-choice accuracy, random-unit, mismatched-label, positive reward-free language).
MvcB9Q9RUr.claimed_gains: not stated (results are qualitative: unit perturbation induces low-effort, low-reward choices while preserving task capability and reward calculation)
MvcB9Q9RUr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the study ambitious, with a broad empirical battery (self-reports, behavioral tasks, fMRI alignment) and behavioral controls showing the effect is specific to reward processing without losing task performance.
MvcB9Q9RUr.main_concern: Claims of specificity to human NAc and parallels with human depression are weakly supported (weak neural-alignment evidence, experiments limited to about 8B-scale models, novelty as an interpretability application), and limitations are discussed too briefly.

S4R2zYtFhs.one_liner: Mean-field model of GRPO shows correct-mode entropy collapse as winner-take-all competition and separates solution-family diversity from token entropy.
S4R2zYtFhs.problem: RLVR improves accuracy while concentrating probability on fewer correct solutions, and the mechanism behind this entropy collapse is not characterized.
S4R2zYtFhs.method: They analyze a finite-mode, clean-verifier mean-field model of GRPO, derive exact entropy-mass relations along a scalar trajectory and finite-window accuracy-entropy approximations (shifted-exponential or logistic), and decompose entropy over solution families and token sequences.
S4R2zYtFhs.key_idea: In a mean-field GRPO model, correct-mode dynamics raise collision probability so a unique initial leader captures all correct mass, which differs from token-entropy trends.
S4R2zYtFhs.evidence: Mean-field theory, a GRPO training run comparing unmodified GRPO with an anti-collision variant, and fits to training curves across model families and sizes on math and coding tasks, including a chronological held-out evaluation.
S4R2zYtFhs.claimed_gains: Family-count ratios stay between 4.4 and 5.9 over the tested training cutoffs when comparing unmodified GRPO with an anti-collision variant, whereas token-entropy ratios cross unity.
S4R2zYtFhs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between token entropy and meaningful solution diversity important and thoughtfully developed, with rigorous derivations of Shannon and Renyi-2 entropy dynamics.
S4R2zYtFhs.main_concern: Theory and experiments are weakly connected: the core collision dynamics come from prior work (Rad et al.), late-stage diversity recovery is left unexplained, and experiments use aggregate token entropy rather than the correct-mode entropy the theory predicts.

VpmF3Fi04e.one_liner: Uncertainty-weighted sensitivity regularization reduces one-epoch overfitting in sparse-embedding recommenders by penalizing reliance on uncertain embeddings.
VpmF3Fi04e.problem: Recommendation models with sparse embeddings overfit in a second epoch, lowering training loss while sharply degrading generalization, because replayed examples are scored with embedding rows already displaced by their own labels.
VpmF3Fi04e.method: They name this self-influence asymmetry (a violation of the prequential principle), analyze it with an exact scalar model and local influence analysis, test it with embedding-consumer update-order interventions, and propose UWSR, which penalizes the consumer's sensitivity to uncertain embeddings.
VpmF3Fi04e.key_idea: Penalize the shared consumer's weighted sensitivity to embedding rows in proportion to their uncertainty, removing its incentive to exploit label-induced displacement during replay.
VpmF3Fi04e.evidence: An exact scalar model, local influence analysis, update-order intervention experiments in deep recommendation models, and three benchmarks comparing four-epoch UWSR with one-epoch training.
VpmF3Fi04e.claimed_gains: Across three benchmarks, four-epoch UWSR reduces test cross-entropy by 1.73%-6.78% and improves AUC by 0.0093-0.0231 relative to one-epoch training.
VpmF3Fi04e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the one-epoch problem practically important and the self-influence/prequential explanation, supported by a scalar model and update-order interventions, a meaningful and informative mechanism.
VpmF3Fi04e.main_concern: The mechanism is not shown to be the primary cause of multi-epoch degradation (the theory is a simplified local model and the intervention changes optimization order), and ablations do not show the uncertainty weights beat simpler sensitivity penalties.

mvhAcfA5mF.one_liner: Real-world human-in-the-loop RL for VLA flow policies that learns values from human corrections and updates via adjoint value-gradient propagation.
mvhAcfA5mF.problem: Human interventions in real-world VLA adaptation must support informative value learning and then be translated into effective updates of the VLA's multi-step flow policy.
mvhAcfA5mF.method: CAPO couples Corrective Value Learning, which learns action values from the observed outcomes of human corrections and compares them against rejected policy proposals, with Adjoint-based Policy Optimization, which propagates action-value gradients along the VLA's native flow trajectories into local policy updates while preserving the deployment sampler.
mvhAcfA5mF.key_idea: Propagate critic action-value gradients along the VLA's flow trajectory with adjoint matching to form local updates, while the critic learns from human corrections versus rejected actions.
mvhAcfA5mF.evidence: Six real-world manipulation tasks against evaluated HiL-RL methods, with ablations on critic ranking, corrective behavior cloning, gradient validity, reference-policy refreshing and computational cost.
mvhAcfA5mF.claimed_gains: Across six real-world manipulation tasks, CAPO achieves the highest mean autonomous success of 93.3% and the lowest intervention rate among the evaluated methods.
mvhAcfA5mF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the setting well motivated and the use of corrections for both value learning and policy optimization well justified, with comprehensive experiments including critic ranking, gradient validity and compute cost.
mvhAcfA5mF.main_concern: Actor comparisons may be confounded by unequal corrective behavior cloning, novelty over prior methods is questioned, and the approach assumes human corrections beat rejected actions with evaluation limited to a few tasks.

YESnLwnbDF.one_liner: Proves routing predictors' gain over self-confidence is bounded by model suboptimality plus added-parameter gain
YESnLwnbDF.problem: Routing methods train separate performance predictors for candidate LLMs without comparing against the model's own self-confidence, so it is unclear when prediction adds anything.
YESnLwnbDF.method: Takes the probability a model assigns to its chosen answer as a baseline and shows any predictor beating it can be converted into a lower-loss model through recalibration. Bounds the predictor's advantage by the model's suboptimality plus the gain from extra parameters, and extends the results to two-model cascades.
YESnLwnbDF.key_idea: A predictor's advantage over self-confidence transfers exactly in log loss through recalibration, so it is bounded by the model's suboptimality plus a parameter-capacity term.
YESnLwnbDF.evidence: Propositions and theorems on log-loss transfer and capacity bounds, a two-model cascade extension, and experiments with 16 language models on four benchmarks.
YESnLwnbDF.claimed_gains: No numeric gains stated; reports that predictors gain a larger advantage over self-confidence on more suboptimal models (16 models, four benchmarks).
YESnLwnbDF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear and correct link between correctness prediction and answer loss, and experiments that retrain predictors with predictor-size and Platt-calibration controls.
YESnLwnbDF.main_concern: Reviewers call the theory limited or near-tautological, with an unobservable capacity floor and a bound that may carry little quantitative information.

XXce8BsDpV.one_liner: RL framework training spreadsheet agents in a real Excel gym with an asynchronous verifier and auto-collected tasks
XXce8BsDpV.problem: Spreadsheet agents mostly prompt general-purpose LLMs, which struggle with the multi-step workflows that dominate real-world spreadsheet use.
XXce8BsDpV.method: An automated data agent collects paired initial-final spreadsheets from online forums, and Spreadsheet Gym provides a multi-turn Microsoft Excel environment with a spreadsheet-native tool harness and an asynchronous Excel-based verifier. Agents are post-trained with RL, and Domain-Spreadsheet adds a benchmark of 1,660 professional tasks.
XXce8BsDpV.key_idea: Train agents with outcome-based RL in a real Microsoft Excel environment whose asynchronous verifier recalculates workbooks and compares cells against forum-derived oracle final workbooks.
XXce8BsDpV.evidence: SpreadsheetBench and Domain-Spreadsheet results on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Qwen3-8B, a human audit of 100 training and 100 Domain-Spreadsheet tasks, and trajectory analysis.
XXce8BsDpV.claimed_gains: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 rises from 12.0% to 23.4% Pass@1 on SpreadsheetBench, Qwen3-8B from 16.8% to 22.3%, and Domain-Spreadsheet from 8.4% to 17.2%; the audit finds majority-valid oracles for 84% and 98% of tasks.
XXce8BsDpV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the real-Excel gym, asynchronous verifier and automated task pipeline address substantive obstacles to RL training of spreadsheet agents.
XXce8BsDpV.main_concern: Automatically built oracles are noisy (only 84% of audited training tasks majority-valid) and the exact-match evaluation contract is described inconsistently across the paper.

cYSCWzF31p.one_liner: Feeds the previous token's cached middle-layer hidden state into an earlier layer of the current token
cYSCWzF31p.problem: Autoregressive decoding compresses rich hidden computation through token space, so intermediate reasoning states cannot persist across decoding steps.
cYSCWzF31p.method: T2MLR fuses a cached middle-layer representation from the previous token into an earlier layer at the current position, keeping one forward pass per token. Recurrence can cover only a middle block (as little as 20% of the network) and can be retrofitted into a pretrained 1.7B Transformer with brief finetuning.
cYSCWzF31p.key_idea: A deep-to-shallow recurrent connection carries the previous token's middle-layer state into an earlier layer of the current token, so abstract intermediate computation persists across decoding steps.
cYSCWzF31p.evidence: Natural-language pretraining and multi-hop reasoning finetuning against data- and parameter-matched Transformers, scaling to 1B parameters or 50B tokens, and a retrofit of a pretrained 1.7B Transformer on math reasoning; reviewers also cite an S5-Retrieval state-tracking test.
cYSCWzF31p.claimed_gains: Outperforms data- and parameter-matched Transformer baselines in every tested setting, with gains persisting at 1B parameters or 50B pretraining tokens; no numeric figures stated in the abstract.
cYSCWzF31p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is a simple, clearly presented modification that keeps the standard Transformer backbone with little decoding overhead, and two cite consistent gains across retrieval, pretraining and retrofitting.
cYSCWzF31p.main_concern: Training is roughly 2-4x slower and prefill is costly, and at equal wall-clock a plain Transformer scores higher (45.30 vs 44.14 zero-shot average in Table 11).

KHY335oIIt.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,604 questions over 24 long case files testing agent memory on invalidation propagation, source conflicts, and counterfactuals.
KHY335oIIt.problem: Existing memory benchmarks test whether agents retrieve scattered facts or detect that a fact changed, not whether they trace which downstream conclusions are affected by the change.
KHY335oIIt.method: RECON provides 24 case files (criminal, medical, financial; 50k to 100k tokens) with six memory-intensive tasks, where gold answers are derived in code from a provenance DAG and an LLM only narrates the constrained surface text.
KHY335oIIt.key_idea: Build the evidence skeleton and provenance graph first, derive gold answers from it in code, and only then narrate it, so questions test downstream propagation of changes.
KHY335oIIt.evidence: Evaluation of current memory architectures (long-context, retrieval, and a structured-graph control) on 24 case files in three domains; reviews mention a 200-question human audit.
KHY335oIIt.claimed_gains: The strongest non-Oracle system reaches only 22.4% accuracy, and no system other than the structured-graph control exceeds it.
KHY335oIIt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that focusing on how revised evidence affects downstream conclusions is useful and that building evidence graphs and answer keys before generating prose is a sound design.
KHY335oIIt.main_concern: Each task has precedents in existing benchmarks, the three similar investigation domains limit broader relevance, and label reliability is uncertain (8 gold answers contradicted and 19 unsure in a 200-question audit).

hIlMyk3zQw.one_liner: Evaluates VMamba as the vision encoder in VLMs across four pretraining setups and studies connector depth and normalization.
hIlMyk3zQw.problem: Transformer vision encoders are the standard in VLMs, and it is unclear whether state-space models are a viable alternative.
hIlMyk3zQw.method: They evaluate VMamba under a shared downstream VLM recipe across contrastive, classification, detection-adaptation, and segmentation-adaptation pretraining, then vary the connector with a pre-connector normalization layer and MLP depth, using representation probes.
hIlMyk3zQw.key_idea: Compare SSM and Transformer encoders under matched VLM recipes per pretraining setting and treat the vision-language connector (normalization, depth) as a controlled variable.
hIlMyk3zQw.evidence: Four pretraining setups with 13 benchmark scores across VQA and referring-expression tasks per reviews, plus connector ablations and representation probes.
hIlMyk3zQw.claimed_gains: Models are generally competitive across VQA and referring-expression benchmarks with the most consistent gains on grounding, and a normalization layer before the connector can substantially improve VLM performance; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
hIlMyk3zQw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the comparison across four pretraining regimes is broad and relatively controlled, the question is practically relevant since most VLMs still use ViT encoders, and grounding gains are fairly consistent.
hIlMyk3zQw.main_concern: The findings are not new or actionable and encoder effects are confounded (contrastive checkpoints differ in initialization, text encoder, and schedule, only VMamba is tested, and prior work on SSM vision encoders is not discussed).

bstvvfFV4y.one_liner: Sparse zeroth-order fine-tuning of BitNet that updates only latent weights near ternary quantizer boundaries.
bstvvfFV4y.problem: For BitNet, MeZO must update full-precision latent weights so its memory no longer matches inference, and existing sparse ZO methods either ignore the ternary structure or need first-order gradients to build a mask.
bstvvfFV4y.method: TerMeZO uses the geometry of the ternary quantizer to pick the latent weights most likely to change quantized value during fine-tuning, at no extra data or memory cost, and runs sparse MeZO on that subset. A convergence analysis argues the reduced effective dimension can converge faster than full-parameter MeZO.
bstvvfFV4y.key_idea: Mask latent weights by proximity to ternary quantization boundaries, since those flip quantized values most easily under perturbation, then run MeZO on the masked subset.
bstvvfFV4y.evidence: Convergence analysis plus experiments on BitNet models from 1B to 3B parameters across classification, instruction-following and mathematical reasoning tasks; the abstract says it matches or exceeds full-parameter MeZO.
bstvvfFV4y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, quantizer-grounded selection criterion that needs no gradients or extra data, and the competitive performance with substantially lower memory than full-parameter MeZO.
bstvvfFV4y.main_concern: Evidence gaps: no ablation of the fixed 0.05 selection fraction, no empirical convergence curves or edge-hardware latency results, and weights frozen once are never reactivated.

o4nvaYybuu.one_liner: Stabilizes primal-dual constrained MARL by pulling each policy toward a slowly moving copy of itself.
o4nvaYybuu.problem: At binding cost budgets, the policy and Lagrange multiplier in primal-dual multi-agent RL can cycle and deep training can collapse.
o4nvaYybuu.method: They add an anchored policy regularizer that pulls each policy toward a slow copy of itself, and prove in the tabular robust constrained Markov game that the weaker equilibrium notion behind their multiplier update exists under robust Slater.
o4nvaYybuu.key_idea: Add a regularizer toward a slowly updated copy of each agent's policy to damp policy-multiplier cycling under binding cost budgets.
o4nvaYybuu.evidence: Cooperative navigation at tight budgets and a pursuit-evasion task, with a bounded action-perturbing adversary retrained against each final policy and a navigation budget grid, plus theory in the tabular robust constrained Markov game.
o4nvaYybuu.claimed_gains: The anchor removes the collapse and lifts the goal rate above every constrained variant without it, and meets every budget pair of a navigation grid without per-pair tuning; numeric goal rates are not stated in the abstract.
o4nvaYybuu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the anchor substantially improves training stability and task success at tight budgets, supported by well-controlled ablations against unanchored, PID-based, and adversarially trained variants.
o4nvaYybuu.main_concern: The benefit does not transfer broadly: the anchor helps mainly on navigation and pursuit-evasion, does not reproduce gains in the official MAPPO-Lagrangian code, and is justified only by a toy bilinear model.

tTKdR2Z4WB.one_liner: GITA conditions a value function on abstraction factor k and aggregates advantage-weighted supervision across several k for offline goal-conditioned RL.
tTKdR2Z4WB.problem: Offline goal-conditioned RL struggles on long horizons because discounting shrinks value differences between distant states, and no single temporal-abstraction k suits all state-goal distances.
tTKdR2Z4WB.method: GITA conditions a single value function on k and trains one policy by aggregating advantage-weighted supervision across several k values, so scales assigning larger positive advantages to a state-goal pair contribute more to its update.
tTKdR2Z4WB.key_idea: Condition one value function on the abstraction factor k and weight policy supervision by each scale's advantage, implicitly selecting the scale per state-goal pair.
tTKdR2Z4WB.evidence: OGBench against a broad range of offline GCRL baselines, including HIQL and OTA.
tTKdR2Z4WB.claimed_gains: Raises average success rate across all tasks by 25 percentage points (73% relative improvement) over HIQL, and improves over the strongest fixed-k method OTA by 7 percentage points (14% relative).
tTKdR2Z4WB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is well grounded (a fixed k trades long-range value propagation against local resolution) and that conditioning on k with advantage aggregation is a simple fix with the largest gains on hard long-distance tasks.
tTKdR2Z4WB.main_concern: Results are mixed across tasks (OTA, GCIQL, or CRL win on some), and the method still needs per-task tuning of the discount factor gamma with high sensitivity, shifting tuning from k to gamma.

J3L4S6pRX5.one_liner: HeteroNet models irregular multivariate time series with observation encoding, sparse pattern tokens, pattern interaction, and kernel fusion.
J3L4S6pRX5.problem: Time series pattern machines target regularly sampled data, whereas irregular multivariate time series have uneven intervals and asynchronous variates that require heterogeneous pattern representations.
J3L4S6pRX5.method: HeteroNet combines Observation Encoding, Sparse Pattern Tokenization (recent states, changes over elapsed intervals, variate histories), Pattern Interaction within and across asynchronous variates, and Kernel Fusion of the resulting representations.
J3L4S6pRX5.key_idea: Tokenize each irregular series into separate state, interval-change, and variate-history tokens, then model their interactions within and across asynchronous variates.
J3L4S6pRX5.evidence: Per reviews, 15 datasets, five tasks, and 40 baselines with standard deviations for most tasks; the abstract is cut off before the results.
J3L4S6pRX5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically relevant, the representation design clear, and the evaluation broad across tasks, datasets, and baselines.
J3L4S6pRX5.main_concern: The incremental value of the heterogeneous tokens and branches is weakly shown (small ablation changes), and the unified-model and 'pattern machine' framing is questioned.

ZDxdyHapf7.one_liner: Small-VLM risk forecasts decide when to warn and when to verify in streaming video, enabling pre-incident warnings.
ZDxdyHapf7.problem: Warning methods that confirm a hazard once visible use up the time left to warn, and serial confirmation filters out early candidates or returns too late.
ZDxdyHapf7.method: The same risk read at two horizons drives an immediate path that does not wait for a verifier and an advisory path combining predicted risk with a returned state judgment; a risk-dependent schedule decides when to query the verifier, and thresholds are calibrated on normal footage per deployment.
ZDxdyHapf7.key_idea: Predicted near-future risk gates both the warning path (immediate versus advisory) and the verifier query schedule, so forecasts act before confirmation where time is short.
ZDxdyHapf7.evidence: Five public domains, self-recorded live trials, and three Jetson edge devices against four recent baselines, plus a one-step analysis of verification value.
ZDxdyHapf7.claimed_gains: Raises macro pre-incident recall from 0.473 for the strongest of four recent baselines to 0.670 with a similar number of verifier calls.
ZDxdyHapf7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of fast risk forecasting from slower verification, with an immediate path that bypasses verification, a meaningful and well-motivated design for a practical problem.
ZDxdyHapf7.main_concern: Higher recall comes with a false-alarm burden (balanced accuracy falls below 0.5 on some domains such as OCCU), and ablations and novelty relative to fast-slow cascades are insufficient.

uxzUGKp7kL.one_liner: Extends normal-form analysis of large-step gradient descent to vector-valued least squares and manifolds of flat minima.
uxzUGKp7kL.problem: Classical GD analysis requires a step size below twice the reciprocal sharpness, which deep networks often violate, and prior large-step theory covers only scalar-output least squares near an isolated flat minimum.
uxzUGKp7kL.method: They generalize the normal form and all three convergence theorems of prior work to overparametrised least squares with vector-valued outputs and to a neighbourhood of a manifold of flat minima. They apply the framework to deep matrix factorisation, showing the flat minima form a fibre bundle over a product of spheres and that sharpness is Morse-Bott along it.
uxzUGKp7kL.key_idea: Reduce large-step GD near a manifold of flat minima to a normal form that separates tangential dynamics along the manifold from normal-direction dynamics.
uxzUGKp7kL.evidence: Theorems for vector-valued least squares and manifolds of flat minima, a deep matrix factorisation application, and small three-layer 2x2 factorisation trajectory plots mentioned in reviews.
uxzUGKp7kL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending the analysis to vector-valued outputs and manifolds of flat minima is a substantial, rigorous generalization of prior work.
uxzUGKp7kL.main_concern: The geometric assumptions (for example Assumptions 3.4 and 3.5) are restrictive and hard to verify beyond matrix factorisation, and the experiments are small.

It5i9DvZA1.one_liner: Models talking-face affect jointly across expressions, action units, and valence-arousal with a probabilistic atlas and differentiable rules.
It5i9DvZA1.problem: Audio-driven talking-face methods treat emotion as a weak or isolated conditioning signal, giving faces that look plausible but are affectively inconsistent with speech.
It5i9DvZA1.method: AffectAtlas builds a probabilistic affect atlas capturing bidirectional relations among expressions, action units, and valence-arousal, adapts it to talking-face data with teacher-guided adaptation, and enforces consistency with differentiable neuro-symbolic rules. The refined representations condition a diffusion-based generator through an emotion-aware A/V module.
It5i9DvZA1.key_idea: A probabilistic atlas links expression, action-unit, and valence-arousal spaces, adapted by teachers and constrained by differentiable symbolic rules before conditioning a diffusion generator.
It5i9DvZA1.evidence: Quantitative, qualitative, cross-dataset, ablation, and user-study evaluations; reviews cite RAVDESS and VFHQ transfer plus MEAD and HDTF.
It5i9DvZA1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports better emotion fidelity, temporal affect alignment, visual quality, and realism than SOTA methods, without numbers)
It5i9DvZA1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling relations among expression, action-unit, and valence-arousal spaces addresses a real limitation of single-space emotion conditioning, with cross-dataset transfer and human evaluations.
It5i9DvZA1.main_concern: The validity of the structured affect modeling is insufficiently established (atlas construction details, teacher consistency, rule satisfaction measured on the trained rules) and component contributions are not separately ablated.

7DFQWXfKWf.one_liner: On-policy distillation that diagnoses a student's first uncorrected error with a frozen teacher and concentrates supervision around it.
7DFQWXfKWf.problem: In on-policy distillation of failed math reasoning, it is unclear where teacher supervision should go, and teacher-student disagreement need not identify the real error.
7DFQWXfKWf.method: SELD uses a frozen teacher and a reference solution to diagnose the first error, emphasizes that step and its predecessor, retains sparse earlier-prefix supervision, allocates nonuniform weights within these regions, and excludes the later continuation.
7DFQWXfKWf.key_idea: Locate the first uncorrected error semantically with a teacher and reference solution, then weight distillation loss on that step, its predecessor, and a sparse earlier prefix only.
7DFQWXfKWf.evidence: A controlled placement study of supervision windows, 159 expert-annotated incorrect solutions for localization, four math benchmarks with three seeds on Qwen3-1.7B, a larger student, a smaller teacher, and repeated ablations.
7DFQWXfKWf.claimed_gains: Semantic diagnosis raises first-error coverage from 44.7% to 67.9% over maximum-disagreement anchors, and SELD improves Qwen3-1.7B macro-average response accuracy by 2.54 percentage points over full-token OPD.
7DFQWXfKWf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-error localization idea is concrete and well controlled, with error-centered windows beating other placements and gains over full-token OPD holding across seeds.
7DFQWXfKWf.main_concern: SELD needs complete reference solutions, its first-error localization is imperfect (51.6% exact, 67.9% coverage), and gains over stronger weighted-OPD baselines are modest.

bEverDN9Zm.one_liner: Graph world model combining a state-aware graph transformer with transition-aware GRPO, evaluated on the new GWM-Zero benchmark.
bEverDN9Zm.problem: Prior graph-related world models use graph structure to organize internal states or support task-specific reasoning, rather than treating the evolving graph itself as the modeled world.
bEverDN9Zm.method: Formulates graph world modeling over observed graph evolution, latent graph states and heterogeneous transition predictions, builds GWM-Zero covering node-, edge- and graph-level transitions over eight temporal graph datasets, and proposes WorldGraph: a state-aware graph transformer plus transition-aware GRPO with dynamic grouping and structure-aware verifiable rewards.
bEverDN9Zm.key_idea: Model graph evolution itself as the world dynamics with a state-aware graph transformer trained by GRPO with dynamic grouping and structure-aware verifiable rewards.
bEverDN9Zm.evidence: GWM-Zero over eight temporal graph datasets against baselines from graph representation, temporal graph learning, graph pretraining and graph world-model families.
bEverDN9Zm.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms representative baselines across all three transition granularities (node, edge, graph); no numbers are stated.
bEverDN9Zm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating node-, edge- and graph-level transitions in one benchmark is a useful framing and that the method outperforms the compared baselines.
bEverDN9Zm.main_concern: The theorems are near-vacuous or inconsistent with the method's own equations, and part of the benchmark's change labels are synthetically constructed.

sIJzfux1bC.one_liner: Flow-matching time-series model generating whole future paths, distilled to one or two steps with a shared history attention cache.
sIJzfux1bC.problem: Most time-series foundation models predict marginal quantiles and leave the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified, which matters for cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing.
sIJzfux1bC.method: PathFM uses flow matching to generate complete multivariate future paths, distills the model to one or two steps, and shares a history attention cache across draws, which also makes direct optimization of a calibration loss practical. They also introduce fps-bench, which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics.
sIJzfux1bC.key_idea: Distilled flow matching samples full joint trajectories in one or two steps with a shared history attention cache, making path-level calibration training practical.
sIJzfux1bC.evidence: Marginal accuracy on fev-bench and TIME, path scores on the new fps-bench, and chaotic-system experiments on long-run variability.
sIJzfux1bC.claimed_gains: PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on fev-bench and TIME and the highest aggregate path score on fps-bench among the evaluated models, generating multiple paths in roughly the time of one quantile-model query.
sIJzfux1bC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating joint path quality beyond marginals fills a real gap, and that flow matching is a well-motivated way to sample the joint future distribution with competitive marginal accuracy.
sIJzfux1bC.main_concern: The fps-bench margin may be overstated (it shrinks to about 2.5% once a baseline gets a cheap copula) and the training data and code are insufficiently documented.

AYYuAnCmP7.one_liner: Derives a closed-form tilted-temperature decoding rule that maximizes pass@k under entropy-floor and cross-entropy-ceiling constraints.
AYYuAnCmP7.problem: There is no formal account of what objective temperature tuning optimizes, even though larger sample budgets are known to benefit from higher sampling temperatures.
AYYuAnCmP7.method: They pose decoding as pass@k maximization with an entropy floor and a cross-entropy ceiling and prove the optimum is a tilted temperature rule, q* proportional to (p * exp(eta * V))^(1/T), where V is a verifier potential. The online J-EOS algorithm tracks the two constraint multipliers and learns V from binary pass/fail feedback, and an offline design is given for calibrated models.
AYYuAnCmP7.key_idea: Constrained pass@k maximization yields temperature sampling tilted by a verifier potential V, with the optimal temperature increasing with the sample budget k.
AYYuAnCmP7.evidence: Proofs of the closed-form rule and temperature scaling, the online J-EOS algorithm, an offline calibration reduction, and code-generation experiments that reviewers describe on HumanEval and MBPP.
AYYuAnCmP7.claimed_gains: not stated (theoretical result: under a natural diversity-budget rule the optimal temperature increases with k).
AYYuAnCmP7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and gives a mathematically sound framework linking sequence-level success to token-level decoding.
AYYuAnCmP7.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the tilt and use baselines below published numbers, while the theory resembles known entropy-regularized RL results and k does not enter the optimization.

kGpJLamtoZ.one_liner: Streaming non-autoregressive video captioning with two yoked closed-form schedules: a monotone text frontier and a matching source horizon.
kGpJLamtoZ.problem: Autoregressive captioners can stream but need one sequential pass per token, while non-autoregressive ones are faster but cannot stream because no prefix is final until the last pass.
kGpJLamtoZ.method: ViNAYA fixes a monotone text frontier that commits and emits spans left to right and a yoked monotone source horizon that reveals the clip at a matching pace, both closed-form and set before decoding. A ratio nu joins the two knobs and yields an exposure budget of 1/(1+nu).
kGpJLamtoZ.key_idea: Declared closed-form text and source schedules, joined by a ratio nu, make every emitted span final and causal on arrived video, with predictable exposure 1/(1+nu).
kGpJLamtoZ.evidence: Three video captioning corpora with three frozen encoders, compared with AR and blockwise NAR baselines (including an author-built BD3-LM) on quality, latency, and inference efficiency.
kGpJLamtoZ.claimed_gains: ViNAYA reduces Average Lagging by 43 to 50 percent against the strongest NAR streaming baseline while holding quality.
kGpJLamtoZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, the yoked schedules give clear causality and prefix-finality guarantees, and experiments on three datasets show consistent latency gains.
kGpJLamtoZ.main_concern: The schedules are content-agnostic and fixed from corpus statistics, the latency gain may come from a fixed pass budget, and the setup may use annotated segment lengths unavailable in true streaming.

N6bS03pkah.one_liner: Compresses expert-parallel MoE communication by sending only compressed differences from a periodically refreshed earlier-layer reference hidden state.
N6bS03pkah.problem: The synchronous dispatch and combine collectives in expert parallelism have become a bottleneck for MoE inference as compute throughput outpaces interconnect bandwidth.
N6bS03pkah.method: EchoMoE is a lightweight architecture change that retrofits existing MoE models, requiring about 8500 times fewer training tokens than full pretraining. It uses a hidden state from an earlier layer as a reference, refreshes it periodically, and communicates only the compressed difference to the current state.
N6bS03pkah.key_idea: Exploit the incremental update of the residual stream by communicating compressed differences against a periodically refreshed earlier-layer reference instead of full hidden states.
N6bS03pkah.evidence: Quality results on an adapted Qwen3-30B-A3B checkpoint with ablations against plain compression, plus system-level throughput and communication measurements (larger models tested with random weights for runtime only).
N6bS03pkah.claimed_gains: EchoMoE reduces inter-node communication volume by 58% and improves throughput by 22.6%.
N6bS03pkah.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-layer references improve the quality-communication trade-off over plain activation compression, with a concrete implementation and useful ablations.
N6bS03pkah.main_concern: The practical benefit is uncertain because decode gains are limited, reference-transfer overhead offsets savings, an optimized FP8 communication baseline is missing, and quality is shown on one pretrained checkpoint.

G54coMSTRj.one_liner: Selected query-key relations in pretrained ViTs separate same-category object instances through shared, movable attention addresses.
G54coMSTRj.problem: How native self-attention keeps object instances separate in pretrained Vision Transformers is unresolved.
G54coMSTRj.method: Across eight pretrained ViTs, they compare query-key relations against value similarity and residual representations for instance separation, define an attention address (the common region that one object's patches read from in a head), and edit the query component at a selected head to redirect that address.
G54coMSTRj.key_idea: Instance identity lives in attention routing: patches of one object share an attention address set by the query's interaction with the spatial structure of keys.
G54coMSTRj.evidence: Eight pretrained ViTs, a controlled patch-pair test, editing the query component at a selected head, and instance clustering scored by FG-ARI (abstract cut off).
G54coMSTRj.claimed_gains: Grouping patches by the query component reaches .615 FG-ARI versus .289 for the same clustering of a comparison representation (abstract cut off).
G54coMSTRj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a fundamental question with abundant experiments across eight ViTs and that finding instance separation in attention routing rather than token content is interesting.
G54coMSTRj.main_concern: The causal claim is weak: redirecting one head's attention address does not show the mechanism is responsible for object binding in the full network, and the routing-versus-content comparison relies on cosine-similarity readouts.

UAinvs2t8U.one_liner: DM-OPD distills autoregressive teachers into diffusion language models by matching completed-text distributions with an unbiased on-policy block-KL gradient.
UAinvs2t8U.problem: AR-to-diffusion conversion methods fit intermediate predictions, but a better fit does not necessarily improve the distribution of the text the student generates.
UAinvs2t8U.method: DM-OPD defines distillation on the text distribution induced by the student's actual decoder and derives an on-policy gradient estimator for each completed-block KL at student-generated prefixes. It makes this trainable by estimating student text likelihoods, decomposing feedback into dependency-based action credit, and defining probabilities for refinement decisions.
UAinvs2t8U.key_idea: Distill on the decoder-induced completed-text distribution using a per-block KL gradient at student-generated prefixes, instead of matching intermediate token predictions.
UAinvs2t8U.evidence: Qwen3 initialization and teacher checkpoints with OPDLM's prompt corpus, 4B students against SDAR and OPDLM on eight benchmarks at 4K and 8K response limits, and a matched-compute controlled comparison with token distillation.
UAinvs2t8U.claimed_gains: 4B students outperform SDAR in thinking evaluation and OPDLM in non-thinking evaluation across all eight benchmarks, and the objective improves 4K macro accuracy by 11.0 points over OPDLM-style token distillation at matched training compute.
UAinvs2t8U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of the objective mismatch in diffusion-LM distillation is principled and well motivated, with a formal treatment and large gains over other diffusion conversions.
UAinvs2t8U.main_concern: The gains are confounded and parallelism is unproven: the main comparison differs from baselines in decoder and thinking-mode training, and the best setting uses block size 4 with 1.0 tokens per forward and about twice the AR latency.

1nI6TTfmLu.one_liner: Adaptive nonstationary bandit algorithm exploiting known arm classes with separate change budgets, with matching lower bounds.
1nI6TTfmLu.problem: Existing nonstationary bandit algorithms ignore heterogeneous volatility across arms, so regret scales with the global product of total arms and total switches.
1nI6TTfmLu.method: The authors formulate K arms partitioned into M known classes of sizes K_m with individual change budgets L_m, and design an adaptive algorithm that needs no prior knowledge of these budgets. They also prove complementary lower bounds.
1nI6TTfmLu.key_idea: Detect changes and restart locally within each arm class so that each class's volatility is paired only with its own size, without knowing change budgets.
1nI6TTfmLu.evidence: Theoretical analysis only: a dynamic regret upper bound and lower bounds; reviewers note the absence of empirical evidence.
1nI6TTfmLu.claimed_gains: Expected dynamic regret of order sqrt(M T sum_m (L_m+1) K_m), optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed M, with the sqrt(M) class-search overhead unavoidable in general.
1nI6TTfmLu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the class-structured model is a well-motivated refinement of the switching-budget formulation, with thorough, well-written theory and a direct-sum lower bound.
1nI6TTfmLu.main_concern: The relationship to AdSwitch and GLR-klUCB (local restarts, multi-scale monitoring) is insufficiently discussed, and the algorithm is computationally impractical with no empirical evidence.

CSZN8xOTjX.one_liner: Augments the environment graph with agent-plan nodes linked to resource nodes, enabling message-passing coordination in dynamic multi-agent combinatorial optimization.
CSZN8xOTjX.problem: Existing multi-agent neural combinatorial optimization assumes all instance information is known upfront, so it fails to coordinate agents when information is revealed progressively during execution.
CSZN8xOTjX.method: PACT adds auxiliary nodes representing agents' plans to the environment graph, connected to resource nodes to indicate future dependencies. Message passing over this augmented graph grounds inter-agent coordination in the environment and enables proactive rather than reactive conflict resolution.
CSZN8xOTjX.key_idea: Mediate coordination through plan nodes attached to demanded resources, so conflicts are resolved by aggregating plan load against remaining capacity rather than through pairwise agent interactions.
CSZN8xOTjX.evidence: Dynamic routing and scheduling problems compared with learning-based baselines such as MAPPO, evaluated with best-of-128 sampling against hindsight oracles and on transfer to larger instances.
CSZN8xOTjX.claimed_gains: With best-of-128 sampling PACT approaches the cost of hindsight oracles on small instances, and it has the best transfer to larger instances among the learning-based baselines.
CSZN8xOTjX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the plan-and-resource graph representation is a clear, reusable coordination mechanism for routing and scheduling that improves solution quality, including under single-run greedy evaluation.
CSZN8xOTjX.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate whether resource-mediated, multi-step plan coordination drives the gains, and best-of-128 reporting and the 'dynamic' framing (essentially partial observability) are questioned.

L6sLS9pn9b.one_liner: Hybrid quantum-classical EEG decoder where component i sets qubit i's rotation and Riemannian relation (i,j) conditions qubit-pair interaction.
L6sLS9pn9b.problem: Cross-patient ALS EEG decoding must learn from small clinical cohorts, but deep encoders and Riemannian or graph methods are compressed or aggregated without preserving component-wise correspondence.
L6sLS9pn9b.method: QRG-EEG preserves component identity across deep, graph, and quantum representations: local evidence from component i controls a single-qubit operation on qubit i, while its Riemannian relation (i, j) directly conditions the interaction between qubits (i, j). The authors analytically show how this edge conditioning becomes observable and induces a joint node-node-edge response.
L6sLS9pn9b.key_idea: Map each EEG component to a qubit with evidence-driven rotations, and let pairwise Riemannian relations set the interaction angles between the corresponding qubits.
L6sLS9pn9b.evidence: Four public ALS-EEG datasets with 30 patient-level LOSO folds, strict source-only selection, matched classical and quantum controls, and targeted edge interventions (exact statevector simulation per reviews).
L6sLS9pn9b.claimed_gains: Achieves the strongest dataset-level Macro-F1, with secondary metrics (AUROC for P300, balanced accuracy for MI), on three of the four datasets.
L6sLS9pn9b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the component-aligned node-edge conditioning is clearly formulated and analytically supported, and that LOSO evaluation with source-only selection, classical and quantum baselines, and ablations is relatively comprehensive.
L6sLS9pn9b.main_concern: The benefit of quantum interactions over equally expressive classical node-edge models is not established, and results rest on small datasets (6-8 subjects each) evaluated with exact simulation.

RJ4eHLjXTf.one_liner: Builds zero-shot-coordination training populations of socializer, achiever, and explorer agents via three lightweight objective modifications from Bartle's taxonomy.
RJ4eHLjXTf.problem: Population-based zero-shot cooperation needs training populations that capture the structured diversity of human behavior rather than undirected diversity.
RJ4eHLjXTf.method: TEAM induces trait-based behaviors inspired by Bartle's taxonomy through three lightweight modifications to the learning objectives (an empowerment bonus, reward reallocation, and an entropy coefficient per reviews), without task-specific reward modifications. The authors also formalize ZSC as training on a set of MDPs with a new MDP sampled at test time.
RJ4eHLjXTf.key_idea: Induce socializer, achiever, and explorer traits by modifying the learning objective, then train the ego agent against this human-inspired, focused-coverage population.
RJ4eHLjXTf.evidence: AI-AI and real-human tests on Overcooked and StarCraft, plus SMAC, Coin Game, and a 32-participant Overcooked human study per reviews, with an empirical space-coverage study.
RJ4eHLjXTf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is well motivated, lightweight, interpretable and controllable, and evaluated broadly across Overcooked, SMAC, and Coin Game.
RJ4eHLjXTf.main_concern: Novelty over FCP, MEP, HSP and related heterogeneous-partner methods is limited, and generalization beyond game environments and a small Overcooked human study is unclear.

pjlDwz7qGF.one_liner: Averages forecasts from input views that beat the raw context in rolling-origin backtests, a causal verifier for time series models.
pjlDwz7qGF.problem: Test-time compute recipes from language models do not transfer to forecasting because a forecaster is causal and cannot use future information to score candidates.
pjlDwz7qGF.method: Backtest-Gated Augmentation Averaging scores structured views of the context with rolling-origin backtests on the series' own history, discards views that underperform the untransformed context, and averages the survivors' predictive distributions.
pjlDwz7qGF.key_idea: Build a verifier from the series' own past by backtesting transformed contexts, keep only views that beat the untransformed one, and average their predictive distributions.
pjlDwz7qGF.evidence: Tested TSFM-benchmark combinations on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench, and BOOM, plus an analysis of view selection on 53 cross-fittable GIFT-Eval configs; reviews cite random-view, jitter, ungated-ensemble, and restricted-pool controls.
pjlDwz7qGF.claimed_gains: Reduces MASE by 0.5-1.0% on GIFT-Eval, 1.3-5.0% on fev-bench, and 1.7-5.9% on BOOM, where a 313M model with TTC outperforms the 1B and 2.5B models in its family.
pjlDwz7qGF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method carefully causal and leak-free, and the improvements consistent across all model-benchmark combinations, with controls showing gains come from informative views rather than extra forecasts.
pjlDwz7qGF.main_concern: The gains are small relative to cost (about 7.9-9.4 times baseline compute for roughly 0.5-1.1% MASE on GIFT-Eval), with no latency measurements or comparison with other test-time compute methods.

1DHx7yOj3u.one_liner: Argues LLM evaluation should be temporal, forecasting future model performance from time-stamped historical benchmark scores with time-series forecasters.
1DHx7yOj3u.problem: Random train-test splits assume IID data, but text distributions shift continuously over time and models are deployed on future data.
1DHx7yOj3u.method: Shows web text is non-stationary, that shifts are temporally local and model performance changes continuously across benchmarks, then predicts future performance from recent evaluation data and from time-series forecasters applied to historic performance, using forecasts for model selection.
1DHx7yOj3u.key_idea: Treat time as an evaluation variable: forecast a model's future score from its historical time-ordered performance instead of using static or historic scores directly.
1DHx7yOj3u.evidence: Analyses of web text drift (compressibility, semantics, domains, embeddings), nine new dated benchmarks, and 411M models each pretrained on a single year, with forecasting and model-selection experiments.
1DHx7yOj3u.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims forecasters on historic performance predict future performance best and enable more reliable model selection.
1DHx7yOj3u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the temporal perspective on LLM evaluation well motivated and practically relevant, noting that recent evaluation data is more informative about future performance.
1DHx7yOj3u.main_concern: Single-year pretrained 411M models and retrospective forecasts on benchmarks that predate model cutoffs do not reflect how models are trained or deployed, so real-deployment benefit is unproven.

aOQngtAnMB.one_liner: Conditions a diffusion font generator on donor-font deformation priors and predicted local appearance to extend typefaces to new scripts.
aOQngtAnMB.problem: Chinese reference glyphs do not determine how Latin, kana, or Bopomofo characters should be realized, so translating a family's visual language to structurally different characters is hard.
aOQngtAnMB.method: The Character Realization Prior represents same-character examples from a font bank as variations relative to neutral content to condition spatial deformation in the denoiser. Target-character appearance completion reads multi-scale local reference features to predict a spatial appearance representation, and both guide the diffusion generator.
aOQngtAnMB.key_idea: Condition deformation on donor-font same-character variations from neutral content, and predict the target glyph's spatial appearance from multi-scale local reference features.
aOQngtAnMB.evidence: Paired reconstruction and cross-script reference-style consistency on 47 fonts across Latin, kana, and Bopomofo, plus a blinded Latin-character study with 28 designers and domain experts.
aOQngtAnMB.claimed_gains: Highest-ranked generated method in a blinded Latin-character study with 28 designers and domain experts, with a 77.5% Top-2 inclusion rate.
aOQngtAnMB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-script problem is practical and that treating structural variation and local appearance as complementary objectives is well motivated, with comprehensive comparisons, ablations, and expert evaluation.
aOQngtAnMB.main_concern: Limited novelty and missing closest baselines: the donor-font prior resembles basis-font fusion in CF-Font and ABW-Font, which are not compared, and the components build on established retrieval and cross-attention.

INDBnbXOU4.one_liner: Derives layer-wise 1/width recursions and Feynman-diagram rules for finite-width statistics of orthogonally initialized networks.
INDBnbXOU4.problem: Orthogonal initialization is known to improve training and keep finite-width tensors stable at large depth, but no theory explained this stability.
INDBnbXOU4.method: The paper derives explicit layer-wise recursion relations for the tensors in the finite-width expansion under orthogonal initialization and extends Feynman diagrams for the i.i.d. recursions to all orders in 1/width. It shows the recursions reproduce the observed stability for activations with a vanishing fixed point.
INDBnbXOU4.key_idea: Layer-wise recursions for the 1/width expansion under orthogonal weights, whose solutions saturate with depth where i.i.d. initializations do not, for activations with vanishing fixed point.
INDBnbXOU4.evidence: Theory plus numerical solutions of the recursions compared against simulations; per reviews, tanh networks without biases at mostly small widths and no training experiments.
INDBnbXOU4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analytic recursions and the diagrammatic extension to orthogonal networks are a substantive theoretical contribution, with numerical predictions closely matching simulations.
INDBnbXOU4.main_concern: The claim of explaining improved performance outruns the evidence: only statistics at initialization are analyzed, with no link to training speed, loss, or accuracy.

xeKcT9GqDd.one_liner: Fixed conversational stages turn harm-sparse scenes and category cues into target-generated harmful events before image generation.
xeKcT9GqDd.problem: Existing jailbreak studies largely assume attackers specify harmful events, leaving target-generated event details and intermediate text exposure underexamined.
xeKcT9GqDd.method: I-CON supplies a harm-sparse scene and coarse category, follows three fixed text turns, and requests one image. It traces event provenance and examines intermediate descriptions and safeguards.
xeKcT9GqDd.key_idea: Use fixed ideation and concretization turns to make the target elaborate an unspecified event from a harm-sparse scene and category cue.
xeKcT9GqDd.evidence: Evaluation compares native and harm-sparse baselines, component ablations, four safeguards, and human-validated event-provenance traces.
xeKcT9GqDd.claimed_gains: The paper estimates that 99.35% of realized harmful events in successful cases are introduced by the target and not entailed by the input.
xeKcT9GqDd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a useful safety problem involving multi-turn image generation and harmful intermediate scene descriptions.
xeKcT9GqDd.main_concern: Dependence on the harmful category limits the interpretation of event delegation and needs stronger analysis.

tEkcE3HKIV.one_liner: Joint exploit-blocking and service-health checks evaluate agents repairing live vulnerable systems with or without vulnerability reports.
