tEkcE3HKIV.problem: Exploit-only evaluation misses repairs that block attacks by breaking the protected service.
tEkcE3HKIV.method: SysRepair-Bench provides live vulnerable services that agents modify through a shell and grades exploit blocking jointly with service health. Paired conditions supply or withhold the vulnerability report.
tEkcE3HKIV.key_idea: Require simultaneous exploit blocking and service health, then compare repairs with and without an explicit vulnerability report.
tEkcE3HKIV.evidence: The benchmark contains 313 remediation scenarios, including 297 binary scenarios, and uses scripted reference repairs and negative controls.
tEkcE3HKIV.claimed_gains: Median model-and-suite performance reaches 90.0% with reports and 49.4% without them, with a median per-model loss of 37.4 points.
tEkcE3HKIV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing live-system remediation while accounting for service-breaking behavior.
tEkcE3HKIV.main_concern: The grading checks need stronger evidence that they reliably establish exploit closure, service functionality, and resistance to tampering.

j1BCrHfEaj.one_liner: Layerwise generalized smoothness bounds control parameter growth to prove gradient-descent stationarity for feedforward neural networks.
j1BCrHfEaj.problem: General feedforward networks lack convergence guarantees without restrictive assumptions on width, initialization, data, or bounded iterates.
j1BCrHfEaj.method: The analysis propagates activation smoothness bounds across layers to bound gradient changes by a polynomial of parameter norms. A norm-dependent learning-rate rule controls parameter growth and yields a stationarity bound.
j1BCrHfEaj.key_idea: Bound gradient variation with a degree-2L-2 polynomial of endpoint parameter norms and control its leading term through the learning rate.
j1BCrHfEaj.evidence: The theory covers arbitrary-width and arbitrary-depth feedforward networks under stated activation and output-loss smoothness assumptions.
j1BCrHfEaj.claimed_gains: The minimum squared gradient norm converges to zero in T iterations at rate O(1/T^{1/L}).
j1BCrHfEaj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate explicit layerwise smoothness estimates and stationarity guarantees under broad assumptions.
j1BCrHfEaj.main_concern: The slow depth-dependent rate and restrictive learning-rate constants leave the practical strength of the guarantee unclear.

Z3dXHNL258.one_liner: Skill-derived executable tasks and code-verified trajectories train agents to perform reusable workflows.
Z3dXHNL258.problem: Human-written skills usually remain external instructions instead of becoming reusable capabilities within language models.
Z3dXHNL258.method: SkillGym converts skill documents into executable tasks, validates outcomes with code-based checkers, and tests skill dependence through contrastive executions. Verified trajectories and outcome rewards support supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
Z3dXHNL258.key_idea: Instantiate human-written procedures as executable environments and train on successful workflows verified by task-specific code checkers.
Z3dXHNL258.evidence: The resource contains 2,756 environments across 12 categories and 8,364 trajectories, with evaluation on GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and SkillsBench v1.1.
Z3dXHNL258.claimed_gains: Under Claude Code, fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B gains 199 Elo on GDPval-AA v2, 19.10 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and 28.13 and 14.68 points on SkillsBench v1.1 with and without skills, while SkillGym-Agent reaches 51.47% on skill-assisted SkillsBench.
Z3dXHNL258.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the executable training resource and substantial improvements over the base model.
Z3dXHNL258.main_concern: The experiments do not distinguish internalizing source skills from the benefits of additional high-quality workflow supervision and stronger teachers.

8UyLPIcKqX.one_liner: Meta-evolution edits the skill governing agent search, evaluation, resource allocation, and stopping decisions.
8UyLPIcKqX.problem: Agent evolvers optimize prompts and workflows while leaving the search process itself fixed by hand.
8UyLPIcKqX.method: FreeEvolve lets an evolver choose experiments, evidence budgets, candidate selection, and stopping within environment limits. Meta-evolution scores editable evolution skills by the fresh target agents they produce, then freezes skills for reuse.
8UyLPIcKqX.key_idea: Optimize the evolver's own search-governing skill using the performance of fresh workers produced by complete evolution campaigns.
8UyLPIcKqX.evidence: Four environments test fresh workers under matched budgets using seed, no-execution rewrite, and meta-evolved skills, with additional transfer and external-baseline comparisons.
8UyLPIcKqX.claimed_gains: Meta-evolved skills improve held-out performance by 6.9 points on average over the seed skill across four environments under the same budget.
8UyLPIcKqX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value learning the evolution process itself and fresh-worker experiments supporting reusable optimization skills.
8UyLPIcKqX.main_concern: Main external-baseline comparisons use unequal computational budgets and stopping conditions, obscuring the source of performance differences.

UWkhmzBj5B.one_liner: Softmax concentration in toy models produces one-third logit-growth and loss-decay laws, suggesting an attention bottleneck in language-model training.
UWkhmzBj5B.problem: The origin of training power laws remains unclear when models contain multiple softmax operations at different depths.
UWkhmzBj5B.method: The paper analyzes toy models in which softmax functions learn peaked distributions and derives corresponding logit-growth and loss-decay behavior. It tests the proposed mechanism through gate and optimizer studies and language-model logit and entropy measurements.
UWkhmzBj5B.key_idea: Softmax concentration requires growing logit magnitudes, creating a power-law training bottleneck even when the softmax occurs inside the network.
UWkhmzBj5B.evidence: Toy-model theory and experiments accompany Pythia and OLMo-2 measurements and logit-MSE training that tests whether the output softmax is necessary.
UWkhmzBj5B.claimed_gains: Under the toy-model assumptions, logit magnitudes grow with exponent $1/3$ and the associated loss contribution decays with exponent $1/3$.
UWkhmzBj5B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mechanistic softmax perspective and targeted toy-model experiments on training scaling.
UWkhmzBj5B.main_concern: Evidence that attention causes the observed scaling remains correlational and lacks direct interventions on the proposed bottleneck.

ZyH24rjReu.one_liner: Sign-constrained population-specific neural ODE terms decompose excitatory and inhibitory contributions to neural dynamics.
ZyH24rjReu.problem: Homogeneous NODE models obscure how distinct neuronal populations contribute to observed neural dynamics.
ZyH24rjReu.method: EI-NODE expresses population dynamics as additive source-population influences. Monotonic neural networks impose excitatory and inhibitory sign constraints on those influences.
ZyH24rjReu.key_idea: Decompose each population's derivative into per-source terms and constrain their signs with monotonic networks.
ZyH24rjReu.evidence: Synthetic circuits with known currents and recorded activity during naturalistic climbing with optogenetic perturbations test prediction and population-interaction interpretation.
ZyH24rjReu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the readable, biologically constrained decomposition and synthetic validation of population influences.
ZyH24rjReu.main_concern: The paper insufficiently distinguishes its capabilities from existing multi-population and cell-type-specific dynamics models.

Qs0Yt9gXza.one_liner: First-variation per-sample rewards from distributional functionals regularize ELBO-based reward fine-tuning of diffusion and flow models.
Qs0Yt9gXza.problem: Aggressive reward fine-tuning of diffusion and flow-matching models induces mode collapse and distributional drift, which velocity-space reverse-KL penalties constrain only indirectly through sampling dynamics.
Qs0Yt9gXza.method: Distributional Functional Rewards (DFR) generalizes the KL-regularized reward objective from expected rewards to functionals of the generated distribution and uses the first variation to define distribution-dependent per-sample rewards, recovering Fréchet distance, MMD, and DreamSim diversity terms. The framework integrates these additive rewards into ELBO-based flow fine-tuning without differentiating through feature encoders.
Qs0Yt9gXza.key_idea: Take the first variation of KL-regularized distributional functionals to derive per-sample divergence and diversity rewards for ELBO-based flow fine-tuning.
Qs0Yt9gXza.evidence: Propositions establish population functional derivatives including full-covariance Fréchet distance, supported by three-seed fine-tuning experiments and regularization-coefficient sweeps against standard KL penalties at matched task reward.
Qs0Yt9gXza.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the functional-derivative formulation cleanly unifies several output-distribution diversity rewards without encoder backpropagation and outperforms velocity-level KL regularization in preserving distributional properties.
Qs0Yt9gXza.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow novelty over prior functional and distribution-aware fine-tuning methods such as Flow Density Control, MMD rewards, kCGM, and LOO-FID, alongside bias in group-mean baseline subtraction for coupled sample rewards.

qiGzMLZhG0.one_liner: CNPC fuses neural attribute predictions with causal-circuit interventional marginals through a product of experts.
qiGzMLZhG0.problem: Standard concept bottleneck interventions overwrite corrected concepts without propagating their causal effects to related concepts.
qiGzMLZhG0.method: CNPC combines a neural attribute predictor with a probabilistic circuit compiled from a causal graph. Under interventions, a product of experts fuses neural predictions with circuit-derived interventional marginals, with compositional error analysis.
qiGzMLZhG0.key_idea: A causal probabilistic circuit supplies interventional marginals that a product of experts combines with input-dependent neural evidence.
qiGzMLZhG0.evidence: The paper derives conditional error bounds and evaluates four datasets with oracle comparisons, learned graphs, and domain shifts.
qiGzMLZhG0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the separation of neural recognition from causal inference and the explicit treatment of intervention dependencies.
qiGzMLZhG0.main_concern: Reviewers find that the theory and evaluation do not establish the accuracy or causal consistency of the product-of-experts interventional approximation.

gRbFEs5deR.one_liner: Element-wise clipping and a shared bounded parameterization replace activation and weight normalization in residual networks.
gRbFEs5deR.problem: Normalization adds computational overhead and complicates the interpretation of training dynamics in deep residual networks.
gRbFEs5deR.method: The method clips each residual branch's output before addition and constrains weights through a parameterization with one global bound. This also controls effective learning rates across layers and suppresses activation and weight outliers.
gRbFEs5deR.key_idea: A single global constant bounds residual-branch outputs and weights through element-wise clipping and scaled parameterization.
gRbFEs5deR.evidence: Experiments cover autoregressive language modeling, block diffusion, ASR, activation distributions, and post-training weight quantization.
gRbFEs5deR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple clipping mechanism and the reported resilience to low-bit weight quantization.
gRbFEs5deR.main_concern: Reviewers agree that comparisons and positioning against existing normalization-free and clipping-based methods are insufficient.

v7kG4uGXEJ.one_liner: RealLit benchmarks tabular foundation models on longitudinal literacy records with natural missingness and student-level subgroup metadata.
v7kG4uGXEJ.problem: Early-literacy prediction lacks benchmarks that capture longitudinal school data, heterogeneous assessments, missing values, and demographic differences.
v7kG4uGXEJ.method: RealLit combines research assessments with operational school records across cohorts and evaluates tabular foundation models and classical baselines. Analyses examine subgroup performance, ensembling, model versions, and missing-data handling.
v7kG4uGXEJ.key_idea: Longitudinal cohorts with natural missingness and demographic metadata support comparisons beyond aggregate literacy-prediction accuracy.
v7kG4uGXEJ.evidence: The benchmark includes 4,582 students across 53 schools and six U.S. states, with classification, regression, and subgroup evaluations.
v7kG4uGXEJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the longitudinal literacy datasets, operational records, and student subgroup information make a useful benchmark.
v7kG4uGXEJ.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of subgroup conclusions because of inconsistent ensembling findings and limited subgroup sample sizes.

r7z9xY47M2.one_liner: recAMPLIFY repeatedly applies a weight-tied Transformer core to residue states and mixes recursive states through learned gating and halting.
r7z9xY47M2.problem: Protein language models rely heavily on parameter scaling, while masked encoders lack an autoregressive loop for conventional test-time scaling.
r7z9xY47M2.method: recAMPLIFY pretrains a recursive masked protein model whose shared Transformer core refines residue-aligned states over adjustable cycles. Gated Mixture Recurrence combines visited states probabilistically and learns how much of each proposed update to accept.
r7z9xY47M2.key_idea: Weight-tied recurrence refines residue representations, while probabilistic state mixtures and residual gates jointly control adaptive computation.
r7z9xY47M2.evidence: A 155M-parameter model trains on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M and undergoes CASP contact-recovery and four supervised-task evaluations.
r7z9xY47M2.claimed_gains: With 56% fewer parameters, recAMPLIFY improves three out of four supervised tasks and raises fold accuracy by 22.8%.
r7z9xY47M2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large-scale pretraining and substantial parameter-efficient fold-prediction results across a broad task evaluation.
r7z9xY47M2.main_concern: Reviewers agree that matching training tokens does not control compute, so deeper recurrence and differing optimization settings confound attribution.

zNolMfwGC7.one_liner: Per-agent activation probes feed composite hypothesis tests that detect collusion by unknown subgroups across multi-agent environments.
zNolMfwGC7.problem: Transcript monitoring can miss covert coordination, while collusion by an unknown subgroup requires joint inference across agents.
zNolMfwGC7.method: The paper derives group-level collusion statistics from composite hypothesis testing and uses activation probes as per-agent sensors. NARCBench evaluates these statistics and heuristics under environment shifts and transfer to emergent collusion.
zNolMfwGC7.key_idea: Combining per-agent activation evidence through group-level hypothesis tests detects coordination without knowing the colluding subgroup.
zNolMfwGC7.evidence: Experiments cover four open-weight models, NARCBench holdout environments, committee-to-steganographic transfer, and third-party emergent-collusion settings.
zNolMfwGC7.claimed_gains: The best method on every model reaches 0.99 to 1.00 AUROC when transferring from committee deliberations to steganographic collusion.
zNolMfwGC7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers with positive assessments value group-level activation monitoring and evidence of transfer across structurally different collusion environments.
zNolMfwGC7.main_concern: Reviewers question the grounding and reliability of collusion labels, especially when emergent-collusion episodes do not explicitly reveal coordination.

1NgSAgPC8n.one_liner: Activation mean differences define warmth and perspective-taking directions tested through patching, projection ablation, and steering.
1NgSAgPC8n.problem: Output-based studies do not establish whether empathy-related response behaviors correspond to distinct internal directions in language models.
1NgSAgPC8n.method: The paper extracts affective and cognitive directions from differences in mean activations. Directional patching tests sufficiency, while projection ablation tests effects on warmth and noticing readouts and cross-direction interference.
1NgSAgPC8n.key_idea: Paired-prompt activation differences define candidate directions whose behavioral roles are tested by adding or removing their projections.
1NgSAgPC8n.evidence: Experiments use paired prompts, matched random directions, patching, and ablation across models, with ten warmth instruments and five replicated cognitive write bands.
1NgSAgPC8n.claimed_gains: The warmth effect averages 5.30 × matched random directions, its ablation reduces the readout gap by 1.55 projection units on 8 of 10 models, and replicated cognitive write bands average 1.57 × matched randoms.
1NgSAgPC8n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of testing separable empathy-related behaviors through interventions on model internals.
1NgSAgPC8n.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the measured directions reflect the claimed empathy functions rather than wording, event severity, or emotional salience.

U7ONNWWUMA.one_liner: GRAFT replaces concept-bearing latent video frames with safe same-video frames and fine-tunes toward the edited latent.
U7ONNWWUMA.problem: Video unlearning methods adapted from images lack erasure targets tied to videos the model would actually generate.
U7ONNWWUMA.method: GRAFT constructs targets by grafting concept-free donor frames over concept-bearing latent frames and trains with the model's native objective. Split-prompt generation creates partially concept-bearing videos when safe donor frames would otherwise be unavailable.
U7ONNWWUMA.key_idea: Safe donor frames from the same generated video provide context-matched latent targets for concept erasure.
U7ONNWWUMA.evidence: Experiments evaluate nudity, ImageNet object, and celebrity-identity erasure on CogVideoX and HunyuanVideo.
U7ONNWWUMA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that same-video donor supervision and split-prompt generation make substantive use of temporal video structure.
U7ONNWWUMA.main_concern: Reviewers question preservation of technical and temporal video quality, citing quality degradation and insufficient motion-focused evaluation.

7RvZXo8a2W.one_liner: Translation and rotation latent geometry motivate additive and orientation-field interventions that steer physical motion in decoded videos.
7RvZXo8a2W.problem: Reading physical quantities from world-model representations does not establish how to edit those representations to control motion.
7RvZXo8a2W.method: The paper analyzes simulated translation and rotation trajectories in latent space. It builds an additive writer for translation and a configuration-conditioned orientation field for rotation, then measures physical motion in decoded videos.
7RvZXo8a2W.key_idea: Different latent trajectory geometries determine separate additive translation edits and orientation-conditioned rotational edits.
7RvZXo8a2W.evidence: Simulation experiments cover linear and angular velocity and acceleration, six motion types, appearance changes, and robotic simulation with writer and decoder ablations.
7RvZXo8a2W.claimed_gains: Translation direction errors stay below 10°, speed correlations reach 0.750 in 2D and 0.861 in 3D, and spin-rate correlations reach ρ=0.942 and 0.945 under appearance changes.
7RvZXo8a2W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the geometry-motivated distinction between translation and rotation interventions and the supporting ablations.
7RvZXo8a2W.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization beyond simple synthetic scenes to complex real-world settings and stronger physical-conditioning baselines.

0Cxn7UQC8P.one_liner: A convex activation-pattern formulation fits sparse two-layer ReLU reward heads with Bradley–Terry preference likelihoods and finite-sample guarantees.
0Cxn7UQC8P.problem: Finite-sample analyses of preference learning focus mainly on linear reward heads rather than nonlinear heads.
0Cxn7UQC8P.method: The estimator combines a convex activation-pattern representation of a two-layer ReLU head with Bradley–Terry likelihood and block-sparsity regularization. The paper derives lower and upper estimation bounds and a sharper calibration when sparsity is known.
0Cxn7UQC8P.key_idea: Block-sparse selection of retained ReLU activation patterns turns nonlinear reward-head fitting into a convex preference estimator.
0Cxn7UQC8P.evidence: The paper presents minimax and estimation theory and tests synthetic rewards, language-model representations, and five preference datasets.
0Cxn7UQC8P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value systematic estimation-rate analysis for nonlinear preference learning and experiments supporting the formal results.
0Cxn7UQC8P.main_concern: Reviewers question the strength and justification of assumptions on sparse retained-pattern representation and design geometry.

RxxL8fQC96.one_liner: ImageParser distills dense verified annotations into small vision-language models that generate hierarchical, spatially grounded image parses.
RxxL8fQC96.problem: Image descriptions often omit spatial relationships, parts, or visible text needed to preserve an image's semantic information.
RxxL8fQC96.method: ImageParser trains compact vision-language models on image-parse pairs generated by frontier perception models and iterative verification. Models output JSON linking global appearance to localized entities and parts with explicit parent relationships.
RxxL8fQC96.key_idea: Train autoregressive vision-language models to serialize dense image descriptions, grounded regions, visible text, and explicit parent-child links into reusable JSON parses.
RxxL8fQC96.evidence: Training uses 6.1 million pairs; evaluation covers 1,975 human-reviewed images, six parsing metrics, detection, OCR, captioning, reconstruction, and pixel-free QA.
RxxL8fQC96.claimed_gains: ImageParser-4B improves caption and hierarchy F1 over their strongest external baselines by 20.0 and 11.8 percentage points, respectively.
RxxL8fQC96.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the dense annotation pipeline and benchmark and recognize strong structured parsing results from compact models.
RxxL8fQC96.main_concern: Standard supervised distillation offers limited modeling advances, with insufficient validation separating annotation-pipeline effects from general semantic parsing ability.

omauAGDEnW.one_liner: FactCheckRL trains search-augmented agents with reinforcement learning to locate factual errors and supply factuality rewards for language-model training.
omauAGDEnW.problem: Language models generate factual errors that fixed fact-checking pipelines do not reliably recover.
omauAGDEnW.method: FactCheckRL trains agents to interleave reasoning and search when identifying factual errors in responses. Their outputs also provide a factuality reward alongside helpfulness rewards during online reinforcement learning.
omauAGDEnW.key_idea: Learn adaptive search-and-reason policies for error detection, then reuse their factuality judgments as rewards for response-model training.
omauAGDEnW.evidence: Two human-verified sets compare error recovery with SAFE, VeriScore, and FaStFact, while LongFact and ArenaHard assess factuality and helpfulness after post-training.
omauAGDEnW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive search-based fact checking addresses a practical problem and produces encouraging error-detection results.
omauAGDEnW.main_concern: Limited evaluation across naturally occurring errors and broader factuality settings leaves the generality of the gains uncertain.

8xRwleVLG8.one_liner: SI-CDB uses asymmetric opponent selection and localized Eluder analysis to reduce saturation dependence in contextual dueling bandits.
8xRwleVLG8.problem: Saturated Bradley–Terry–Luce preferences provide weak reward information and inflate existing sample-complexity and regret bounds.
8xRwleVLG8.method: SI-CDB chooses opponent arms through an asymmetric selection rule. Its analysis uses a localized Eluder dimension for general reward classes and specializes the resulting bounds to linear rewards.
8xRwleVLG8.key_idea: Choose asymmetric comparison arms so queried-pair estimation errors control two-arm regret without worst-case inverse curvature in the leading term.
8xRwleVLG8.evidence: Theoretical analysis covers general function approximation and linear reward classes, with no experiments reported in the supplied reviews.
8xRwleVLG8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the asymmetric selection rule and improved leading regret dependence for linear rewards.
8xRwleVLG8.main_concern: An exponentially large additive reward-scale term remains and may dominate finite-horizon regret, limiting the saturation-insensitive claim's practical meaning.

i7p6mKUQFJ.one_liner: EvoHarness-RL trains agents to selectively access a shared Belief, Progress, and Experience workspace using cost-aware reinforcement learning.
i7p6mKUQFJ.problem: Environment-specific prompts and heuristics make long-horizon agent coordination with external execution support difficult to optimize jointly.
i7p6mKUQFJ.method: EvoHarness-RL exposes four state-access and update actions through a shared interface over a Belief, Progress, and Experience workspace. Supervised initialization followed by cost-aware GRPO trains agents to coordinate workspace use.
i7p6mKUQFJ.key_idea: Represent external-state access and updates as policy actions, then train their selective invocation with cost-aware GRPO.
i7p6mKUQFJ.evidence: Experiments use ALFWorld, WebShop, and WebArena, including unseen-task generalization and analyses of changing workspace use during training.
i7p6mKUQFJ.claimed_gains: EVOHARNESS-BASE improves frontier models' average success rate by 10.0 percentage points, and EVOHARNESS-RL exceeds the strongest open-source baseline by 8.5 percentage points.
i7p6mKUQFJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learned coordination with external state meaningful and acknowledge strong benchmark results.
i7p6mKUQFJ.main_concern: The framework unifies a limited state-management interface rather than the heterogeneous execution support implied by its broader harness claims.

W7GXEGdS6T.one_liner: LEAP learns a path-space action correction against a reference process to support reusable scientific trajectory objectives.
W7GXEGdS6T.problem: Local dynamics predictors and trajectory generators do not directly supply reusable objectives for complete-path inference and constrained optimization.
W7GXEGdS6T.method: LEAP decomposes stochastic action into an evaluable reference action and a learned path-space correction. Contrastive density-ratio estimation on complete trajectories yields a differentiable objective reusable for ranking, optimization, constraints, and sampling.
W7GXEGdS6T.key_idea: Estimate a density ratio between observed and reference trajectories, then combine its learned correction with the reference action.
W7GXEGdS6T.evidence: Stochastic transition, orbital, and molecular experiments examine drift recovery, persistent latent regimes, trajectory completion, constraints, and temperature transfer, alongside action-recovery theory.
W7GXEGdS6T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusable objectives over complete trajectories and the treatment of nonadditive dependencies across scientific tasks.
W7GXEGdS6T.main_concern: The paper does not clearly establish methodological advantages over existing energy-based and contrastive density-ratio models operating on complete trajectories.

qvOe1NElgR.one_liner: Enforces reversal and linear scaling constraints in neural ODE flows via shared state-dependent vector fields for zero-support transition prediction.
qvOe1NElgR.problem: Learned state-transition models struggle to generalize to unobserved condition pairs, such as reversing a state change or scaling it to a larger shift without target-edge examples.
qvOe1NElgR.method: Mechanism-Preserving Transport (MPT) models state transitions across condition pairs using shared state-dependent generator vector fields scaled linearly by the condition difference, so reversing a condition shift runs the flow backward and doubling it integrates twice as long. The paper also characterizes activation patterns that identify generator directions up to scaling and permutation.
qvOe1NElgR.key_idea: Couples condition-pair transitions through shared state-dependent vector fields scaled linearly by the condition difference to enforce exact flow reversal and scaling.
qvOe1NElgR.evidence: Evaluated with identifiability theory and experiments on PDEBench Burgers, periodic advection, Shapes3D, and Norman Perturb-seq across ten seeds.
qvOe1NElgR.claimed_gains: Reduces direct prediction MSE by 37.8% on PDEBench Burgers relative to a zero-preserving conditional ODE over ten seeds.
qvOe1NElgR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear problem formulation and systematic comparison of structural constraints (autonomy, reversal, and linear scaling) across PDE, image, and single-cell domains, including honest reporting of where linear scaling hurts.
qvOe1NElgR.main_concern: Reviewers point out unmatched optimization protocols on Shapes3D, missing control baselines on Norman Perturb-seq, and limited testing of multi-parameter interactions.

pYulMBcFGq.one_liner: Maps object pixels to a canonical rest-pose shape space with learned local descriptors to estimate long-term point tracks on deformable objects.
pYulMBcFGq.problem: Point tracking algorithms struggle to maintain long-term correspondences under complex articulation, rapid motion, and occlusion of deformable objects.
pYulMBcFGq.method: CEFFYL models the amodal representation of each pixel as a set of points on the canonical rest pose of an object category and learns a descriptor feature for local correspondences within this shared canonical space. Trained on synthetic horse data, it estimates point tracks and visibility across video frames from the canonical mapping.
pYulMBcFGq.key_idea: Projects pixels into an amodal category-level canonical rest-pose space paired with local canonical descriptors to perform pose-invariant point tracking.
pYulMBcFGq.evidence: Trained on synthetic horse data (VarenPoser) and evaluated on real horse tracking benchmarks including Horse10 and a newly introduced nine-video Showground benchmark.
pYulMBcFGq.claimed_gains: Outperforms AllTracker by 8.9 and 15.2 points and DualPM by 7.9 and 8.1 points on Horse10 and Showground videos, respectively.
pYulMBcFGq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mapping deformable objects to a shared canonical rest-pose space yields strong quantitative tracking improvements on challenging horse videos.
pYulMBcFGq.main_concern: Reviewers note that quantitative evaluation is restricted entirely to a single category (horses), incremental architectural changes over DualPM lack broad novelty, and the sim-to-real gap is insufficiently analyzed.

9lGtCNdSGM.one_liner: Generates 1.2M densely annotated multi-application desktop screens in a controllable environment to supervise GUI grounding for computer-use agents.
9lGtCNdSGM.problem: Existing training datasets for computer-use agents rarely pair complex multi-application desktop scenes and overlapping windows with dense, visibility-aware element annotations.
9lGtCNdSGM.method: DeskForge composes and explores real desktop applications while varying window layouts, states, appearance, and resolution, fusing screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry into visibility-aware element annotations. Using this system, the authors build the 1.2M-screen DeskForge-1M corpus (159.7M elements) and fine-tune vision-language models on 200K grounding examples.
9lGtCNdSGM.key_idea: Fuses accessibility trees, window geometry, and rendered screenshots during automated multi-application desktop exploration to produce occlusion- and visibility-aware GUI grounding supervision.
9lGtCNdSGM.evidence: Fine-tuned four vision-language models (including Qwen3.5-4B) on 200K examples from DeskForge-1M and evaluated on held-out desktop scenes, five external GUI grounding benchmarks (including ScreenSpot-Pro), and downstream task completion.
9lGtCNdSGM.claimed_gains: Constructs 1.2M annotated desktop observations with 159.7M element instances; fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B reaches 63.2% on ScreenSpot-Pro.
9lGtCNdSGM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize DeskForge as a substantial engineering and data-generation effort that consistently improves GUI grounding across multiple vision-language models and external benchmarks.
9lGtCNdSGM.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over prior executable GUI environments (such as OS-Atlas and ScaleCUA) and insufficient controlled ablations or matched-budget comparisons to isolate specific pipeline components.

GJTblHThsV.one_liner: Folds pixel encoding, latent diffusion generation, and pixel decoding into a single shared transformer backbone conditioned on mode tokens and timesteps.
GJTblHThsV.problem: Latent diffusion pipelines rely on separate encoder, generator, and decoder networks, leaving the standalone decoder unable to share capacity with the generative backbone.
GJTblHThsV.method: UNIFIED casts encoding, latent generation, and decoding as position-aligned sequence mappings over a single fully shared diffusion transformer backbone. The three operating modes share transformer weights and differ only in lightweight input/output heads, a mode token, and timestep conditioning.
GJTblHThsV.key_idea: Executes pixel tokenization, latent denoising, and pixel decoding within a single weight-shared transformer switched via mode tokens and timestep conditioning.
GJTblHThsV.evidence: Evaluated on ImageNet-1K 256x256 generation and reconstruction at three parameter scales (~60M, ~115M, and ~215M) against separate-network pipelines (UNITE/UNITE++), plus text-to-image generation at 218M parameters.
GJTblHThsV.claimed_gains: Improves gFID over separate-network pipelines at ~60M, ~115M, and ~215M parameters on ImageNet-1K 256x256, and reaches a GenEval score of 0.849 with 218M parameters on text-to-image generation.
GJTblHThsV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the parameter-matched comparisons are well-controlled and convincingly show that folding the decoder into a shared transformer improves FID across model scales.
GJTblHThsV.main_concern: Reviewers point out that matching parameter counts does not match training or inference compute (requiring ~1.5x more TFLOPs per image than UNITE), leaving equal-compute comparisons unaddressed.

q3ugqFEEji.one_liner: Combines density power divergence fitting with predictive Studentization to preserve finite-sample predictive efficiency in robust Gaussian process regression.
q3ugqFEEji.problem: Robust Gaussian process fitting mitigates outlier influence but typically sacrifices finite-sample predictive efficiency when data follow the assumed model.
q3ugqFEEji.method: The paper derives in closed form the finite-sample expected log predictive density gain of Studentization (accounting for uncertainty in a shared variance scale) over plug-in Gaussian prediction in GP regression. It then combines density power divergence fitting with predictive Studentization and uses a local expansion around the ordinary GP fit to quantify and bound the robustness-efficiency trade-off.
q3ugqFEEji.key_idea: Pairs density power divergence GP fitting with predictive Studentization over a shared variance scale to retain finite-sample log predictive density gains under outlier robustification.
q3ugqFEEji.evidence: Supported by closed-form theoretical derivations, local expansion bounds, controlled synthetic experiments on clean and contaminated data, and post-hoc Studentization applied to three existing robust GP models on benchmark datasets.
q3ugqFEEji.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical analysis is rigorous and clearly written, and that post-hoc Studentization offers a simple, practical way to improve joint predictive log-likelihood in robust GP models.
q3ugqFEEji.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical guarantees apply to a restrictive setting (fixed kernel, shared variance scale, small datasets with large joint prediction dimension) and use parameter intervals smaller than the robustification values tested in experiments.

m7sHHHARqS.one_liner: Conditions 4D radiative Gaussian attenuation on neighboring primitives via coverage and confidence graphs for ultra-sparse dynamic angiography reconstruction.
m7sHHHARqS.problem: Radiative Gaussian models for ultra-sparse dynamic digital subtraction angiography query each primitive independently, leaving vascular neighborhood dependencies implicit under severe angular undersampling.
m7sHHHARqS.method: RIVER introduces a relational 4D Gaussian representation where neighboring primitives explicitly condition the forward time-varying attenuation model using a coverage graph for message propagation and a confidence graph for structural regularization. It incorporates directional-state stabilization alongside transport-inspired, segment, and tubular priors.
m7sHHHARqS.key_idea: Conditions each 4D Gaussian primitive's dynamic attenuation on neighboring primitives using a dual coverage-and-confidence graph architecture paired with vascular structural priors.
m7sHHHARqS.evidence: Evaluated on ten private clinical DSA acquisitions and two public acquisitions across sparse-view settings, including capacity-matched, self-context, neighbor-context, and priors-only ablation controls.
m7sHHHARqS.claimed_gains: At ten views, increases private-cohort projection PSNR from 29.76 to 31.40 dB over the strongest compared baseline.
m7sHHHARqS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated relational design and the thorough ablation controls that separate model capacity, self-processing, neighbor communication, and structural priors.
m7sHHHARqS.main_concern: Reviewers note that 3D geometric gains (such as Chamfer distance and clDice) are inconsistent, classical iterative tomographic baselines are missing, and a large share of the PSNR gain comes from increased capacity rather than the relational mechanism.

x6A9YB9TpN.one_liner: Fuses time-aligned dual-resolution vibration spectra through a compact 39,528-parameter selective oscillatory state-space model for scarce-label fault diagnosis.
x6A9YB9TpN.problem: Machine fault diagnosis from vibration signals must learn from very limited labeled fault duration while fitting within the tight compute and memory constraints of edge devices.
x6A9YB9TpN.method: DualRes combines two time-aligned multi-resolution spectral views of vibration signals—capturing rapid transients and fine frequency structure—and processes them with a selective oscillatory state-space memory module that learns decay and rotation dynamics within a 39,528-parameter encoder.
x6A9YB9TpN.key_idea: Processes time-aligned dual-resolution spectral views with a selective damped-oscillatory state-space model to capture multi-scale vibration dynamics with minimal parameters.
x6A9YB9TpN.evidence: Evaluated under recording-level splits across six bearing datasets, a main gearbox benchmark at seven label-duration budgets, and a gearbox pilot against twelve baselines.
x6A9YB9TpN.claimed_gains: Uses 39,528 encoder parameters and, on the main gearbox benchmark with about six labeled seconds per class, improves macro-F1 by 12.06 percentage points over the next strongest comparator with a 1.24-fold speedup and 9.19-fold checkpoint storage reduction.
x6A9YB9TpN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the rigorous recording-level split protocol, duration-based label accounting, and compact physics-motivated architecture.
x6A9YB9TpN.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the contribution of the oscillatory state-space layer is not isolated from the dual-resolution spectral frontend, performance varies across bearing datasets, and single-seed ablations limit statistical confidence.

5D5pfq3nHz.one_liner: Reconstructs occluded 3D scenes from two views using bidirectional ray-intersection layers and 3D position-aware cross-view feature aggregation.
5D5pfq3nHz.problem: Single- and two-view feedforward layered 3D reconstruction methods suffer from view-dependent occlusion ordering ambiguity and weak appearance correspondence in heavily occluded regions.
5D5pfq3nHz.method: LaRI3R is a feedforward two-view 3D reconstruction framework that predicts layered scene geometry in both forward and backward ray orders to resolve occlusion inconsistencies. It pairs this bidirectional layered representation with geometry-aware feature aggregation that uses explicit 3D positional cues to link geometrically related regions across views.
5D5pfq3nHz.key_idea: Predicts multi-layer ray intersections in both forward and backward ray directions while aggregating cross-view features with explicit 3D positional cues.
5D5pfq3nHz.evidence: Evaluated on object-level and scene-level 3D reconstruction benchmarks as well as downstream relative pose estimation.
5D5pfq3nHz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and well-motivated, and that the bidirectional ray representation achieves solid object- and scene-level reconstruction performance.
5D5pfq3nHz.main_concern: Reviewers note that the representation reduces in performance equivalence to the well-studied N=2 first-and-last surface case, geometry-aware aggregation adds minimal gain in ablations, and the relative-pose evaluation metric has formulation flaws.

shmE3X8QIq.one_liner: Bounds sample-wise teacher-student f-divergence within a trust region during self-distillation fine-tuning to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
shmE3X8QIq.problem: In Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), the divergence between the demonstration-conditioned teacher and the student policy is heavy-tailed, causing high-divergence samples to drive catastrophic forgetting.
shmE3X8QIq.method: Trust-Region Constrained Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (TRSD) constructs a sample-wise trust-region-constrained teacher distribution that limits f-divergence (including forward KL, reverse KL, and squared Hellinger distance) from the current student policy without requiring extra forward passes.
shmE3X8QIq.key_idea: Projects the demonstration-conditioned teacher distribution onto a sample-wise f-divergence trust region around the student policy to cap heavy-tailed update divergences.
shmE3X8QIq.evidence: Evaluated across two model families and three adaptation domains (tool use, scientific question answering, and medical reasoning) under single-task and sequential continual adaptation across 311 sweep configurations.
shmE3X8QIq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing the heavy-tailed teacher-student KL distribution in SDFT as a driver of forgetting is an insightful empirical finding and that TRSD adds no extra forward-pass overhead.
shmE3X8QIq.main_concern: Reviewers question whether TRSD's gains simply reflect a smaller effective step size on an over-stepped SDFT baseline, note the omission of the simple high-divergence down-weighting baseline from main tables, and point out a gap between the theoretical token-level constraint and batch-relative implementation.

mhGlMHaqWM.one_liner: Combines natural-language abstractions, a Bayesian belief state over ontology errors, and executable program synthesis to learn unknown game mechanics.
mhGlMHaqWM.problem: Programmatic world modeling methods require pre-supplied symbolic representations and fail when objects, causal mechanics, and goals are unknown and dynamically evolving.
mhGlMHaqWM.method: OPINE-World maintains a hybrid world model comprising natural-language abstractions, a Bayesian exploration-centric belief state over provisional objects and unresolved interactions, and an executable programmatic transition and reward model. Interactive exploration prioritized by ontology errors and epistemic uncertainty jointly revises the hypothesized mechanics and synthesized programs.
mhGlMHaqWM.key_idea: Maintains a Bayesian hypothesis space over natural-language object ontologies and unresolved interactions to guide interactive exploration and programmatic world-model revision.
mhGlMHaqWM.evidence: Evaluated on the 25-game ARC-AGI-3 open-world benchmark using Claude Opus 4.8 high and GPT-5.5 high backbones.
mhGlMHaqWM.claimed_gains: Improves the Relative Human Action Efficiency score on ARC-AGI-3 from 1.5% to 78.4% for Claude Opus 4.8 high and from 0.5% to 84.3% for GPT-5.5 high.
mhGlMHaqWM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling natural-language abstractions and Bayesian uncertainty tracking with programmatic world models is an effective approach that achieves strong gains on ARC-AGI-3.
mhGlMHaqWM.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the dense notation and hard-to-follow presentation in Section 3, note that the natural-language ablation is only tested on three levels of one game, and point out unmatched base LLMs across baselines.

5RVLO5VJHZ.one_liner: Predicts continuous B-spline residual motion trajectories to directly splat low-resolution latent features onto arbitrary high-resolution space-time grids.
5RVLO5VJHZ.problem: Existing continuous space-time video super-resolution methods either fuse frames at low resolution—losing explicit sub-pixel positions—or upsample frames before splatting at high computational cost.
5RVLO5VJHZ.method: The method predicts per-pixel continuous motion trajectories that refine linear optical-flow paths with smooth B-spline residual motion estimated from full-sequence video features. It then directly splats consecutive low-resolution latent features onto a high-resolution grid at their predicted sub-pixel positions using learned visibility weights before decoding.
5RVLO5VJHZ.key_idea: Refines linear optical flow with continuous residual B-spline trajectories to directly forward-splat low-resolution features onto a target high-resolution space-time grid with visibility weights.
5RVLO5VJHZ.evidence: Evaluated on continuous space-time video super-resolution benchmarks including GoPro and Adobe240 across standard and extreme space-time magnification factors.
5RVLO5VJHZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving sub-pixel alignment by directly splatting low-resolution features along continuous residual motion trajectories is well-motivated and achieves strong quantitative quality and speed on GoPro and Adobe240.
5RVLO5VJHZ.main_concern: Reviewers note missing core ablations isolating direct LR-to-HR splatting from upsample-then-splat and flow-residual from full-trajectory prediction, alongside questions about whether sub-pixel aliasing theory applies to deep encoder features.

OtjsyaZBuF.one_liner: Appends a single learned probe token after each generated sentence to detect RAG hallucinations in real time from frozen generator hidden states.
OtjsyaZBuF.problem: Most RAG hallucination detectors either inspect complete responses post hoc or require a separate model to re-read retrieved documents for real-time sentence-level checking.
OtjsyaZBuF.method: After each sentence is generated, ProbeTok feeds a single shared learned probe token to the frozen RAG generator, reads out a hallucination score from its hidden states via a lightweight classifier, and restores the exact KV cache to resume generation unchanged.
OtjsyaZBuF.key_idea: Inserts a single learned probe token at sentence boundaries to query the frozen generator's existing KV cache for document support before restoring the cache.
OtjsyaZBuF.evidence: Evaluated on real-time sentence-level RAG hallucination detection benchmarks (including RAGTruth and TRIVIA+) across multiple generator architectures.
OtjsyaZBuF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the low computational overhead (one single-token forward pass per sentence with verified exact cache restoration) and the simplicity of turning a frozen generator into its own real-time detector.
OtjsyaZBuF.main_concern: Reviewers point out an asymmetric evaluation setup where ProbeTok is trained in-distribution on each dataset and generator while baseline detectors are evaluated out-of-distribution, and note that a simple last-hidden-state probe trained on the same labels performs comparably.

PTqxnXzmEa.one_liner: Optimizes LoRA matrix factors using curvature-preconditioned spectral orthogonalization and update-magnitude control.
PTqxnXzmEa.problem: Training LoRA adapters with Adam treats the two low-rank matrix factors as a flat parameter vector, ignoring their matrix-product structure and curvature coupling.
PTqxnXzmEa.method: PoLoRA (Preconditioned Orthogonalized LoRA) is a product-aware spectral optimizer derived from bounding linearized per-sample loss changes. It applies curvature preconditioning across the coupled low-rank factors, orthogonalizes updates, and controls the magnitude of each factor update.
PTqxnXzmEa.key_idea: Preconditions each LoRA factor update with the complementary factor's curvature before applying spectral orthogonalization and update-size control.
PTqxnXzmEa.evidence: Evaluated on code and math instruction-tuning datasets across language models from 1B to 8B parameters (including Llama-3.2-1B and OLMo-2-1B) against tuned Adam and Muon variants.
PTqxnXzmEa.claimed_gains: Reaches the final held-out loss of tuned Adam with a 1.2--1.7x speedup in training steps and at most 3% per-step overhead.
PTqxnXzmEa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that respecting LoRA's matrix-product structure via preconditioned spectral updates is well-motivated and yields consistent validation-loss speedups and learning-rate stability across ranks.
PTqxnXzmEa.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluations focus on held-out validation loss rather than downstream code and math benchmark accuracy, comparisons with Muon/RPLoRA baselines are limited, and the magnitude-control ablation confounds factor initialization.

On8XFD1VK3.one_liner: Compresses an entire document collection into 16 query-dependent latent memory tokens in a frozen LLM's input embedding space.
On8XFD1VK3.problem: Frozen LLMs rely on context-window memory systems that struggle to gather and combine relevant information from large document collections while keeping the prompt context short.
On8XFD1VK3.method: Memorilla encodes documents once into reusable dense embeddings and uses a learned query-conditioned cross-attention module to retrieve and compress query-specific information from the entire collection into a fixed budget of 16 soft memory tokens fed directly to a frozen LLM.
On8XFD1VK3.key_idea: Aggregates precomputed document embeddings via query-conditioned cross-attention into a fixed set of 16 soft memory tokens injected into a frozen LLM.
On8XFD1VK3.evidence: Evaluated across eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document QA, and knowledge-intensive QA (including FactKG, PersonaMem-v2, and PersonalizationV4) plus a continual TextWorld agent environment against Mem0, MemoRAG, and RAG.
On8XFD1VK3.claimed_gains: Using 16 memory tokens, achieves the best performance on five of eight benchmarks and reaches 84.33% accuracy on FactKG versus 80.43% for full-context inference while using 108x fewer tokens.
On8XFD1VK3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the query-conditioned Perceiver-style latent memory architecture clean and practical for compressing arbitrary document collections into a fixed 16-token context budget.
On8XFD1VK3.main_concern: Reviewers unanimously point out an unfair comparison: Memorilla's 194M-parameter memory module is fine-tuned on the training splits of all eight evaluation benchmarks, whereas the RAG, Full Context, Mem0, and MemoRAG baselines are evaluated training-free.

0OiV0zzVIE.one_liner: Measures deviation from a circulant Gram matrix to test whether language models represent cyclic concepts with true rotational symmetry.
0OiV0zzVIE.problem: Standard geometric tests for circular representations in language models—such as successor-operator spectra, Fourier mode concentration, and wrap-around gaps—cannot distinguish a true cycle from a linear ordering.
0OiV0zzVIE.method: The authors show mathematically and empirically that ordered non-cyclic sequences pass existing circularity tests, and derive a strict symmetry test based on the property that advancing a cyclic concept by one step is an isometry if and only if the Gram matrix of its K states is circulant. They quantify non-circulance of concept token representations against matched-length ordered controls.
0OiV0zzVIE.key_idea: Tests whether advancing one step along a K-element concept sequence acts as an isometry by measuring the distance of the states' Gram matrix from the space of circulant matrices.
0OiV0zzVIE.evidence: Evaluated across nine language models from three families (Pythia 160M to 12B, Llama-3.1-8B base and instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) on days, months, compass directions, clock hours, and ordered controls.
0OiV0zzVIE.claimed_gains: Days and months are more circulant than every same-length ordered control in all nine tested models.
0OiV0zzVIE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating how Fourier and successor tests conflate linear orderings with cycles is a valuable diagnostic insight, backed by thorough experiments across nine models.
0OiV0zzVIE.main_concern: Reviewers find the writing overly dense and long-winded, question the broader significance of testing strict Euclidean rigidity on a narrow set of cyclic concepts, and note missing circular RSA baselines.

pJIQOqOcKV.one_liner: Establishes nonconvex convergence guarantees for a randomized PipeDream abstraction, proving that steady-state pipeline staleness induces an S^4 optimization penalty.
pJIQOqOcKV.problem: PipeDream-style asynchronous pipeline parallelism eliminates synchronization bubbles using stale weights, but lacks formal convergence theory quantifying the optimization penalty of its stage-dependent staleness.
pJIQOqOcKV.method: The authors introduce Randomized PipeDream (RPD), a stale block-SGD abstraction that provides a nonconvex stationarity guarantee for pipeline-parallel training. They prove that steady-state PipeDream delay grows quadratically with the number of stages S as S^2 - S/2 + O(1), inducing a Theta(S^4 / K) stale-read optimization penalty, and compare it against pipeline-parallel LocalSGD.
pJIQOqOcKV.key_idea: Models asynchronous pipeline parallelism as randomized block-SGD with stage-dependent stale reads and proves that steady-state 1F1B scheduling produces quadratic delay in stage count S.
pJIQOqOcKV.evidence: Supported by theoretical convergence and delay derivations and simulated-time experiments comparing PipeDream, RPD, and LocalSGD on synthetic quadratic, logistic regression, and small language-modeling objectives.
pJIQOqOcKV.claimed_gains: Proves steady-state PipeDream delay grows as S^2 - S/2 + O(1) for S stages, yielding a stale-read convergence term scaling as Theta(gamma^2 S^4) or Theta(S^4 / K) under tuned step sizes.
pJIQOqOcKV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear explanation of how linear pipeline schedules induce quadratic global update delays and value the comparative framing against LocalSGD.
pJIQOqOcKV.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical guarantee applies only to the randomized RPD abstraction rather than deterministic PipeDream, closely follows prior stale coordinate-descent analyses, and is tested only on small/toy models.

Fn7fIzUIcN.one_liner: Trains a conversational memory agent across filtering, consolidation, and recall roles using stage-wise process rewards and reward-decomposed contrastive refinement.
Fn7fIzUIcN.problem: Training multi-stage conversational memory agents with end-to-end reinforcement learning suffers from severe credit assignment bottlenecks across distinct memory operations.
Fn7fIzUIcN.method: SaliMory organizes conversational memory into user facts, preferences, and working memory managed by three roles: selective filtering, consolidation, and cue-driven recall. It trains these operations end-to-end by combining GRPO with stage-wise process rewards and reward-decomposed contrastive refinement to supervise each memory operation.
Fn7fIzUIcN.key_idea: Combines group-relative policy optimization with stage-wise process rewards and role-specific contrastive preference losses across filtering, consolidation, and recall stages.
Fn7fIzUIcN.evidence: Evaluated across four conversational memory and personalization benchmarks (including LoCoMo, LoCoMo-P13n, and LongMemEval) against memory baselines such as A-Mem and Memory-R1.
Fn7fIzUIcN.claimed_gains: Cuts memory-attributed failures by one-third, outperforms prior state-of-the-art by over 10% in end-to-end recall accuracy, and more than doubles the Good Personalization rate across 4 datasets.
Fn7fIzUIcN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that structuring memory into facts, preferences, and working memory with fine-grained stage-wise evaluation metrics and rewards yields strong personalization and QA improvements.
Fn7fIzUIcN.main_concern: Reviewers question whether role-level credit assignment is genuinely isolated when all three roles share policy parameters under a summed GRPO reward, note potential reward hacking toward empty memory, and point out missing untrained same-backbone baselines and split details.

hb8lrY1Bjb.one_liner: Enables highly off-policy GRPO training in a few large generation-optimization stages by combining relaxed clipping with a negative-advantage suffix veto.
hb8lrY1Bjb.problem: Standard GRPO trains in a near-on-policy regime with frequent rollout-optimization switching, incurring high system overhead, whereas naive off-policy training collapses under high rollout staleness.
hb8lrY1Bjb.method: mu-GRPO organizes RLVR training into a small number (e.g., four) of large sequential generation-optimization stages with high rollout staleness. To prevent training collapse on stale rollouts, it combines relaxed importance-ratio clipping with a negative-advantage veto that masks out destabilizing gradient updates after low-probability trigger tokens in negative-advantage responses.
hb8lrY1Bjb.key_idea: Combines relaxed off-policy importance clipping with a negative-advantage veto that masks post-trigger suffix tokens in negative-advantage rollouts during multi-stage batch RL.
hb8lrY1Bjb.evidence: Evaluated across five language models (including Qwen3-Base-8B) on math reasoning and coding benchmarks against standard GRPO, M2PO, and BAPO.
hb8lrY1Bjb.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds standard GRPO accuracy on four of five models while reducing wall-clock training time by 1.21--2.25x (1.53x on average).
hb8lrY1Bjb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the systematic empirical diagnosis showing that off-policy GRPO collapse concentrates in suffix tokens following low-probability triggers in negative-advantage responses.
hb8lrY1Bjb.main_concern: Reviewers note an unexplained accuracy drop on Qwen3-Base-8B, unnormalized response-length differences that confound wall-clock speedup claims across methods using the same 4-stage pipeline, and checkpoint selection on test benchmarks.

iclhiABCZH.one_liner: Uses an LLM agent framework to autonomously synthesize and repair reusable Datalog rules for multi-stage symbolic binary decompilation.
iclhiABCZH.problem: Neural and agentic LLM decompilers either encode knowledge implicitly in weights or reason per-program at high runtime cost without accumulating inspectable, reusable decompilation rules.
iclhiABCZH.method: RuleCrafter decomposes decompilation into interdependent substeps (such as control-flow and data-flow analysis) and uses LLM agents guided by execution feedback, provenance tracing, and MaxSMT selection to learn symbolic Datalog rules for each stage. At evaluation time, the learned Datalog rule base executes deterministically without any LLM calls.
iclhiABCZH.key_idea: Decomposes binary decompilation into symbolic analysis stages and uses LLM agents with provenance tracing to synthesize reusable Datalog rule bases that run without LLMs at inference.
iclhiABCZH.evidence: Evaluated on decompilation re-execution benchmarks including HumanEval and MBPP across multiple LLM rule-generation backends.
iclhiABCZH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the concept of distilling LLM reasoning into inspectable, reusable symbolic Datalog rules that eliminate LLM inference costs during decompilation.
iclhiABCZH.main_concern: Reviewers point out severe sensitivity to the underlying LLM worker, missing component ablations (e.g., provenance tracing and MaxSMT selection), undefined mathematical notation in Equation 1, and limited gains over traditional decompilers.

IVM6ixB865.one_liner: Bridges the decision-making gap of visual-history agents by distilling trajectories and token-level policies from the same model's text-history policy.
IVM6ixB865.problem: Compressing multi-step agent interaction histories into rendered images reduces context cost but causes a capability drop driven by systematic drift in agentic decision-making rather than OCR failure alone.
IVM6ixB865.method: Cross-modal Agentic Policy Self-distillation (CAPS) trains a visual-history VLM agent using its own stronger text-history policy as a teacher in two stages: offline trajectory self-distillation transfers successful text-policy trajectories to rendered image histories, followed by online reinforcement learning (GRPO) with dense token-level self-distillation on student-visited states.
IVM6ixB865.key_idea: Supervises a rendered-image-history VLM agent with offline trajectories and online token-level policy distributions from the same backbone operating on uncompressed text histories.
IVM6ixB865.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B backbones on SearchQA and full-history ALFWorld against AgentOCR and text-history baselines.
IVM6ixB865.claimed_gains: Improves over AgentOCR by 5.0 and 3.4 percentage points on SearchQA and by 15.6 and 14.5 percentage points on full-history ALFWorld (for 3B and 7B backbones), while reducing average memory-context cost by up to 63.3% and peak cost by up to 83.4%.
IVM6ixB865.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the empirical diagnosis separating OCR reading fidelity from downstream agentic policy drift and find the two-stage cross-modal self-distillation pipeline well-motivated.
IVM6ixB865.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments are limited to two benchmarks (SearchQA and ALFWorld) and small Qwen2.5-VL (3B/7B) models without multi-seed variance reporting, and question whether generic History QA fully rules out task-specific OCR bottlenecks.

oXLIu8YGwK.one_liner: Distills an agent's post-failure self-reflections into lightweight LoRA adapters stored in a persistent, routable skill library.
oXLIu8YGwK.problem: In-context reflections on agent mistakes are forgotten across sessions and consume context window budget, while full-model fine-tuning is costly and risks catastrophic forgetting.
oXLIu8YGwK.method: When an agent fails a task, Self-Direction prompts the agent to reflect on its trajectory, extracts a corrective lesson, and distills it into a lightweight LoRA adapter (~0.02% parameters) while keeping base weights frozen. The resulting adapters are stored in a persistent skill library and automatically routed by embedding similarity to future tasks.
oXLIu8YGwK.key_idea: Converts single-task failure reflections into tiny modular LoRA adapters (~0.02% parameters) indexed in a persistent library for similarity-based routing on future tasks.
oXLIu8YGwK.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen-family open agents on GAIA, Claw-Eval, and Terminal-Bench 2.1 across immediate recovery, repeated encounters, and cross-difficulty transfer.
oXLIu8YGwK.claimed_gains: Trains ~0.02% additional parameters per adapter and improves overall success rates by 8.9 to 17.0 percentage points across GAIA, Claw-Eval, and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
oXLIu8YGwK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that converting failure reflections into parametric LoRA skills is an interesting continual-learning direction supported by thorough experiments on persistence and transfer.
oXLIu8YGwK.main_concern: Reviewers question whether parametric adapters clearly outperform well-matched textual skill retrieval (noting only a 2.5-point edge over Skills.md on GAIA with mismatched base rates) and raise concerns about unverified synthetic lessons and long-term adapter bank maintenance.

WATdZEo4tj.one_liner: Learns candidate safe subgraphs and performs variance-adaptive optimistic planning to achieve instance-dependent regret in tabular CMDPs with step-wise constraints.
WATdZEo4tj.problem: Existing algorithms for constrained Markov decision processes with step-wise safety constraints do not exploit how the induced safe subgraph restricts return variance and reshapes instance-dependent learning difficulty.
WATdZEo4tj.method: Safe Variance-Adaptive Exploration (SVAE) estimates candidate safe subgraphs under step-wise cost constraints and executes variance-adaptive optimistic planning within them. The theoretical analysis decomposes regret into safe-policy return variance and a statistical complexity term capturing the difficulty of eliminating unsafe actions.
WATdZEo4tj.key_idea: Combines online safe-subgraph estimation with variance-adaptive optimistic planning to bound regret by the return variance of safe policies and safety-identification complexity.
WATdZEo4tj.evidence: Supported by high-probability instance-dependent regret upper bounds, sublinear and gap-dependent step-wise constraint violation bounds, and matching lower-bound proofs in episodic tabular CMDPs.
WATdZEo4tj.claimed_gains: Attains cumulative regret of order \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{SAH\min\{V_\Sigma, K\mathrm{Var}^\star\}} + S\sqrt{AH^3\min\{K, \mathcal{C}\}} + S^2AH^2) and step-wise constraint violation of \widetilde{O}(H\sqrt{SAK} + S^2AH^2) over K episodes.
WATdZEo4tj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating safe-policy return variance from safety-identification complexity provides a clear, insightful instance-dependent characterization of learning in step-wise constrained MDPs.
WATdZEo4tj.main_concern: Reviewers note that the results are restricted to finite-horizon tabular CMDPs, the algorithmic design mainly combines existing safe-subgraph estimation with MVP-V variance-adaptive planning, and the complexity term C only reflects immediate one-step cost gaps.

MRvkRet7iP.one_liner: Derives third-order asymptotic converse and generalized-gamma achievability bounds on the minimum mean squared error of (epsilon, delta)-differentially private additive noise.
MRvkRet7iP.problem: First-order asymptotic analyses of (epsilon, delta)-differentially private additive noise mechanisms do not precisely quantify the finite-dimensional mean squared error gap relative to the calibrated Gaussian mechanism.
MRvkRet7iP.method: Using optimization duality under hockey-stick divergence privacy constraints, the authors derive a converse lower bound on the minimum MSE over all M-dimensional data-independent additive noise mechanisms for queries with l2-sensitivity Delta_2. Under a shape condition, they establish a matching achievability upper bound up to O(Delta_2^2 M^{-2}) using a closed-form calibrated generalized gamma noise mechanism.
MRvkRet7iP.key_idea: Uses linear-programming duality on the hockey-stick divergence constraint to bound optimal additive-noise MSE to three asymptotic terms in dimension M and matches it via generalized gamma noise.
MRvkRet7iP.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs of three-term asymptotic converse and achievability bounds and numerical MSE comparisons against the Gaussian and spherical generalized gamma mechanisms.
MRvkRet7iP.claimed_gains: Bounds the optimal MSE V_M(Delta_2) within A_M(Delta_2) +/- O(Delta_2^2 M^{-2}), where A_M(Delta_2) = M Delta_2^2 v_0 - Delta_2^2 C(epsilon, delta) + Delta_2^2 J(epsilon, delta) / M.
MRvkRet7iP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that proving matching converse and achievability bounds up to three asymptotic terms in query dimension M is a strong theoretical refinement in differential privacy.
MRvkRet7iP.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the technical exposition and proofs are difficult to follow, the monotonicity assumption fails for common privacy parameters like (2.5, 10^{-5}), and empirical MSE is slightly worse than the existing spherical generalized gamma mechanism.

oHUGaCVmrD.one_liner: Generates geometry-consistent long videos from a single image by conditioning a video diffusion model on hybrid point-cloud/mesh 3D priors and object-anchored Plucker camera rays.
oHUGaCVmrD.problem: Single-image long-horizon video generation models struggle to maintain 3D geometric consistency, complete unseen object surfaces, and prevent camera drift across novel views.
oHUGaCVmrD.method: VivaWorld builds a compositional hybrid 3D scene representation combining reconstructed background point clouds with generated textured foreground meshes, cleaned by a connected-region filter. It pairs rendered visual guidance from this 3D representation with a hybrid camera embedding combining global and object-anchored Plucker rays, injecting both into a video generator via a control adapter.
oHUGaCVmrD.key_idea: Combines filtered background point clouds and generated foreground textured meshes with global and object-anchored Plucker ray embeddings to guide long-horizon video generation.
oHUGaCVmrD.evidence: Evaluated on long-horizon video generation, camera control, and 3D reconstruction benchmarks (including DL3DV) with component ablations.
oHUGaCVmrD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining observed background point clouds with generated foreground meshes and object-anchored camera embeddings is a well-motivated design that improves long-horizon geometry and camera control.
oHUGaCVmrD.main_concern: Reviewers point out conflicting baseline numbers across ablation tables (Tables 3 and 4 on DL3DV), unvalidated connectivity assumptions in the mesh-seeded point-cloud filter, and unclear behavior in scenes lacking distinct foreground objects.

6OhvNc64ko.one_liner: Combines Thompson sampling with Neyman-orthogonalized reward and feature residualization to achieve horizon-optimal regret in confounded linear contextual bandits.
6OhvNc64ko.problem: In linear contextual bandits where rewards are additively confounded by a strong context-dependent baseline term, standard bandit algorithms struggle to isolate the action's treatment effect.
6OhvNc64ko.method: INF-TS draws on Neyman orthogonalization to decouple the linear context-action treatment effect from the action-independent confounding baseline by centering chosen action features with exact Thompson sampling propensities and residualizing rewards with a baseline regression oracle.
6OhvNc64ko.key_idea: Applies Neyman orthogonalization within Thompson sampling by centering action features under exact sampling propensities and residualizing rewards against an estimated context baseline.
6OhvNc64ko.evidence: Supported by an upper regret bound proof, a matching horizon lower bound proof, and empirical evaluations under stochastic and adversarial confounders including a semi-synthetic movie-recommendation task.
6OhvNc64ko.claimed_gains: Achieves \tilde{O}(d\sqrt{T\log N}) regret over horizon T for dimension d and N actions, matching the proved \Omega(\sqrt{dT\log N}) lower bound in T.
6OhvNc64ko.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using known Thompson sampling propensities to form an unbiased Neyman-orthogonalized estimator against strong user-level baseline confounding is clean, sound, and well-motivated.
6OhvNc64ko.main_concern: Reviewers note that the problem formulation and propensity-centered Thompson sampling approach are very close to prior semiparametric contextual bandit work by Kim & Paik (2019, 2021), which was omitted from comparisons.

oXZNmxg4iC.one_liner: EchoTab learns measurement-specific tokens through cross-attention and measurement reconstruction, then selects tokens for echocardiographic diagnosis.
oXZNmxg4iC.problem: Existing echocardiography representations do not expose individual measurements as intermediate features that diagnostic tasks can selectively use.
oXZNmxg4iC.method: Each measurement token attends to relevant echocardiographic views and learns to predict its corresponding tabular measurement value. Task-specific combinations of these tokens form diagnostic study embeddings.
oXZNmxg4iC.key_idea: Supervise view-attending query tokens with individual measurement targets, then combine relevant tokens for each diagnosis.
oXZNmxg4iC.evidence: Reviews describe evaluations on public and private data with method comparisons and component ablations.
oXZNmxg4iC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful empirical evidence for measurement-based representations through comparisons and ablation studies.
oXZNmxg4iC.main_concern: The method's technical distinction from established query-based learning and multi-output regression is unclear.

LrVluT9WDr.one_liner: GLARE blends global MLP and local ridge reconstructions from exogenous variables before linearly forecasting the residual.
LrVluT9WDr.problem: Relationships between exogenous variables and a forecasting target can differ between the full training period and recent observations.
LrVluT9WDr.method: A pointwise MLP learns global exogenous-to-endogenous relationships, while ridge regression fits each instance's lookback window. GLARE blends the reconstructions and uses a linear forecaster for the remaining residual.
LrVluT9WDr.key_idea: Blend a globally trained nonlinear reconstruction with a locally fitted ridge reconstruction, then forecast their residual.
LrVluT9WDr.evidence: Experiments cover the 12 TSF-X datasets, standalone and adapter settings, component ablations, and computational-cost comparisons.
LrVluT9WDr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that GLARE is small and computationally efficient, with clear experimental support in known-covariate settings.
LrVluT9WDr.main_concern: Comparisons insufficiently control access to future exogenous variables and baseline configurations, weakening attribution of the reported gains.

KOF09wtlUM.one_liner: Fast sketches accelerate power iterations, with regularized spectral approximation supplying low-rank error and runtime guarantees.
KOF09wtlUM.problem: Matrix multiplication costs make power-method low-rank approximation expensive when the target rank is large.
KOF09wtlUM.method: The framework applies fast sketching to power iterations for singular value decomposition, low-rank factorization, and Nystrom approximation. Regularized spectral approximation extends error and runtime guarantees across sketching methods.
KOF09wtlUM.key_idea: Replace expensive power-method matrix operations with fast sketches and control their error through regularized spectral approximation.
KOF09wtlUM.evidence: Theoretical error and runtime bounds cover several sketching methods, while benchmark matrix experiments compare numerical accuracy and speed.
KOF09wtlUM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the theoretical analysis of sketched power methods and its runtime-accuracy tradeoffs as substantive.
KOF09wtlUM.main_concern: The algorithm closely follows prior sketched power methods, limiting the distinct contribution mainly to the theoretical extension.

yCUgKKFuuV.one_liner: Input-adaptive spectral filtering shapes adversarial perturbations toward each time series' frequency distribution.
yCUgKKFuuV.problem: Unconstrained adversarial perturbations can violate sensor-frequency characteristics and degrade clean accuracy in time-series models.
yCUgKKFuuV.method: The method adaptively filters adversarial perturbations to regularize their spectra toward each input's spectral distribution. It avoids application-specific frequency cutoffs.
yCUgKKFuuV.key_idea: Shape adversarial perturbations with an input-adaptive filter that penalizes spectral mismatch with the original time series.
yCUgKKFuuV.evidence: Experiments span nine datasets across five health-related applications and compare clean performance and adversarial robustness with multiple baselines.
yCUgKKFuuV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean-accuracy versus robustness problem, simple adaptive filtering, and broad health-related time-series evaluation.
yCUgKKFuuV.main_concern: The robustness evaluation lacks sufficiently strong adaptive attacks and relevant adversarial-training comparisons.

yAP2Q1SVGd.one_liner: Graph neural networks score summarized reasoning-trace graphs to select code candidates without execution.
yAP2Q1SVGd.problem: Selecting correct competitive-programming candidates from reasoning alone remains difficult without execution or other answer signals.
yAP2Q1SVGd.method: The method summarizes each reasoning trace and converts it into a graph of steps, dependencies, and case analysis. A graph neural network predicts candidate correctness, with seed ensembles and problem-separated cross-testing.
yAP2Q1SVGd.key_idea: Encode reasoning summaries as dependency graphs and train a graph neural network to rank candidates by predicted correctness.
yAP2Q1SVGd.evidence: LiveCodeBench-v6 evaluation uses a leakage-free 10-fold cross-test protocol, Qwen3-8B traces, judge and topology-free baselines, and seed-ensemble analyses.
yAP2Q1SVGd.claimed_gains: Ensembles recover 0.29 of the pass@1 to pass@64 gap (+9.5 points over random selection), versus 0.12 for a frontier judge and 0.16 for an MLP; single models recover 0.19 and the worst fold 0.16.
yAP2Q1SVGd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reasoning-only candidate selection meaningful and appreciate problem-separated evaluation and analyses of ensemble variability.
yAP2Q1SVGd.main_concern: A single generator and competitive-programming setting provide insufficient support for general conclusions about reasoning-only selection limits.

MiNv8dHfC7.one_liner: Multi-view scene editing turns real driving logs into structured corner cases scored by continuous severity-aware metrics.
MiNv8dHfC7.problem: Natural driving logs contain too few rare safety-critical events for scalable evaluation of driving planners.
MiNv8dHfC7.method: CornerFactory constructs corner cases from structured specifications using multi-view object insertion, ego-pose view synthesis, and camera-platform transfer. CornerBench organizes these scenarios into a taxonomy and evaluates planners with graded safety metrics.
MiNv8dHfC7.key_idea: Generate geometrically consistent corner cases from real driving logs and score planner responses with continuous severity-aware measures.
MiNv8dHfC7.evidence: CornerBench evaluates representative planners across training scale, multimodal sensing, language reasoning, and world-model-based prediction and planning.
MiNv8dHfC7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical corner-case generation pipeline and its support for evaluating diverse planners with consistent inputs.
MiNv8dHfC7.main_concern: Quantitative validation is insufficient to establish the generation pipeline's advantages and the benchmark's added diagnostic value.

CkzayeKOgB.one_liner: Task-mixture geometry supports convex recovery of specialized experts and input-dependent routing for federated personalization.
CkzayeKOgB.problem: Federated learning often addresses differences between clients without resolving mixtures of latent tasks within each client.
