1ivlJ9lC5d.key_idea: Auditing VLA simulators via trajectory-vs-checker plots to expose and fix task-consistency, initialization, reproducibility, and physics bugs distorting acceleration comparisons.
1ivlJ9lC5d.evidence: Code-level audit and re-evaluation across seven VLA benchmarks, primarily using the π0.5 policy.
1ivlJ9lC5d.claimed_gains: Identifies 22 bugs and 4 design limitations across seven benchmarks (abstract truncated).
1ivlJ9lC5d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that auditing widely used VLA benchmarks and cataloging 22 concrete defects with fixes provides direct practical value for evaluation reliability.
1ivlJ9lC5d.main_concern: Reviewers note that many observed ranking reversals fall within statistical noise without episode counts or confidence intervals, and evaluation relies heavily on a single policy (π0.5) and limited tasks.

N24hGs7FvL.one_liner: Audits MathNet-Retrieve via controlled synthetic-versus-algebraic training pairs to measure benchmark recipe-matching.
N24hGs7FvL.problem: Synthetic LLM-generated retrieval benchmarks may reward models for matching their generation pipeline rather than learning mathematical equivalence.
N24hGs7FvL.method: The authors audit MathNet-Retrieve by training the same base retriever on equal-sized datasets of either LLM-generated recipe pairs or computer-algebra-verified pairs without LLMs, plus factorial ablations over unrelated LLM rewrites, back-translations, and negatives. They also evaluate whether benchmark gains transfer to organic human-written duplicate math problems.
N24hGs7FvL.key_idea: Compares retrievers trained on benchmark-prompt LLM pairs against computer-algebra-verified pairs across factorial positive/negative ablations and organic human duplicates.
N24hGs7FvL.evidence: Controlled training comparisons on MathNet-Retrieve across three difficulty tiers, eight seeds, prompt/negative/contamination ablations, and real human-written duplicate evaluations.
N24hGs7FvL.claimed_gains: The recipe-trained model leads by 45 R@1 points on the easiest tier; unrelated LLM rewrites recover half to two thirds, matched-closeness LLM paraphrases recover 9 points, and benchmark-prompt positives add 3 points with computer-algebra negatives versus 25 with prompt near-misses before vanishing on real duplicates.
N24hGs7FvL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the thorough, multi-seed ablation grid with contamination and negative-sampling controls, and the inclusion of organic duplicate evaluations.
N24hGs7FvL.main_concern: Reviewers note that back-translation produces shallower paraphrases than LLM rewrites, confounding LLM authorship with transformation depth, and that hard-tier labeling confounds equivalent reformulations.

sJBOHGwhUN.one_liner: Separates spatial and temporal video robustness using fixed-weight benchmarks and eight targeted temporal corruption tests.
sJBOHGwhUN.problem: Single-frame noise and blur robustness tests miss temporal degradations like dropped, reordered, or retimed frames when selecting video models.
sJBOHGwhUN.method: The authors construct a controlled fixed-weight robustness benchmark spanning spatial and temporal corruptions and prove that identical per-frame corruption distributions can still require opposite video model choices. They propose an evaluation design that separates spatial and temporal scores using eight temporal tests.
sJBOHGwhUN.key_idea: Decouples spatial and temporal robustness evaluation using fixed-weight multi-dataset benchmarks and eight temporal fault tests for model selection.
sJBOHGwhUN.evidence: Experiments across seven settings on four datasets including Diving48, SSv2, and DAVIS, single-frame controls, 37 Diving48 models under packet loss and variable frame rate, and an existence theorem.
sJBOHGwhUN.claimed_gains: On 37 Diving48 models under packet loss and variable frame rate, eight temporal tests reduce the gap to the most robust candidate by 90.4% averaged over five-model candidate sets using 20.5% as many corrupted-clip evaluations as spatial tests.
sJBOHGwhUN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad experimental scale across tasks and model constructions and the theoretical existence result showing rank reversal under dynamic degradations.
sJBOHGwhUN.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor readability with key details buried in the appendix, missing benchmark code, and a headline claim broader than the main empirical test.

ffEf4liRLb.one_liner: Models leaderboard view overlaps as graphs and audits ranking uncertainty via anchored cross-view empirical Bayes.
ffEf4liRLb.problem: Sparse evaluation leaderboards with partially overlapping views can have unidentifiable shared scales that undermine confidence intervals and ranking probabilities.
ffEf4liRLb.method: The authors represent view overlaps as a graph, proving that bipartite connected components leave a scale ambiguity whereas odd cycles eliminate it, and derive a Gaussian log-moment information bound. They introduce ACEB, a target-label-free audit combining graph diagnostics, fixed-anchor latent-score estimation, leave-view residual-noise estimation, and selective abstention.
ffEf4liRLb.key_idea: Uses overlap-graph odd-cycle diagnostics and fixed-anchor cross-view empirical Bayes with leave-view noise estimation to audit scale identifiability and abstain on low-confidence rankings.
ffEf4liRLb.evidence: Graph-identifiability theorems, Gaussian information bounds, sparse heterogeneous simulations with six baselines, and evaluation on 13,077 MedHELM pairwise-gap records.
ffEf4liRLb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear graph-based identifiability analysis, explicit assumptions, component ablations, and candid discussion of limitations.
ffEf4liRLb.main_concern: Reviewers point out that MedHELM false-declaration reductions are confounded by lower declaration rates (78.6% vs. 98.3%), iteration caps lack convergence diagnostics, and the bipartite-graph criterion overlaps with prior work.

AvP3MH0PjD.one_liner: Selects multi-target LLM post-training data mixtures via portfolio-style quadratic programming over signed dataset gradients.
AvP3MH0PjD.problem: Selecting a single auxiliary post-training dataset mixture for multiple potentially conflicting target tasks under a fixed budget is harder than single-target selection.
AvP3MH0PjD.method: The authors formulate Multi-Target Kernel Mean Matching (MT-KMM) as a Markowitz portfolio optimization problem using linear scalarization over user-specified target preferences and a shared auxiliary redundancy penalty. Each dataset is represented once by its normalized signed gradient at a frozen reference model, allowing the selected mixture to be reused across larger models.
AvP3MH0PjD.key_idea: Solves a scalarized Markowitz-style quadratic program over normalized signed gradients from a frozen reference model to score and mix auxiliary post-training datasets.
AvP3MH0PjD.evidence: Finite-preview stability theory and post-training experiments across Llama and Qwen model families (up to 70B) using SFT and GRPO, with representation and allocation ablations.
AvP3MH0PjD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical one-shot selection that transfers across scales, the broad empirical evaluation across model families and SFT/GRPO, and the thorough experimental controls.
AvP3MH0PjD.main_concern: Reviewers consider the method incremental over single-target KMM with linear scalarization and signed features, noting missing direct comparisons to multi-target mixture optimizers and a gap between signed-sum matching and actual mixture updates.

3jo3PqZibw.one_liner: Speeds up block-diffusion LM inference by reusing bounded, recoverable sparse KV-cache read plans across denoising steps.
3jo3PqZibw.problem: Long-context inference in block-wise diffusion language models is memory-bound because every denoising step re-reads a growing KV cache, while naive sparse attention inflates collective reads or permanently evicts needed history.
3jo3PqZibw.method: RISA partitions newly generated historical KV into priority and recovery tiers without permanently evicting history. Seed queries build a bounded shared read plan whose indices are reused across denoising steps in the block while attention is recomputed with fresh queries and current-block KV.
3jo3PqZibw.key_idea: Separates tiered historical KV preservation from repeated reading by having seed queries build a bounded shared sparse read plan reused across block denoising steps.
3jo3PqZibw.evidence: Experiments on DreamReasoner-8B at a 32K-token prefix, a 128K scalability study, and ablations on cold recovery, per-step selection, and hot read caps.
3jo3PqZibw.claimed_gains: On DreamReasoner-8B at a 32K-token prefix, RISA retains comparable task performance while delivering 2.32× sparse-attention and 1.36× per-request speedup over dense attention.
3jo3PqZibw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating KV preservation from repeated reads is well-motivated, practical without modifying the backbone, and delivers consistent speedups while preserving accuracy.
3jo3PqZibw.main_concern: Reviewers note that the priority-score rule is underspecified, largest speedups occur beyond the 32K context limit via hot-read capping rather than cold recovery, and hyperparameter ablations and LoSA comparisons are missing.

en9hEsMNud.one_liner: Maps inference compute allocation across summaries, retrieval, and model size on LongBench-v2 via a 15-parameter scaling law.
en9hEsMNud.problem: It is unclear how to optimally split inference compute between reusable document summaries, question-time retrieval, and model size for long-document QA.
en9hEsMNud.method: The authors sweep five levers—summary length, retrieval call count, passages per call, passage length, and Qwen3.5 model size (0.8B–27B)—while counting exact theoretical FLOPs. They fit a 15-parameter predictive law capturing summary-retrieval substitutability and a model-size capability threshold near 4B parameters to derive compute-optimal allocations.
en9hEsMNud.key_idea: Models accuracy across summary length, retrieval parameters, and model size via a 15-parameter law over exact per-question FLOPs to derive compute-optimal RAG allocations.
en9hEsMNud.evidence: Approximately 860k question-configuration pairs on LongBench-v2 across five Qwen3.5 sizes (0.8B to 27B) with exact theoretical FLOPs accounting.
en9hEsMNud.claimed_gains: The 15-parameter law predicts unseen lever combinations close to the sampling-noise limit, whereas an agent left to choose how often to search stays about 7 accuracy points below the compute-optimal allocation.
en9hEsMNud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the large-scale 860k-pair experimental grid, exact per-token FLOPs accounting, and quantitative analysis of summary-retrieval trade-offs.
en9hEsMNud.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty and transferability of the 15-parameter curve fit given prior RAG compute-allocation laws and evaluation on only one model family, benchmark, and pipeline.

eFt7AX16Hj.one_liner: Benchmarks policy-governed tool-use agents against adaptive conversational social engineering paired with matched benign tasks.
eFt7AX16Hj.problem: Existing safety benchmarks do not jointly test whether policy-governed tool-use agents resist adaptive conversational attacks while completing matched legitimate requests.
eFt7AX16Hj.method: The authors build TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark using personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation targeting policy-prohibited actions hidden from the attacker, paired with benign counterparts (TACT-Base) and benign-before-attack sequences (TACT-TrustPrime). They introduce Paired Selective Trustworthiness (PST) to jointly measure safe refusal and matched benign task completion.
eFt7AX16Hj.key_idea: Pairs policy-blind adaptive conversational attacks with matched benign tool-use tasks in stateful environments and scores both refusal and utility via Paired Selective Trustworthiness.
eFt7AX16Hj.evidence: Evaluations across six assistant models, attack baselines, and defense mechanisms on TACT-Base and TACT-TrustPrime.
eFt7AX16Hj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing adaptive conversational attacks with matched benign tasks and evaluating safety alongside utility via PST addresses a practically important gap.
eFt7AX16Hj.main_concern: Reviewers note that all tasks are confined to a single retail environment with one LLM attacker simulator, dense notation hinders readability, and the benign false-block defense metric conflates blocking unauthorized calls with false positives.

CKZvQpG6fh.one_liner: Disentangles item multimodal representations into content-aware and bias-aware components using contrastive learning and independence regularization for debiased recommendation.
CKZvQpG6fh.problem: Multimodal recommendation models suffer from popularity-amplified presentation bias when user clicks are driven by superficial visual or textual cues rather than intrinsic item content.
CKZvQpG6fh.method: CORE formalizes presentation bias in a structural causal model as collider bias from coupled multimodal features. It separates each item's representation into independent content-aware and bias-aware components via automated contrastive learning and an independence constraint, then recommends using only the content representation.
CKZvQpG6fh.key_idea: Disentangles multimodal item embeddings into content and bias branches via automated contrastive pairs and an independence penalty, then discards the bias branch at inference.
CKZvQpG6fh.evidence: Evaluated on three recommendation datasets using accuracy, coverage, and diversity metrics against recommender baselines.
CKZvQpG6fh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating intrinsic content from superficial presentation cues in multimodal recommendation is a relevant problem with a simple, easy-to-implement architecture.
CKZvQpG6fh.main_concern: Reviewers identify flawed causal claims—independence regularization does not identify latent variables or perform a true intervention—alongside using popularity as a proxy for presentation and inconsistent or questionable reported metrics.

eGepP68iQh.one_liner: Aligns conversational multimodal emotion features using momentum class anchors, speaker-aware transition prototypes, and transition-targeted modality perturbation consistency.
eGepP68iQh.problem: Existing multimodal emotion recognition methods in conversations often overlook class-level multimodal priors and speaker-aware emotional transitions across adjacent turns.
eGepP68iQh.method: SEDAL constructs momentum-evolving class-level multimodal emotion anchors to align text, audio, visual, and fused representations. It extends these to adjacent turns via speaker-aware emotion transition prototypes and applies anchor-guided modality perturbation consistency learning selectively on transition-relevant utterances.
eGepP68iQh.key_idea: Combines momentum-updated class-level multimodal anchors with speaker-aware adjacent-turn transition prototypes and selective perturbation consistency on transition utterances.
eGepP68iQh.evidence: Evaluated on IEMOCAP and MELD against multimodal emotion recognition baselines with ablation studies and robustness evaluations.
eGepP68iQh.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers agree that the framework coherently integrates class anchors and speaker-aware conversational context with strong empirical results on IEMOCAP and MELD.
eGepP68iQh.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the transition prototype bank only indexes the current emotion and same/cross-speaker flag rather than modeling previous-to-current emotion transitions, and question the complexity and incremental novelty.

f0NgAoN25v.one_liner: Compares compute efficiency of search-trace versus solution-only Transformer training across scaling, task structure, heuristic availability, and trace completeness.
f0NgAoN25v.problem: Training Transformers on intermediate search traces improves accuracy over solution-only supervision but uses longer sequences, leaving unclear when search imitation is actually compute-efficient.
f0NgAoN25v.method: The authors systematically vary training compute budget, model and dataset scale, problem structure, and intermediate trace supervision across maze navigation, regular Countdown, and a heuristic-resistant modular Countdown variant. They characterize two empirical regimes—search-optional and search-efficient—and test incomplete or semantically unrelated traces.
f0NgAoN25v.key_idea: Systematically benchmarks compute-matched search-augmented versus solution-only Transformer training while varying problem structure, heuristic utility via modular Countdown, and trace completeness.
f0NgAoN25v.evidence: Five-seed Transformer training experiments across model and dataset scales on maze navigation, regular Countdown, simplified Countdown, and modular Countdown.
f0NgAoN25v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the compute-matched evaluation of search-trace supervision is well written, systematically executed, and asks a meaningful question.
f0NgAoN25v.main_concern: Reviewers note that each regime is represented by only one task with confounded differences between Maze and Countdown, and the taxonomy describes experimental outcomes rather than yielding a predictive principle.

f4TzyqXvHT.one_liner: Benchmarks persistent LLM agents chronologically over 13,407 evolving ten-year workplace documents without answer feedback across finance, medicine, and law.
f4TzyqXvHT.problem: Existing agent benchmarks reset agents between tasks or assume static records, failing to measure whether persistent agents improve or degrade over years of evolving real-world documents without ground-truth feedback.
f4TzyqXvHT.method: TenureBench replays 13,407 official documents spanning ten years of finance, medicine, and law in chronological order to one persistent agent per domain while retaining old document versions alongside revisions. Agents solve 920 multi-date tasks without ever receiving ground-truth answers, and are compared against fresh agents and human experts.
f4TzyqXvHT.key_idea: Replays a decade of versioned official documents chronologically to persistent agents without feedback to measure accuracy and tool-use trajectories over a simulated career.
f4TzyqXvHT.evidence: Evaluates five frontier models and human experts on a 300-task sample of 920 tasks built from 13,407 documents across finance, medicine, and law, plus fresh-agent controls.
f4TzyqXvHT.claimed_gains: On the 300-task sample, the best of five frontier models solves 52.7% versus 84.0% for human experts, while a fresh agent given source documents and grading criteria solves 92%.
f4TzyqXvHT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TenureBench introduces a realistic, well-documented chronological evaluation setting for persistent agents operating over evolving records.
f4TzyqXvHT.main_concern: Reviewers point out that performance decline on later tasks is confounded with growing archive size and task difficulty, tool-call reductions ignore token/latency costs, and the human-expert and single-judge evaluations are insufficiently validated.

jYfZCtkBo9.one_liner: Uses prompt-conditioned VLM representations instructed to ignore distractors as prediction targets for training latent action models.
jYfZCtkBo9.problem: Latent action models fail when video observations contain action-correlated distractors because they encode irrelevant visual noise instead of controllable agent motions.
jYfZCtkBo9.method: The authors prompt pretrained Vision-Language Models with brief task descriptions instructing them to ignore distractors and use the resulting embeddings as prediction targets during latent action model training. They benchmark a wide range of VLMs, prompting strategies, and representation extraction settings against CLIP and DINOv2.
jYfZCtkBo9.key_idea: Replaces pixel or visual-encoder forward-dynamics targets in latent action models with task-prompted VLM representations instructed to filter out visual distractors.
jYfZCtkBo9.evidence: Benchmarks multiple VLMs, CLIP, and DINOv2 across prompts and hyperparameters, measuring latent action quality and downstream task success on Distracting MetaWorld.
jYfZCtkBo9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using promptable VLM representations as LAM targets is a clear, simple intervention backed by extensive benchmarking and strong Distracting MetaWorld improvements.
jYfZCtkBo9.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over existing LAPO and promptable-representation work, and argue comparisons against CLIP/DINOv2 confound language conditioning with architecture and pretraining differences.

DSSLq567KW.one_liner: Compresses OmniLLM audio-visual tokens training-free via activity-based temporal budgeting and correlation-routed separate selection or joint merging.
DSSLq567KW.problem: Fixed audio-visual token compression strategies in OmniLLMs either discard modality-unique cues when audio and video are complementary or retain redundant tokens when they overlap.
DSSLq567KW.method: OmniTrim is a training-free pre-LLM token compression framework with two stages: Information-Aware Budgeting allocates token budgets across temporal chunks based on audio-visual activity and temporal variation, and Correlation-Aware Selection switches between separate token selection and joint token merging based on chunk-level audio-visual cosine similarity.
DSSLq567KW.key_idea: Allocates per-chunk token budgets by audio-visual activity and dynamically routes chunks between separate selection and joint merging using chunk-level audio-visual feature correlation.
DSSLq567KW.evidence: Evaluated across six audio-visual benchmarks on two Qwen2.5-Omni model sizes (including Qwen2.5-Omni-7B) against existing OmniLLM token compression baselines.
DSSLq567KW.claimed_gains: At 25% token retention on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, OmniTrim preserves 98.8% of full-token performance while achieving a 4.35× prefill speedup and 55.3% higher decoding throughput.
DSSLq567KW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that OmniTrim's training-free two-level design (budget allocation plus adaptive selection/merging) is clean, cheap, and addresses a real limitation of fixed policies.
DSSLq567KW.main_concern: All three reviewers criticize that the chunk-level cosine correlation signal between unaligned audio and vision encoders is never directly validated as measuring redundancy versus complementarity.

rQBeZDPPlM.one_liner: Weights audio-visual contrastive positive pairs using semantic agreement scores derived from modality-specific captions with warmup and gradual thresholding.
rQBeZDPPlM.problem: Standard audio-visual contrastive learning treats all co-occurring pairs as equally aligned, even when off-screen sounds or unrelated visuals create weak semantic correspondence.
rQBeZDPPlM.method: Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL) generates modality-specific captions for audio and video, estimates semantic agreement scores between them via an LLM, and uses those scores to weight positive pairs in contrastive loss without inference overhead. It introduces the weighting progressively via a warmup period and gradual thresholding.
rQBeZDPPlM.key_idea: Reweights positive audio-visual contrastive pairs using semantic agreement scores computed from separate audio and video captions, phased in via warmup and gradual thresholding.
rQBeZDPPlM.evidence: Applied to three contrastive learning baselines and evaluated on audio-visual retrieval benchmarks, including out-of-domain datasets and a 15% synthetic audio-shuffling setting.
rQBeZDPPlM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CGAAL is a simple, model-agnostic weighting scheme with zero inference overhead that consistently improves retrieval across three baselines.
rQBeZDPPlM.main_concern: All three reviewers note missing comparisons against simpler correspondence estimators and existing noisy-correspondence or soft-weighted contrastive methods, leaving the need for LLM caption scoring unproven.

x9lHlsYYKk.one_liner: Improves self-reflective unified multimodal image generation training-free by amplifying corrective KV signals and adding an external verification fallback.
x9lHlsYYKk.problem: Self-reflective unified multimodal models struggle on compositional multi-object image generation due to failing to diagnose errors during reflection or failing to execute visual corrections.
x9lHlsYYKk.method: The authors decompose self-reflective generation bottlenecks into reflection failure and correction failure and propose RECAF, a training-free framework that retains the unified model for generation and reflection. RECAF strengthens visual edits via KV-cache correction amplification and applies an external verification fallback when reflection misses constraint violations.
x9lHlsYYKk.key_idea: Combines training-free KV-cache amplification of corrective feedback with an external verification fallback to address correction and reflection failures in unified multimodal models.
x9lHlsYYKk.evidence: Evaluated on GenEval, GenEval++, and GenEval2 compositional image generation benchmarks with component ablations.
x9lHlsYYKk.claimed_gains: RECAF outperforms baselines by 5.0 points on GenEval, 5.7 points on GenEval++, and 3.5 points on GenEval2.
x9lHlsYYKk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing iterative generation errors into reflection versus correction failures is analytically clear and that RECAF yields consistent training-free gains.
x9lHlsYYKk.main_concern: Reviewers question fairness and novelty, noting that the external verification fallback closely mirrors GenEval scoring criteria, methodological components combine existing KV scaling and verification, and mechanistic justification for amplification is incomplete.

0m0HaCHIuR.one_liner: Evaluates graph generative models using 20 localized graphlet correlation descriptors conditioned on pairwise orbit adjacency matrices.
0m0HaCHIuR.problem: Standard graph generative model descriptors such as average orbit counts or global graphlet correlations discard how substructure roles co-vary across locally connected nodes.
0m0HaCHIuR.method: The authors introduce localized graphlet correlation, a family of 20 descriptors that condition pairwise orbit-count correlations on orbit adjacency matrices recording how often two nodes co-occur in specific orbits of the same graphlet instance. Each descriptor acts as an assortativity coefficient between orbit positions.
0m0HaCHIuR.key_idea: Conditions pairwise graphlet orbit-count correlations on orbit-adjacency matrices to measure local assortativity of substructure roles across co-occurring nodes.
0m0HaCHIuR.evidence: Evaluated on three procedurally generated synthetic graph benchmark datasets with known generative properties, plus hyperparameter and perturbation analyses.
0m0HaCHIuR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning graphlet correlations on local orbit adjacency addresses a real expressivity limitation of global graph descriptors in an interpretable way.
0m0HaCHIuR.main_concern: Multiple reviewers flag major numerical and configuration inconsistencies between the recommended 5-conditioning descriptor in the text and the results reported in Table 1 and ablations, alongside missing neural evaluation baselines.

WiFUsSPiMd.one_liner: Combines selective memory-snapshot recall, hierarchical multi-level credit, and listwise trajectory reranking for long-context multi-hop QA agents.
WiFUsSPiMd.problem: Recurrent long-context agents lose overwritten hypotheses during memory compression, conflate intermediate decision failures, and lack joint partial-trajectory ordering.
WiFUsSPiMd.method: HITRA equips recurrent agents with selective snapshot recall to recover prior hypotheses, hierarchical credit assignment normalizing planning, action, and structural-validity feedback separately, and listwise learning with a separable surrogate to rank concurrent partial trajectories.
WiFUsSPiMd.key_idea: Integrates recoverable memory snapshots, separately normalized hierarchical step-and-terminal credit, and separable listwise trajectory reranking within a bounded active context.
WiFUsSPiMd.evidence: Evaluated on HotPotQA using Qwen-family models with diagnostic studies on hypothesis recovery and trajectory selection.
WiFUsSPiMd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that HITRA targets real coupled failure modes of recurrent long-context memory agents and shows positive results on HotPotQA.
WiFUsSPiMd.main_concern: Reviewers highlight unacknowledged overlap with ReMemR1 (which already uses memory recall and multi-level rewards), evaluation restricted to one benchmark (HotPotQA) and one model family, and dense notation.

ei8NxUoCD5.one_liner: Augments JEPA world models with an inverse-dynamics action reconstruction loss to preserve controllable unstable modes for feedback stabilization.
ei8NxUoCD5.problem: Standard JEPA next-step prediction with anti-collapse regularization can still collapse controllable unstable modes required for feedback stabilization.
ei8NxUoCD5.method: The paper augments JEPA world-model training with an action reconstruction (inverse dynamics) loss. It proves for linear systems that exact action reconstruction makes the encoder injective on the finite-horizon reachable subspace, preserving controllable unstable directions.
ei8NxUoCD5.key_idea: Adds an inverse-dynamics action reconstruction objective to JEPA training so the encoder remains injective on the finite-horizon controllable reachable subspace.
ei8NxUoCD5.evidence: Provides linear-system counterexamples and injectivity theory plus nonlinear visual control experiments on CartPole, Walker2D, and PointMaze.
ei8NxUoCD5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the control-theoretic distinction between non-collapsed predictive representations and representations sufficient for feedback stabilization.
ei8NxUoCD5.main_concern: Reviewers question whether unstable-mode collapse actually occurs in practical nonlinear tasks and note that empirical evidence (mostly CartPole LQR) does not isolate unstable-mode preservation from local dynamics accuracy.

IlaF243TcO.one_liner: Pairs a 5B single-stream DiT pretrained for bilingual text-layout control with an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancer.
IlaF243TcO.problem: Open-weight text-to-image models struggle to render dense long-form text and complex layouts from brief user requests.
IlaF243TcO.method: MORTIS pretrains a 5B single-stream DiT from scratch where natural-language descriptions and explicit layouts share a text-conditioning pathway, paired with an intention-aware agentic prompt-enhancement module translating brief requests into detailed content and layout specifications. It also introduces LongLongTextBench (LLTB) and RealLayoutArena (RLA).
IlaF243TcO.key_idea: Couples a 5B single-stream DiT trained for unified text-and-layout conditioning with an agentic prompt enhancer generating structured layout specifications.
IlaF243TcO.evidence: Evaluated on LLTB (English/Chinese long-form text), RLA (61 poster/infographic/UI tasks), and 7Bench, including shared-prompt cross-backbone comparisons.
IlaF243TcO.claimed_gains: Achieves 96.3% average text coverage on LLTB, ranks second end-to-end on RLA, and ranks first among generators under shared enhanced prompts.
IlaF243TcO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean separation of specification enhancement from rendering, the shared-prompt cross-backbone test, and the documented 5B training effort.
IlaF243TcO.main_concern: Reviewers flag unisolated pretraining recipe choices, unresolved 3x discrepancies against published Ideogram 4 scores on 7Bench, potential OCR-judge leakage, and limited differentiation from prior systems.

t8p3BkzOKo.one_liner: Trains trace-inversion models to synthesize reasoning chains from black-box LLM input-output pairs for downstream reasoning distillation.
t8p3BkzOKo.problem: It is unknown whether hiding internal chains of thought behind black-box APIs prevents attackers from distilling a model's reasoning capabilities.
t8p3BkzOKo.method: The paper trains Trace Inversion models on surrogate traces to reconstruct detailed reasoning traces given only a target model's inputs, final outputs, and optional brief reasoning summaries. Student models are then fine-tuned on these synthesized traces.
t8p3BkzOKo.key_idea: Trains a surrogate-based trace inverter to synthesize chains of thought from black-box input-output pairs and optional summaries for student distillation.
t8p3BkzOKo.evidence: Evaluates downstream student reasoning accuracy and trace overlap with ground-truth reasoning traces across settings with and without summaries.
t8p3BkzOKo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing whether hiding reasoning traces prevents capability extraction is a relevant practical question with a clear distinction between faithful recovery and useful supervision.
t8p3BkzOKo.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty over existing answer-conditioned rationale synthesis (STaR, RLT, REER), confounded gain attribution, and missing experimental controls (such as direct/full).

Hpst1JDKCq.one_liner: Solves large-scale Ordered Clustered TSP using layered-DAG dynamic programming orchestrating RL-warm-started attention-GNN sub-solvers.
Hpst1JDKCq.problem: Optimizing clusters independently in the Ordered Clustered Traveling Salesman Problem misses non-local inter-cluster dependencies and limits solution quality.
Hpst1JDKCq.method: COMPASS formulates OCTSP as a layered DAG coordinating intra-cluster routes and inter-cluster bridges, orchestrating sub-solvers (including cuOpt) warm-started by reinforcement learning over an attention-enhanced GNN on general asymmetric distance matrices. Global dynamic programming and post-optimization remove fixed quality ceilings.
Hpst1JDKCq.key_idea: Orchestrates RL-warm-started attention-GNN intra-cluster sub-solvers over general distance matrices via layered-DAG dynamic programming across ordered clusters.
Hpst1JDKCq.evidence: Provides conditional exactness theory and benchmarks on large-scale asymmetric OCTSP instances up to 100K scale including real e-commerce order locations.
Hpst1JDKCq.claimed_gains: Reaches an asymmetric routing scale 9x beyond established ATSP benchmarks.
Hpst1JDKCq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear writing, principled layered-DAG formulation, and strong large-scale empirical scalability on OCTSP.
Hpst1JDKCq.main_concern: Reviewers note missing component ablations (e.g., cuOpt without RL warm-start), modest gains over heuristics relative to compute, narrow OCTSP scope, and minimal learned-component novelty for ICLR.

bkIXwcoMQ2.one_liner: Combines a pointwise convex-weight motion calibrator with associative projective geometric-algebra motor products for evaluation-path-invariant odometry.
bkIXwcoMQ2.problem: Learned neural sequence composers lack associativity, causing outputs to change under different binary reduction trees or chunking schedules.
bkIXwcoMQ2.method: A 2,311-parameter pointwise network assigns convex weights to redundant 0.1 s rigid-motion estimates using label-free disagreement descriptors with bounded extrapolation. Projective geometric-algebra (PGA) motor products compose calibrated leaves into an exactly associative, mergeable summary.
bkIXwcoMQ2.key_idea: Calibrates leaf rigid motions via a tiny convex-weighting network and composes them using associative projective geometric-algebra motor products for exact reparenthesization invariance.
bkIXwcoMQ2.evidence: Proves reachable-closure associativity equivalence and evaluates on 11,219 family-held-out ETH3D odometry windows, KITTI, and MovieLens diagnostics with five-seed clustered intervals.
bkIXwcoMQ2.claimed_gains: On family-held-out ETH3D at 3.2 s, achieves 0.104 m translation and 4.1 deg rotation error vs 0.915 m / 45.1 deg for identity, 0.440 m / 28.6 deg for the original gate, 0.320 m / 14.9 deg for best non-learned filter, 0.180 m / 7.9 deg for best of 31 non-learned rules, and 0.351 m for recurrent regression (51.9% reduction vs identity in TL;DR).
bkIXwcoMQ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean structural mergeability guarantee, thorough uncertainty estimation, and diagnostic separation of path invariance from sequence-length generalization.
bkIXwcoMQ2.main_concern: Reviewers note that associativity-to-path-invariance equivalence is classical with limited theoretical novelty, while predictive gains are dataset-dependent (worsening KITTI translation error) and stem from calibration rather than PGA.

7tsy5BAqPe.one_liner: Adapts computer-use agents to evolving interfaces and workflows via hybrid GUI-code actions and failure-driven synthetic RL curricula.
7tsy5BAqPe.problem: Application updates and evolving user workflows degrade computer-use agents, while manually curating updated training environments is costly.
7tsy5BAqPe.method: CUAEvolve interleaves GUI actions with executable code to bypass brittle visual grounding when programmatic interfaces persist, and runs a self-improving RL loop that diagnoses failures to synthesize targeted tasks, initial states, and evaluators. It also introduces OSEvolveBench pairing original tasks with application and workflow variants.
7tsy5BAqPe.key_idea: Interleaves GUI and code actions while using failure diagnoses to automatically synthesize targeted task curricula, initial states, and evaluators for continual RL.
7tsy5BAqPe.evidence: Evaluated on OSEvolveBench (held-out application and workflow evolutions) and general computer-use tasks against static and random curricula with human task audits.
7tsy5BAqPe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting computer-use agents to evolving apps and workflows is a timely problem and value OSEvolveBench and the curriculum ablations.
7tsy5BAqPe.main_concern: Reviewers note OSEvolveBench relies on synthetic single-axis React mock mutations that code execution may bypass, results come from single seeds with small 2-3 point margins, and task generation depends on GPT-5.6 Sol.

5Wxva1Z8ls.one_liner: Implants trigger-activated LLM backdoors by optimizing only gated parametric memory parameters while keeping backbone weights frozen.
5Wxva1Z8ls.problem: Gated parametric memory modules in open-weight LLMs create an unexamined supply-chain attack surface separable from backbone weights.
5Wxva1Z8ls.method: BadEngram uses post-training gradient optimization solely on gated-memory parameters (such as Engram or Per-Layer Embedding subsystems) while freezing the backbone and execution graph, implanting persistent trigger-dependent harmful behavior.
5Wxva1Z8ls.key_idea: Backpropagates a backdoor objective exclusively into gated parametric memory weights while keeping the LLM backbone frozen and unchanged.
5Wxva1Z8ls.evidence: Evaluated with causal pathway interventions on a controlled Engram model and at production scale on the 176B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Per-Layer Embedding subsystem across HarmBench, AdvBench, and SQuAD.
5Wxva1Z8ls.claimed_gains: Achieves 96.6% ASR with 0.1% false activation and 99.6% clean accuracy on controlled Engram (dropping to <=0.32% under clean memory/gate ablation), and 50.4% HarmBench / 60.0% AdvBench ASR with 0.9% dormant ASR on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
5Wxva1Z8ls.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate identifying gated parametric memory as a distinct supply-chain attack surface, strong causal interventions on Engram, and scaling to a 176B model.
5Wxva1Z8ls.main_concern: Reviewers question the threat model (backprop access allows modifying backbone weights too), note small prompt counts (50-115) with separate checkpoints per dataset, and see limited methodological novelty beyond standard backdoor training.

V45YPvnuW8.one_liner: Jointly adapts transferable workflow context prompts and LoRA policy weights at test time from autonomous target-app rollouts.
V45YPvnuW8.problem: Mobile GUI agents perform poorly on unseen applications when target demonstrations are unavailable.
V45YPvnuW8.method: CoAdapt-GUI performs test-time adaptation without target demonstrations by jointly evolving a transfer-constrained workflow context (procedures, failure modes, verification rules excluding app-bound state) and updating a frozen VLM's LoRA adapter via task-context-matched group-relative optimization on target rollouts.
V45YPvnuW8.key_idea: Jointly evolves transfer-constrained workflow context prompts and updates LoRA weights via task-context-matched group-relative RL from autonomous target-app rollouts.
V45YPvnuW8.evidence: Evaluated on unseen-app settings in AndroidWorld-Generalization and AndroidWorld Plus against base, context-only, and policy-only TTA baselines.
V45YPvnuW8.claimed_gains: Reaches 45.0% on AndroidWorld-Generalization vs 37.08% for Policy-Only TTA, and improves AndroidWorld Plus from 37.9% to 52.6%.
V45YPvnuW8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and observe consistent improvements from joint adaptation over context-only and policy-only baselines without human demonstrations.
V45YPvnuW8.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing ablations isolating transfer constraints and task-context matching, unclear rollout-budget parity, reliance on task-level rewards at test time, and lack of external agent baselines.

baqdnFaXZT.one_liner: Builds a durable concurrency-safe graph memory layer on RustFS and FalkorDB to benchmark A-Mem's Zettelkasten evolution at scale.
baqdnFaXZT.problem: LLM-curated graph memory systems report large gains on small validation sets, leaving durability, concurrency, and large-scale statistical efficacy untested.
baqdnFaXZT.method: graphmem implements a durable, concurrency-safe single- and multi-agent graph memory layer on RustFS and FalkorDB (with native HNSW vector indexing), instantiating A-Mem's evolution loop with real traversable graph edges that eliminate ID hallucination.
baqdnFaXZT.key_idea: Instantiates A-Mem's Zettelkasten memory evolution over durable RustFS storage and FalkorDB real graph edges to enable auditable, large-scale statistical benchmarking.
baqdnFaXZT.evidence: Benchmarks answer quality, evolution cost, latency, throughput, and fault behavior across LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and BEAM.
baqdnFaXZT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical dual-engine systems architecture, elimination of hallucinated edges, and timely large-scale empirical scrutiny of memory evolution.
baqdnFaXZT.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty (integrating existing tools and A-Mem's unmodified policy), that the no-evolution ablation outperforms full evolution on benchmarks, and that evaluation uses static long-QA rather than live agents with some unmatched comparisons.

5ktxD1YE1Z.one_liner: Filters software engineering agent trajectories without extra LLM passes by scoring policy hidden states against contrastive trajectory banks.
5ktxD1YE1Z.problem: Execution-free LLM verifiers for test-time scaling of software engineering agents consume roughly as many tokens as trajectory generation itself.
5ktxD1YE1Z.method: LatentSift reuses reasoning, observation, and function-call hidden states already computed by the policy during generation, comparing them to positive and negative state banks from training trajectories and fusing distance scores with a learned linear scorer to shortlist candidates for test execution.
5ktxD1YE1Z.key_idea: Reuses policy hidden states across reasoning, observation, and tool-call channels, fusing contrastive bank-distance scores with a linear probe to filter trajectories token-free.
5ktxD1YE1Z.evidence: Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified across three agent frameworks and two policy sizes at K=16.
5ktxD1YE1Z.claimed_gains: Cuts execution-free verifier tokens by 66.6-81.0% and total verification tokens by 49.1-62.1% at K=16 on SWE-bench Verified, while raising DeepSWE-Preview Best@16 from 59.26% to 60.06%.
5ktxD1YE1Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing policy hidden states is a clean, practical way to cut verification token costs in SWE test-time scaling.
5ktxD1YE1Z.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing branch ablations separating contrastive bank distance from the linear scorer, missing wall-clock latency/memory measurements, and untested generalization across policies or benchmarks.

zE1rjslzM3.one_liner: ProDMM modulates Grounding DINO via soft SKU visual prototypes and introduces Bottle-SKU for multi-SKU surface defect detection.
zE1rjslzM3.problem: Industrial surface defect detectors struggle across product SKUs whose geometry, material, and labels alter defect appearance, while existing datasets lack joint defect and SKU annotations.
zE1rjslzM3.method: The authors release Bottle-SKU (13,119 images, 20,419 boxes, 7 defect classes, 48 shampoo-bottle SKUs) and propose ProDMM. ProDMM builds per-SKU visual prototypes, predicts a soft SKU distribution per image, and dynamically generates low-rank Q/V backbone modulations and residual defect-text-to-visual attention conditioning on Grounding DINO.
zE1rjslzM3.key_idea: Predicts soft SKU prototype mixtures to dynamically generate low-rank visual Q/V modulations and cross-modal residual conditioning on Grounding DINO.
zE1rjslzM3.evidence: Evaluated under an SKU-disjoint protocol on Bottle-SKU and cluster-simulated GC10-DET-SKU with component ablations.
zE1rjslzM3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-SKU industrial defect detection is a practically important problem and that Bottle-SKU's joint defect and SKU-disjoint setup is valuable.
zE1rjslzM3.main_concern: Reviewers note modest AP gains with low precision (38.3%), evaluation restricted to a single product family and unseen-only SKUs (omitting mixed seen/unseen SKUs), and synthetic clustering on GC10-DET.

QXchTWdOPg.one_liner: METIS internalizes RFT curriculum selection by training the policy to predict within-prompt reward variance via in-context recent outcomes.
QXchTWdOPg.problem: Existing LLM reinforcement fine-tuning curricula rely on handcrafted heuristics or external auxiliary models that can misalign with the evolving policy's training dynamics.
QXchTWdOPg.method: METIS uses recent training outcomes as in-context examples so the policy itself predicts within-prompt reward variance (for binary or continuous rewards) to allocate training prompts. It jointly optimizes standard RFT task rewards and a self-judgment reward so curriculum prediction co-evolves with the policy.
QXchTWdOPg.key_idea: Trains the LLM policy to predict within-prompt reward variance from recent in-context outcomes and jointly optimizes this self-judgment with RFT rewards.
QXchTWdOPg.evidence: Evaluated across mathematical reasoning, code generation (CodeContests), and agentic function-calling (BFCL v3) benchmarks across three seeds with ablations.
QXchTWdOPg.claimed_gains: Achieves up to a 1.77x training speedup under a matched number of policy updates across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic function-calling benchmarks.
QXchTWdOPg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate integrating curriculum prediction into the task policy without external models and extending reward-variance curricula to continuous rewards.
QXchTWdOPg.main_concern: Reviewers criticize marginal or inconsistent accuracy gains over simpler baselines like PCL, checkpoint selection directly on test benchmarks, and misleading wall-clock speedup metrics.

zeqhHzWzn8.one_liner: SCOPD distills full-context VLM teachers into sparse-context students on-policy, with SCOPD+ targeting visually sensitive reasoning tokens.
zeqhHzWzn8.problem: Aggressive visual-token pruning sharply degrades reasoning VLM Pass@1 even when fixed-context Pass@K shows usable visual evidence remains in the retained tokens.
zeqhHzWzn8.method: SCOPD has a student VLM generate reasoning trajectories from pruned visual tokens while a privileged full-context teacher supervises those on-policy prefixes without ground-truth labels. SCOPD+ uses a small visual-budget intervention to identify tokens sensitive to visual evidence and selectively distills those positions.
zeqhHzWzn8.key_idea: Performs on-policy self-distillation from a full-context VLM teacher onto pruned-context student trajectories, optionally restricted to tokens sensitive to visual-budget interventions.
zeqhHzWzn8.evidence: Fixed-context Pass@K analysis and evaluations across 13 image benchmarks and 5 video benchmarks on Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL with VisionZip, DivPrune, and FastV.
zeqhHzWzn8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the fixed-context Pass@K observation distinguishing information loss from under-utilization interesting and note the broad 18-benchmark evaluation across models and pruners.
zeqhHzWzn8.main_concern: Reviewers question the causal validity of the language-only Pass@K control, note missing comparisons to prior sparse-context distillation methods (e.g., ShortOPD, VA-OPD), and find SCOPD+'s gains over Top-KL inconsistent.
